**What this unit does NOT prove:** no Google sign-in has run. There is no Web
client id yet, the relay is not deployed with D-130, and the emulator image has
no Google Play services. The button is not in the UI.

THE FINDINGS:

- **Dependencies.**
  - `googleid:1.2.0` declares `androidx.credentials:1.6.0-beta01`, so it would
    have silently lifted the app's 1.5.0 pin to a beta. The app moved to the
    1.6.0 stable line instead.
  - Every `credentials-play-services-auth` release pulls an alpha of
    `play-services-identity-credentials` (1.5.0 → alpha02, 1.6.0 → alpha08),
    so Google ID sign-in cannot be built from the documented libraries
    without one. The rule-4 comment says so.
  - The flavour configuration had to be written
    `add("playImplementation", …)`: the first build failed with "Unresolved
    reference 'playImplementation'", because flavours are created after the
    Kotlin DSL generates its accessors.
- **The Play-manifest gate leg found its subject by luck.**
  - Its `ls -t merged_manifests/*/play*/AndroidManifest.xml` could never match,
    because the variant directory is `processPlayDebugManifest`.
  - Its fallback `find … | head -1` is unordered across every play variant: it
    returned playDebug this time, but a playRelease manifest from Aug 28 was
    equally eligible.
  - The mtimes looked alarming (Aug 31 against a Sep 7 APK) but are Gradle's
    up-to-date skip. `aapt2 dump xmltree` of the packaged APK manifest matched
    the file the check read exactly (10 entries each), so nothing false had
    been approved.
  - The check is now pinned to the variant `make android-app` assembles, and
    fails if that file is missing (sabotage row A9).
- **What the Google libraries add to the merged play manifest**, diffed against
  the pre-D-133 baseline:
  - activities, all `exported=false`: credentials-playservices `HiddenActivity`
    and `IdentityCredentialApiHiddenActivity`; gms `SignInHubActivity` and
    `GoogleApiActivity`;
  - services: `CredentialProviderMetadataHolder` (not exported) and
    `RevocationBoundService` (exported, but binding requires
    `com.google.android.gms.auth.api.signin.permission.REVOCATION_NOTIFICATION`);
  - meta-data: `com.google.android.gms.version` and
    `androidx.credentials.CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_KEY`.

  **No provider, receiver, startup initializer or permission arrived.** The
  direct merged manifest gained nothing Google.
- **ADR-0035 constraint 5, proven in the dex rather than the Gradle file.**
  Distinct type names in each APK's `classes*.dex`:
  - play: `googleid` 14, `com/google/android/gms` 1964 (auth 265),
    `androidx/credentials/playservices` 257;
  - direct: **0, 0, 0**.

  My first count reported play `googleid` 0 and gms 7. `strings | grep '^L…'`
  misses every type name whose ULEB128 length byte happens to be printable,
  because the byte is glued to the front of the line. The recount matched
  unanchored `Lpkg/…;` names and deduplicated them. The APK files differ by
  only ~5.8 KB even though play's entries are 838 KB larger compressed; file
  size is not a content measure here, and no cause is claimed.
- **ADR-0035 constraint 1, at runtime.** On `skipti-shots`, which has no Google
  Play services:
  - `am start -W` cold launch took 538 ms, and the process stayed alive;
  - `dumpsys` showed no service running for the app and only MainActivity;
  - `uiautomator` showed the Balance screen rendered;
  - logcat had zero lines matching GooglePlayServices, GoogleApi, gms,
    SignInHub, RevocationBound, GoogleCredential, credential, FATAL or
    AndroidRuntime from the app. With Play services absent, any gms code
    running at launch would have logged that it was missing.
- **Google's "G" mark ships inside `play-services-auth`**
  (`res/drawable-*/googleg_standard_color_18.png`, and the
  `common_google_signin_btn_*` backgrounds). For Android this may settle the
  branding question without a download. It is the founder's call, reported
  and not acted on.
- **My sabotage runner's first pass was wrong.** It ran `make android-test`,
  whose Gradle invocation has no `--continue`, so the first failing test task
  stopped the second variant. It scored 3/9, and every mismatch was one
  variant only. The gate is not weakened (a failure still fails it), but a
  matrix that claims "both variants go red" needs both to run. The runner now
  calls Gradle with `--continue`; run 1 is archived.

THE FINDINGS:

- **A wrong count, mine, caught by looking for declarations.** After `make
  bindings`, my Swift symbol count said 0 for all eight new names while Kotlin
  said 8/8. `grep -c pattern ios/Skipti/Bindings/*.swift` matches ONE file, and
  with one file grep prints a bare count with no `file:` prefix, so the `awk
  -F: '{s+=$2}'` sum was of empty fields. A direct `grep -c` found each name
  once, and the declaration lines were confirmed (`public func
  ffiCreateNamedGroup` at line 6337, `public struct MemberWire` at 2394, and so
  on), along with six `uniffi_skipti_core_fn_func_ffi_*` header symbols.
- **What "bindings freshness" compares, and how that shaped the gate run.** The
  leg (gate.sh:181–203, full gate only) rebuilds the release dylib, runs `make
  bindings`, then `git diff --exit-code -- ios/Skipti/Bindings
  android/app/src/main/kotlin`. Plain `git diff` compares the working tree with
  the index. CLAUDE.md §4 records that a unit regenerating bindings fails this
  leg before commit. Staging the regenerated files first means regeneration
  reproduces exactly the bytes about to be committed, which is what the leg
  exists to prove, so the pre-commit full gate is honestly green rather than
  "expected red".
- **clippy on the new test.** `std::iter::repeat('ह').take(64).collect()` failed
  `manual_str_repeat` and `manual_repeat_n` under `-D warnings`. It is now
  `"ह".repeat(64)`, with no change in what is tested: 64 Devanagari characters
  are 192 bytes, and the cap still counts characters.
- **The rules, and why each is where it is.**
  - A character cap, not a byte cap: tested with Devanagari (sabotage C1).
  - Control characters refused, because names render inside balance lines
    (C2).
  - You may share a name (the founder's "Tim (You)" example) (C3).
  - Other members may not share one, compared case-insensitively (C4).
  - A stored group's names must match its ids in ORDER, not merely in count
    (C5).
  - Renaming is held to the same duplicate rule (C6).
  - Adding a member updates the group's id list as well as the names (C7).
  - "(You)" is display copy, so the shells compose it; core stores only the
    name.

| C3 | you lose the same-name exemption | `a_named_group_puts_you_first_and_mints_everyone_elses_id` and `adding_and_renaming_keep_the_names_and_the_ids_in_step` |
| C4 | duplicate names compared case-sensitively | `a_named_group_puts_you_first…`, `adding_and_renaming_keep…` and `a_stored_group_whose_names_and_ids_disagree_is_refused`, exactly those three |
| C5 | a stored group compared by member COUNT, not order | `a_stored_group_whose_names_and_ids_disagree_is_refused` only |
| C6 | rename skips the duplicate check | `adding_and_renaming_keep_the_names_and_the_ids_in_step` only |
| C7 | `add_member` appends the name but not to `group.members` | `adding_and_renaming_keep_the_names_and_the_ids_in_step` only |

**The toolchain changed mid-unit.** macOS 27, Xcode 27.0 (27A266a), Swift 6.4
and the iOS 27 SDK installed themselves between 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-16. The
first D-135 run (Xcode 26.x, iOS 26.5) gave 131 executed, 8 skipped, 1 failure
(`ExportFlowTests`, finding 4). Every later run is on Xcode 27, and the tree
needed no source change for the new SDK (`@State` became a macro and the
builders were unified; neither broke this code). The reboots wiped the
session scratchpad and the D-135/D-136 drafts in it. Drafts now live in
`.drafts/`, excluded through `.git/info/exclude`.

**What this unit does NOT do:** Android is untouched (D-136). Groups still do
not sync. A person or a group cannot be removed. The export format carries
member ids, not names. Older screens' primary buttons still render as pills
on iOS 26+ (D-137). (Corrected D-137: expected D-139, the iOS 27 adoption unit; see D-135's row.) See §4.

THE FINDINGS:

- **A fresh install got test data.** Balance and Settle called
  `loadGroupsOrSeed()` and `loadOrSeed(seed: Fixtures.dto(…))`, so a new user
  saw "Goa Trip", four fixture people and four fixture expenses. Every user
  path now reads without seeding. The seeding functions remain for the proof
  launch arguments only, and are commented as such.
- **Settle recomputed from the fixtures after a settlement.** After "Mark
  received", `SettleScreen` rebuilt its lines from `Fixtures.dto(…)`, not from
  the expenses it had loaded. It now recomputes from the loaded ledger.
- **iOS Balance ignored settlements.** `computeLines` passed `settlements: []`,
  while Android's Balance has shared `recomputePlan` since D-111. On the
  simulator: ₹600 owed → "Mark received" from Rahul → Balance ₹300 (before
  the fix it would have stayed ₹600).
- **A test that passed by accident.** `testLedgerStoreSnapshotRoundTripsThroughCore`
  asserted `groups.count == 1`, and it held only because `snapshot()` seeded
  the fixture group: the "Trip" group the test built with `ffiCreateGroup` was
  never stored. Once export stopped seeding, the test failed on the old
  toolchain (131/8/1). It now stores a real group through the group store and
  asserts that exact id, and `testExportingAnEmptyLedgerSeedsNothing` proves an
  empty export writes no group.
- **My own draft had a data-loss bug.** `createGroup` read the existing groups
  with `(try? namedGroups()) ?? []`, so an unreadable list would have become
  empty, and the save would then have written ONLY the new group. That is
  D-127's `try?` trap. It was caught in review before touching the tree, and
  `testACorruptGroupListIsAnErrorAndCreatingAGroupNeverOverwritesIt` pins it
  (sabotages S1 and S4).
- **Placeholder names could make core refuse a whole group.** A group written
  without names, holding two unknown people, would have named both "Member",
  and core refuses duplicate names. Names now resolve one member at a time
  (stored name, then yours, then the legacy fixture name, then "Member N" by
  position). `needsYourName` fires only while you are in a group with no stored
  name for you (S6).
- **Expense dates showed the minute.** The row read "Sep 16, 2026 at 24":
  `setLocalizedDateFormatFromTemplate("dMMMmy")` has carried a stray `m`
  (minute) since D-54 (`3255805`). Now "dMMMy", as on Android (`d MMM y`), with
  `testExpenseDatesShowDayMonthAndYearOnly` (S8).
- **iOS 26+ clips a clear-background list row to a pill.** A 10 pt
  `PrimaryButtonStyle` button in such a row renders as a pill (on 26.5 and 27),
  and a `SecondaryButtonStyle` outline in a single-row section vanished except
  for two arcs ("New group"). The iOS 27 swiftinterface has no API for the row
  clip. "New group" moved to `.safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom)`; "Add another
  person" and "Add person" now sit inside their cards with insets and no
  separator (a stray separator line under "Add another person" is gone too).
  Older screens are D-137's. (Corrected D-137: expected D-139, the iOS 27 adoption unit; see D-135's row.)
- **Xcode 27 spends 600 s collecting a simulator sysdiagnose after ANY
  failing test.** The first S1 row looked hung in `simctl diagnose`, but its
  tests had finished in 4 s. `make ios-app` and the sabotage runner now pass
  `-collect-test-diagnostics never`, so a red gate reports at once.
- **`ensure-ios-sim.sh` took the first "iPhone 17" it found**, which after the
  update is the iOS 26.5 device. It now takes the newest runtime's device, and
  `SIM_OS` pins one.
- Smaller: two `[settle-debug]` prints logged group ids on every load
  (removed); a Balance with a group but no lines showed "…" forever (now the
  empty-ledger copy); Add started in USD for an INR group (now the group's
  currency); PeopleScreen cleared a refused name (now kept for correcting);
  `GroupCopy` names "The group needs a name." and control characters
  separately; Balance and Add use `LedgerStore.defaultStore()`.

On the simulator (`ios/artifacts/d135-*.png`):

- **iOS 27.0, fresh install** (`AFAF4221-…`): onboarding (kit, three words),

  (`d135-ios27-new-group.png`); People, and "priya" refused with the copy
  while the text stays (`d135-ios27-people*.png`). The data survived a reboot.
- **iOS 26.5, the founder's ledger** (`EB725812-…`): the vault was copied to

  (`d135-ios26-migrated-balance.png`), and his fixture-Ada rows now read "PAID

THE FINDINGS:

- **A fresh install got test data on its first saved expense.**
  `AddExpenseUi.buildExpense` called `LedgerStore(vaultPath, openVault).loadGroupsOrSeed()`,
  which writes the fixture "Goa Trip" when no group exists, and the expense was
  paid by `BalanceFixtures.ada`. Android's home was already read-only (D-111),
  so the seeding surfaced one step later than on iOS. `buildExpense` now takes
  `payer` and `groupId` from the screen and reads no vault. The equal-split
  test now proves that building an expense writes no group.
- **A failed settlement was silently dropped.** `recordSettlement` wrapped the
  save in `catch (_: Exception) { // surfaced by the load-error path on the
  next recompute }`, but `onDone` (the recompute) never ran on failure. The
  error went nowhere, and the button stayed "Settling…" until the screen was
  rebuilt. Failures now set an owed-colour message ("Could not record the
  settlement. …", or "Recorded, but the ledger could not be reloaded. …") and
  reset the button. Both the save and the recompute are caught inside the
  coroutine, because on Android an escape crashes the process (the
  FireAndForgetGuard lesson). The settlement itself now comes from
  `SettleUi.settlementFor(entry, currency, group, viewer)`, a pure function
  tested against your own id (A9).
- **An import erased every stored name.** `writeSnapshot` rebuilt `GroupDTO`
  from `PortGroup`, which carries member ids only, so an import would have
  dropped every `memberNames`. Names are now kept by member id, in the merged
  member order; a newcomer gets a placeholder
  (`importing_a_snapshot_keeps_the_names_of_existing_people`, A8).
- **`loadGroups()` hid corruption** by returning `emptyList()` on unreadable
  JSON (D-127's lesson). It now throws `LedgerCorruptException`, and
  `createGroup` cannot write over an unreadable list (A1, A4).
- **Export seeded**, `snapshot()` → `loadGroupsOrSeed()`, the twin of iOS
  (A7).
- **The call-site rewrite was scripted.** 17 `buildExpense` calls across 7
  test files lost `vaultPath`/`openVault` and gained `payer`/`groupId`. The
  script found each call by paren depth and asserted per-file counts. Tests
  whose later lookups need a stored group (SyncTest "Offline write",
  IdentityTest "Signed-out write", SettleTest) seed one explicitly. 5
  `recomputePlan` calls gained the viewer. The JVM suite passed on its first
  run.
- **A sabotage expectation of mine was wrong again** (the same class as D-135's
  S2). A6 turns every placeholder into "Member", which also fails the import
  test because it asserts "Member 3". That red is correct; the expected set
  was corrected and A6 rerun.

The gate ran on the working tree over `2ca8f08`. The commit adds this
BUILD-LOG record, `docs/WORKLOG.md`, and one CLAUDE.md line that replaces
"20–40 minutes" with this gate's measured time, to the tree the gate saw. No
leg reads any of them and none is a heavy input, so the pre-commit hook should skip the heavy legs on the
proof this gate wrote. What the hook actually printed is recorded in
`docs/WORKLOG.md` after the commit (it cannot be recorded here, before it).

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** The founder asked on 2026-09-18 why checks took over 30 minutes.
Measured before this unit (raw data in the local `.drafts/gate-timing/`):
clippy 16m37s to recheck one crate, and the `cargo test` RUN 12m44s for
about 10 s of real tests across 24 binaries. `sample` put rustc in `dlopen` →
dyld `mapSegments` → `fcntl` while `syspolicyd` ran at 45–64%: every build
product carries `com.apple.provenance`, and macOS assesses each proc-macro
dylib the compiler loads and each new test binary. That is not something a
script can fix. The founder enabled the Developer Tools exemption for Claude,
Terminal and Xcode (CLAUDE.md §13). What a script CAN fix is doing the same
proven work twice: every unit commit ran the heavy legs again on Rust inputs a
full gate had just passed, because only BUILD-LOG and screenshots changed in
between.

**What was built.**
- `scripts/gate_inputs.py`: a fingerprint of the heavy inputs, every file
  git sees (tracked, and untracked but not ignored) EXCEPT a denylist of
  paths cargo never reads (`docs/`, `ios/`, `android/`, `web/`, `brand/`,
  `deploy/`, `native/`, `.github/`, root `*.md`, `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, and
  `scripts/` other than `gate.sh` and `gate_inputs.py`). A denylist on
  purpose: a new crate, fixture or config file counts until someone decides
  otherwise, so forgetting costs a slow commit, never a skipped check. The
  toolchain is part of it (`rustc -vV`, `cargo -V`, `cargo clippy -V`, the
  installed targets, the RUSTFLAGS family).
- `scripts/gate.sh`: a fast or full run fingerprints the working tree at
  start and again at end, and writes `.git/skipti-heavy-legs-pass.json` only
  when nothing failed, nothing was skipped and the two agree. Any other
  outcome deletes it; so does a failure of the recorder itself. New
  `--cheap` mode (the six legs that take seconds). `(Ns)` on every leg line
  and a Timing table after the evidence block, where it cannot change the
  shape of recorded evidence. The stale "(~10s warm)" header is gone.
- `.githooks/pre-commit`: the cheap legs run on EVERY commit. The heavy legs
  run when a staged change touches a heavy input (deletions included), unless
  the index's fingerprint equals the proof; the index, because it is what the
  commit records. Anything the helper cannot establish runs the fast gate.
  It prints which case applied.
- `scripts/test_gate_inputs.py`, a new gate leg in every mode (21 tests,
  about 4 s): throwaway repositories for each way the proof could wrongly say
  "proven", and the REAL hook driven by `git commit` against a stub gate.

**Findings.**
- **The Developer Tools exemption was not reaching the gate.** After the
  founder enabled it, R1 below still took 20m37s: clippy sat at 0% CPU for
  minutes, `syspolicyd` logged 191 `GK evaluateScanResult` lines in 10
  minutes, and its connections to an Apple host ran 45–86 s before being
  cancelled. D-136's 20m46s full gate, recorded as the exemption's effect,
  may have owed more to warm caches. Reported to the founder; turning the
  setting on, off or re-granting it is his (CLAUDE.md §13).
- **What the scan costs is first loads.** In this unit's full gate clippy took
  0 s and `cargo test` 37 s, against 456 s and 777 s in R1 an hour earlier on
  the same Rust: the build products had been assessed once already. The whole
  18-leg gate took 8m54s. A unit that changes Rust pays the scan again.
- **The self-test must scrub git's environment.** It runs inside the
  pre-commit hook, where git exports `GIT_INDEX_FILE`: a test `git add`
  inheriting it would write the real repository's index. The test removes
  every `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` variable and ignores global and
  system config. Checked by running it with `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_DIR` and
  `GIT_WORK_TREE` pointed at the real repository: 21/21 green, the real index
  byte-identical afterwards.
- **Gaps the old hook had**, closed: a commit touching only a check script,
  only BUILD-LOG or only Swift ran no check at all (the check-script case was
  an open WORKLOG gap); a staged DELETION of a `.rs` file was not
  "gate-relevant" (`--diff-filter=ACMR`); and a change to an `include_str!`
  input such as `core/src/lykill_bip39_english.txt` skipped the gate.
- **The deploy runbook had three mistakes of mine**, found in the 2026-09-18
  relay upgrade and fixed in `docs/DEPLOY-ORACLE.md`: the backup `cp` glob is
  expanded by the unprivileged shell, which cannot read the `700` directory
  (now `sudo sh -c '…'`, with the reason); step 7 ran `git rev-parse HEAD` on
  the instance, which has no checkout (the commit now travels as
  `skipti-commit.txt` next to the tarball); and a unit file written before the
  Google lines existed has nothing to "uncomment" (now: ADD them). New §7.1,
  "Updating a running relay": build first, then stop, back up, install,
  start, verify; why `cp` is safe only on a stopped database; why a schema
  migration makes the backup the only rollback. The runbook now carries the
  real Google client IDs (public identifiers).
- **D-135 pointed at "D-137" for the iOS 27 work**, five times. D-numbers
  follow recording order, and 137 became this unit; each place is corrected in
  place to "expected D-139".

**Real runs of the new machinery** (`.drafts/d137/`, local):
- **R1, a real fast gate on this tree: 9/9 PASSED in 20m37s** (clippy 456 s,
  cargo test 777 s for 327 tests, self-test 4 s), "heavy-leg marker: written
  (fast gate, 68 heavy inputs)". With the D-137 scripts staged,
  `gate_inputs.py check-index` answered "the fast gate at
  2026-09-19T01:30:01Z (HEAD 2ca8f08) passed on exactly these 68 staged heavy
  inputs and this toolchain".
- **R2, fail path**, with a repo-local cargo stub (`.drafts/d137/shim/cargo`:
  version queries go to the real cargo, heavy legs are stubbed, and the runs
  set `RUSTFLAGS` so nothing they write could match a real toolchain): rustfmt
  fails → "GATE FAILED — 8 passed, 1 failed" → "heavy-leg marker: cleared",
  and R1's marker was gone.
- **R3, edit during the run**: the stub appends a line to `core/src/lib.rs`
  during clippy → the gate passes → "heavy-leg marker: not written (the heavy
  inputs changed while the gate ran)". `lib.rs` restored, `cmp` identical.

**Sabotage 10/10**, each on the first run: one deterministic edit through an
anchor asserted to match once, the expected red set fixed beforehand, every
red a FAILURE (an ERROR would be the wrong red), the file restored and
checked with `cmp`.

| Row | Sabotage | Red |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | the toolchain is left out of the proof | `ProofTests.test_toolchain_change_voids_the_proof` only |
| S2 | an edit made during the run is ignored | `ProofTests.test_edit_during_the_run_writes_nothing` only |
| S3 | a failed run keeps the old proof | `ProofTests.test_failed_run_clears_the_marker` only |
| S4 | a skipped run keeps the old proof | `ProofTests.test_skipped_run_clears_the_marker` only |
| S5 | the proof is checked against the working tree, not the index | `ProofTests.test_index_is_what_counts_not_the_working_tree`, `ProofTests.test_unstaged_change_keeps_the_proof`, `ProofTests.test_untracked_heavy_file_counts_until_it_is_staged` only |
| S6 | scripts/gate.sh stops counting as a heavy input | `ClassificationTests.test_heavy_classification`, `ProofTests.test_non_rust_heavy_inputs_void_the_proof` only |
| S7 | the server crate is excluded from the proof | `ClassificationTests.test_heavy_classification`, `ClassificationTests.test_workspace_members_and_path_dependencies_are_heavy` only |
| S8 | a staged deletion is not seen as a heavy change | `HookTests.test_staged_deletion_of_a_heavy_file_runs_the_fast_gate` only |
| S9 | the hook skips the heavy legs whether or not the proof matches | `HookTests.test_heavy_commit_with_a_stale_proof_runs_the_fast_gate`, `HookTests.test_heavy_commit_without_a_proof_runs_the_fast_gate`, `HookTests.test_staged_deletion_of_a_heavy_file_runs_the_fast_gate` only |
| S10 | a commit with no heavy input skips the gate entirely (the pre-D-137 hook) | `HookTests.test_a_red_gate_refuses_the_commit`, `HookTests.test_check_script_only_commit_runs_the_cheap_legs`, `HookTests.test_docs_only_commit_runs_the_cheap_legs` only |

**What this unit does NOT do:** it does not make the heavy legs themselves
faster; that is the scan, and the founder's setting. It proves nothing about
the Swift or Kotlin legs: the proof covers only what the fast gate checks. The
proof lives in `.git`, so a fresh clone, CI and a second worktree all start
without one. See §4.

**What was built.** D-132 (iOS) and D-133 (Android `play`) built Google
sign-in and hid it until two things existed: the OAuth clients, and Google's
button art. The founder created the clients on 2026-09-18 (Web, iOS, and
Android clients for the upload and debug keys), set both IDs on the relay, and
approved downloading Google's official asset bundle.
- **iOS:** `GoogleSignInConfig.iosClientID` is the iOS client; the
  `GoogleSignInButton` image set is Google's "Sign in with Google" square art
  at @1x/@2x/@3x, light and dark, unmodified, with the words drawn into the
  image (no font, nothing fetched: GUARANTEES #6). `SignInScreen` stacks
  Apple's button and Google's at ONE size, 188 × 44 pt (Google's art at its
  native size, sharp at every scale), because App Store guideline 4.8 wants
  Apple's option at least as prominent and Google's branding rules want
  Google's at least as prominent as any other. Apple's corner radius went from
  10 to 4 to match Google's square art. New copy: "Apple or Google only confirm
  it is you. They never see your ledger." (SPEC §4.2 item 1).
- **Android:** `GoogleSignInConfig.WEB_CLIENT_ID` is the Web client (the
  relay's audience; Credential Manager's `serverClientId`). The art ships ONLY
  in `src/play/res` (`drawable` and `drawable-night` at four densities);
  `BRAND_MARK_BUNDLED` moved into each flavour's `GoogleCredential`, and
  `GoogleSignInButton` exists in both source sets, drawing Google's art in
  `play` and nothing in `direct`, so shared code compiles in both without
  naming a play-only resource. The button sits above ACCOUNT at the art's
  native 180 × 40 dp, padded to a 48 dp touch target, with "Google only
  confirms it is you. It never sees your ledger."
- **NOTICE** now records Google's button art: Google's trademark, used under
  its sign-in branding guidelines, not covered by this project's licence.

**Seen, against the live relay (production `9952f95`):**
- **iOS 27 simulator:** light and dark (`ios/artifacts/d138-ios27-signin-*.png`).
  Tapping Google fetched a nonce from the relay and opened Google's page in
  the system sheet. Google answered **"Sign in to continue to SKIPTI"**, with no
  `redirect_uri_mismatch` or `invalid_client`, so the iOS client ID, the
  derived redirect, PKCE and the `openid`-only request are accepted by Google
  (`d138-ios27-google-consent-page.png`). Closing the sheet left no error.
- **Apple on the simulator:** the relay's nonce arrived, then iOS answered
  "Sign in to your Apple Account" because the simulator has none; closing it
  shows "Sign in with Apple did not finish." (`d138-ios27-apple-no-account-dark.png`).
- **Android `direct`** (skipti-shots, API 34): no Google button
  (`android/artifacts/d138-direct-signin-no-google.png`). **Dex:** the direct
  APK carries 0 `googleid` types, 0 `credentials.playservices` types and no
  reference to the art; play carries 6, 3 and 2.
- **Android `play`** on Pixel_10_Pro_XL (API 37, Google Play services, no
  Google account on the device): the button renders light and dark; a tap
  fetched the relay's nonce, Credential Manager routed the
  `TYPE_GOOGLE_ID_TOKEN_CREDENTIAL` request to Play services' `GoogleIdService`,
  and Google's own add-an-account flow opened. Back returned to SKIPTI with no
  error text (`d138-play-pixel-*.png`).

**Not seen:** a completed sign-in. Every remaining step needs a real Google
or Apple account typed in by its owner. That is the founder's to do, never
Claude's. See §4.

**Findings.**
- **A `*/` inside a KDoc comment ended it early**: my comment named the path
  `drawable*/google_sign_in.png`, and Kotlin read `*/` as the comment's end
  (compile error, caught by the build). Reworded.
- **The direct build has no `R.drawable` class at all** (its only resources are
  mipmaps), so its "no art" test looks the field up by name and accepts either
  the missing class or the missing field.
- **Android 15+ draws SKIPTI under the status bar.** On the API 37 image, the
  "Sign in" title overlaps the clock: `targetSdk = 37` enforces edge-to-edge,
  and the app handles no window insets anywhere. The usual API 34 test AVD
  hides it. Not this unit's change; spawned as its own task and listed in §4.
- **An emulator that has been up for hours can lose DNS** (skipti-shots:
  "Unable to resolve host"). The error line then printed the raw exception,
  the existing `RelayError.Network` copy shared with the code path
  (`android/artifacts/d138-play-stale-emulator-dns-error.png`).
- **Why this gate's Rust legs were slow again, with no Rust changed** (clippy
  246 s, `cargo test` 783 s, against 0 s and 37 s in D-137's full gate):
  `server/build.rs` watches `.git/logs/HEAD` so `/version` names the right
  commit, and two commits landed in between (D-137 and its WORKLOG note). So
  the server crate was rebuilt, every server test binary relinked, and macOS
  assessed each new binary on its first launch (D-137's finding). While the
  scan reaches the gate, the first gate after any commit pays this cost.

**Sabotage 7/7, each on the first run**, expected red sets fixed before the run. iOS
rows rebuild and run the whole hosted suite; Android rows run both JVM
variants, and a guard that lives in one flavour must fail in that flavour
only.

| Row | Sabotage | Red |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | iOS uses the Web client id | `ProviderSignInTests.testThisBuildUsesTheIssuedIOSClient` only |
| I2 | iOS says Google's art is not bundled | `ProviderSignInTests.testGoogleIsOfferedOnlyWithAClientIdAndGooglesMark` only |
| I3 | the dark appearance falls back to the light art | `ProviderSignInTests.testGoogleButtonArtIsBundledForLightAndDark` only |
| A1 | Android uses the iOS client id | `GoogleSignInTest.this_build_uses_the_issued_web_client` only |
| A2 | the play build says Google's art is not bundled | play: `GoogleFlavourTest.this_build_offers_google_with_googles_art` only; direct: all green |
| A3 | the direct build claims Google's art | play: all green; direct: `GoogleFlavourTest.this_build_offers_no_google_and_carries_no_art` only |
| A4 | Google's art is copied into the direct build | play: all green; direct: `GoogleFlavourTest.this_build_offers_no_google_and_carries_no_art` only |

**What this unit does NOT do:** see §4.

**Why.** The founder, 2026-09-16: Xcode 27 arrived with iOS 27, "you can use
the new design elements". D-135 found that iOS 26 and later clip a
clear-background List/Form row to a pill: every primary button placed as
such a row rendered as a capsule, and a secondary button's outline in a
single-row section disappeared. Nothing in the iOS 27 SDK changes the row's
clip. D-135 fixed its own screens; four older ones and one it did not list
still showed it.

**What was built.**
- `formActionBar { … }` in `DesignTokens.swift`: a screen's main action
  sits UNDER the form. On iOS 26+ it is a `safeAreaBar`, the system's own
  bar with its scroll-edge treatment (system chrome, ADR-0023); before 26 a
  plain `safeAreaInset` on the page colour. The button has an opaque
  page-colour backing, because a disabled primary button is drawn at 45%
  opacity and the rows scrolling beneath showed through it (seen on iOS 27:
  "Priya" inside a dimmed "Add expense"). Used for **Add expense**, **Save
  name**, **Create group**, **Send code / Verify** and **Import N expenses**
  (Import Review's list had the same single-row trap; its "Applying writes
  all selected expenses at once." moved into the status row).
- The Balance account glyph is `.topBarPinnedTrailing` on iOS 27, so it can
  never be moved into the overflow menu; earlier systems keep
  `.topBarTrailing`, behind one `#available` around the toolbar body, the
  shape Apple's iOS 27 toolbar reference prescribes.
- `RecordSyncTests`: Swift 6.4's 13 `#NoUseUnstructuredThrowingTask`
  warnings. Each Task awaited `restoreFromRelay` and then fulfilled an
  expectation, so a throw surfaced as a 10-second expectation TIMEOUT that
  named nothing. Each now catches and calls `XCTFail("restoreFromRelay
  threw: …")` before fulfilling. One needless `try` (Swift's
  `#UnnecessaryEffectMarker`) is gone too.
- New gate leg `scripts/check-swift-list-rows.py`: a styled button made
  into a clear, zero-inset list row fails the gate. It walks the button's
  modifier chain in both directions, through multi-line arguments by
  bracket depth.

**Seen** (`ios/artifacts/d139-*.png`): iOS 27 Add expense (the enabled button
rides above the number pad, so an amount can be saved without scrolling),
Sign in light and dark, New group, and the itemised split's "Add line";
iOS 26.5, on the founder's ledger simulator (vault backed up first, nothing
added), Add expense with its bar and his ledger intact on Balance.

**Findings.**

**Why.** The founder, 2026-09-19: "you haven't given any option to modify the
expenses once it's inside the expenses tab which is an essential thing". He
chose tap → a detail page with Edit and Delete, plus a long-press menu, and

semantics, so nothing here was redesigned: §5.7 (edits are new versions, the
prior retained until compaction; deletes are tombstones; "added by" and
"last edited by" shown), §6.1 (field-level last-writer-wins on the HLC; an
AMOUNT conflict is put to the person, never resolved silently), §16.4 (three
devices, offline edits in any order, converge). This unit is the core and
the plumbing; the screens are D-142 (iOS) and D-143 (Android).

**What was built.**
- `straumr::revision` (new): a revision payload (`target`, `seen`,
  `editor`, and any of `money`, `note`, `category`, `deleted`), encoded and
  decoded ONLY by core so both platforms write identical bytes, with unknown
  fields refused rather than half-applied. `project()` folds creations and
  revisions into the ledger: each field takes the value of the revision with
  the greatest HLC that set it; money (payer, amount, currency, conversion,
  shares) is ONE register, because shares must sum to the amount; `deleted`
  is a register too, so Undo is `deleted: false`; a revision whose expense
  has not arrived waits in `pending`; an unreadable one is listed in
  `rejected`, never applied. **Conflict rule:** a revision lists in `seen`
  every earlier revision its device had applied, so R1 happened before R2
  exactly when R1 ∈ R2.seen; two or more money revisions that no other money
  revision saw, with different values, are a conflict. Balances use the last
  writer meanwhile, so every device still agrees. A "keep this one" edit that
  saw them all resolves it.
- Record type `0x05 ExpenseRevision`, its own type rather than a flag on
  `0x01`: a build that read a revision as a creation would count the expense
  twice. (Nothing has shipped; every device updates together. §4.)
- FFI: `ffi_encode_expense_revision`, `ffi_decode_expense_revision`,
  `ffi_project_expenses`; bindings regenerated.
- Both shells: `rebuildProjection` now goes through core; deleted expenses
  leave the kv ledger (balances, list and export skip them). The kv rows keep
  exactly their old shape, so balances and every earlier test are untouched.
  New `projectedExpenses()` (ids, "added by", "last edited by", `seen`, any
  conflict, deleted ones flagged) and `reviseExpense(_:)` (a type-5 record in
  the expense's own group scope, authored and pushed like any local record).
  `ExpenseDTO.addedBy` is new, set by both Add screens.

**Findings.**
- **The legacy backfill would have duplicated every edited expense.** D-121's
  backfill mints a record for any kv row it cannot find among the record
  blobs, on every pull. After an edit, the projection writes the EDITED values
  into the kv row, which no longer equals its creation record, so the next
  pull would have minted the edited row as a brand-new expense. It now runs
  once per vault (`sync/legacy-backfilled`), and `reviseExpense` runs it
  before writing, so the flag is always set before an edit exists. Proven on
  both platforms (`…BackfillNeverReMintsAnEditedExpense`, sabotage I1/A1).
- **No new dependency**: core already had serde and serde_json.
- **The iOS app links a prebuilt Rust library**: new FFI symbols need `make
  ios-core` before the app links (it failed with "Undefined symbols" first).

**Why.** The founder, 2026-09-19: editing expenses from the Expenses tab is
"an essential thing". His choices: tap a row for a detail page with Edit and

and can be undone. D-141 built the records; this unit is the iOS screens.

**What was built.**
- **Detail page** (`ExpenseDetailView`): the amount, who paid and when, the
  whole split, and SPEC §5.7's "Added by … · date, time" and "Last edited by
  … · date, time" (an expense from before D-141 names no author, so it shows
  no "added" line rather than the one-time backfill's time). Edit and
  Delete sit in the action bar under the page (D-139's `formActionBar`).
- **Edit** opens the Add form as a sheet, filled in, in the expense's OWN
  group (not the group selected on Balance). The split type is not stored,
  so it is re-derived: Payer only or Equal when core's split over the same
  people reproduces the stored shares exactly, Exact otherwise (to the minor
  unit). Save writes ONE revision holding only what changed; an untouched
  form writes nothing, and a cleared note is written as "" so the old one
  cannot survive. A new amount or currency drops a frozen conversion.
- **Delete** is confirmed ("Delete this expense?" / "It leaves your balances.
  You can undo it right after."), writes the tombstone, and the list offers
  "Deleted “Dinner”." with Undo until the person leaves the tab. Undo is
  written from the projection that holds the delete.
- **Long press** on a row: Edit and Delete in a context menu, and the same
  two as VoiceOver actions.
- **SPEC §6.1's question**, verbatim for two devices: "Two devices set
  different amounts. Keep ₹1,200.00 or ₹1,250.00?", one card per version
  (amount, payer, split) with a "Keep ₹…" button; versions that share an
  amount say "…changed who paid or how it is split. Keep which?" instead of
  "₹1,200.00 or ₹1,200.00". Keeping one writes a money revision whose `seen`
  covers every competing edit, so the conflict ends everywhere. The list
  flags such a row "CHOOSE A VERSION".
- Core: `ffi_money_input_digits`, the inverse of `ffi_money_parse_minor`, so
  the form starts from the stored amount without Swift doing money
  arithmetic (ADR-0002). The list's header reads "1 EXPENSE" / "3 EXPENSES".
- Proof surface `--expense-conflict`: one device cannot produce a conflict
  (each of its edits sees the last), so it seeds a THROWAWAY vault in the
  temporary directory with two edits that did not see each other and shows
  the real detail page over it. The person's ledger is never opened.

**Findings.**
- **The list was keyed by the PAYER.** `ForEach(sorted, id: \.payer)` gave
  every expense paid by the same person one identity, which SwiftUI requires
  to be unique; a tap has to open THE expense, so the list now reads core's
  projection and keys each row by the expense's own id.
- **iOS 26 and later draw `confirmationDialog` as a popover from the view
  that carries it.** Attached to the whole page (and the whole list), "Delete
  this expense?" floated at the top of the screen pointing at nothing (seen
  on iOS 27, `.drafts/d142/shots/05-confirm-v1.png`). It now hangs from the
  Delete button, and from the row a long press deletes.
- **The split type is not stored**, only the shares it produced, so the edit
  form re-derives it from core's own split (§4 records what that means for
  Percentage, Shares, Adjustment and Itemised).
- **One device cannot produce an amount conflict**: each of its edits sees
  the one before. Hence the `--expense-conflict` proof over a throwaway vault
  and the hosted test that writes two edits with empty `seen`.
- **Seen on iOS 27** (`ios/artifacts/d142-*.png`): the list ("1 EXPENSE");
  the detail page; Edit opening as Equal at 900.00; the saved edit (₹1,200,
  "Dinner", "Last edited by Tim (You) · Sep 21, 2026 at 3:45 PM"); Delete's
  confirmation, the empty list with "Deleted “Dinner”." and Undo, which
  brought it back edited; the long-press menu; the conflict question, and
  Keep ending it with "Added by" and "Last edited by" shown; dark mode.

| I1 | keeping one amount forgets what it saw | `ExpenseEditingTests.testKeepingOneAmountEndsTheConflictInTheLedger` only |

The gate ran on the working tree over `41f8107`. The commit adds only this
BUILD-LOG record, `docs/WORKLOG.md` and the screenshots to the tree the gate
saw.

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** The founder, 2026-09-21: the account section should have "the
toggle to switch modes (light, dark, night)" and "things an actual app
usually has, so research and add those". Asked what Night means, he chose
pure black (ADR-0036). Comparable apps (Splitwise's Account tab: profile,
default currency, notifications; the platforms' own guidance: privacy
policy, open-source licences, data access and deletion) set the rest of the
list; this unit is the page and Appearance, and the one guarantee it found
broken.

**What was built.**
- **Settings** replaces the account page on both shells (the glyph now
  reads "Settings" to VoiceOver and TalkBack): Appearance, Account (the
  existing cards, GUARANTEES #5's shape kept), Your data.
- **Appearance**: System (default), Light, Dark, Night, with one line saying
  what each does. Stored in device preferences, not the vault (not financial
  data; onboarding and the vault-recovery screen draw before the vault
  opens). iOS applies it as window trait overrides (style + `NightTrait`),
  so system chrome, sheets and alerts follow, and bridges `NightTrait` into
  SwiftUI's environment. Android overrides the night bit of
  `LocalConfiguration`, so every existing `isSystemInDarkTheme()` follows,
  and reads Night as snapshot state inside `Tok`.
- **Night tokens** (ADR-0036): bg #000000, surface #080b0e, raised
  #0f1418, text #d5dce2, dim #8797a4, faint #74838f; money and accent
  unchanged. Both shells recompute every pair's WCAG contrast in a test:
  text 7:1, dim/faint/money 4.5:1 on all three surfaces, accent 3:1, a
  primary button's label 4.5:1.
- **Your data**: Export (both shells) and the Recovery Kit (iOS) open from
  Settings. Android's Export gained a Back button and a `HomeRoutes` parent
  (Back returns to Settings).

**Findings.**
- **GUARANTEES #4 was false in the product.** Export (D-119) and the kit
  re-view screen (D-80) were built and proven, but only proof launch
  arguments (`--export`, `--kit-reveal`) opened them; nothing in the D-126
  and D-128 shells linked them. D-119's row recorded the missing entry point
  as residue while its headline said the guarantee was now true; the
  headline is corrected in place.
- **iOS: Night → Dark kept Night's colours.** Choosing Dark after Night
  changes only the custom trait (the style stays dark); SwiftUI saw no
  change and did not re-resolve its colours. Screenshot pixels read
  #000000 (Night's page) after choosing Dark. With the trait bridged into
  the environment and set at the root, the same switch reads #0b0f13 page
  and #0e141a card, and Night reads #000000 and #080b0e.
- **Android: button labels failed contrast in dark mode.** Material's
  `onPrimary` was the TEXT colour: #182430 on the light accent (2.44:1) and
  #e9eef3 on the dark one (1.91:1), under every default-coloured label
  ("Sign in" among them). Fourteen other labels drew `Color.White` on the
  accent (2.05:1 dark). All are the page colour now, iOS's rule (5.99:1
  light, 8.60:1 dark, 9.40:1 night); `skiptiColorScheme` is pinned at 4.5:1
  in every mode.
- **Minute for month, twice more.** The Recovery Kit ("Created …") and the
  import review still used the "dMMMmy" template that D-127 and D-135 fixed
  in other files. Every iOS date now goes through one `AppDate`.
- **An empty ledger's Export said "The ledger could not be read."** on both
  shells (empty shared the failure flag); it now says "Nothing to export
  yet: no expenses or settlements."
- **Seen** (`ios/artifacts/d144-*.png`, `android/artifacts/d144-*.png`):
  Settings in light, dark and night on both; the Expenses list in Night;
  Export from Settings on both, Back returning to Settings on Android; the
  Recovery Kit screen from Settings on iOS; both devices left on System.

**Sabotage 9/9**, expected red sets fixed before the run (the reasoning for
each set is in the local runner). **Run 1's I4 went MISMATCH, and the
prediction was the error**: its expected set named only the new date test,
but the Expenses list's `dateString` now delegates to `AppDate`, so D-135's
own date test (`CategoryWiringTests`) went red as well, which is the point
of one helper. The set was corrected and I4 rerun alone: OK (run 1 kept as
`results_d144_run1.json`).

| Row | Sabotage | Red |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | the token provider ignores Night | `AppearanceTests.testEveryNightPairClearsItsContrastFloor`, `AppearanceTests.testTheTokensResolveNightOnlyUnderTheNightTrait` only |
| I2 | Night's faint text dropped to #4a5560 | `AppearanceTests.testEveryNightPairClearsItsContrastFloor` only |
| I3 | an unknown stored mode falls back to Dark | `AppearanceTests.testAStoredModeThisBuildDoesNotKnowIsSystem` only |
| I4 | the day template back to dMMMmy | `AppearanceTests.testDatesNeverShowTheMinuteAsTheMonth`, `CategoryWiringTests.testExpenseDatesShowDayMonthAndYearOnly` only |
| A1 | Tok ignores Night | `AppearanceTest.the_tokens_resolve_night_only_under_the_night_mode` only |
| A2 | Night's faint text dropped to 0xFF4A5560 | `AppearanceTest.every_night_pair_clears_its_contrast_floor` only |
| A3 | an unknown stored mode falls back to DARK | `AppearanceTest.a_stored_mode_this_build_does_not_know_is_system` only |
| A4 | the light scheme's onPrimary back to the text colour | `AppearanceTest.a_primary_button_label_is_readable_in_every_mode` only |
| A5 | Back from Export goes to the tabs | `AppearanceTest.back_from_export_returns_to_settings` only |

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** The founder, 2026-09-21: the account section should let you "set
up local account (on device) name and stuff, maybe an option to add photo
like an emoji". Asked, he chose emoji OR photo. It is a profile, not an
account: GUARANTEES #5 forbids implying one, so the page says "Your name
and picture stay on this device. They are not an account and are not sent
anywhere."

**What was built (both shells).**
- **Name**: the name D-135 already stores (`SelfDTO.name`); saving goes
  through `setYourName`, which core validates and which renames you in
  every group, so the page can promise "Shown as “Tim (You)” in your
  groups."
- **Picture**: none (initials, or the person glyph with no name), one of 48
  fixed emoji (identical lists, so a picture one shell stores the other
  accepts), or a photo from the system picker — PhotosPicker on iOS,
  PickVisualMedia on Android — which hands over only the chosen photo with
  no permission prompt (the Play manifest allowlist check passed
  unchanged). The photo is centre-cropped square, at most 256 px, JPEG
  (Android also turns it upright from its EXIF orientation), and stored in
  the vault under `ledger/self-avatar`. Anything unreadable decodes to no
  picture: a picture is decoration, and the ledger must never fail to open
  over one.
- **Where it shows**: Settings opens with a profile card ("Edit"); the
  top-right button on every tab shows the photo, emoji or initials (the
  plain glyph until there is a name or picture). A revision counter bumped
  on every change reloads them.

**Findings.**
- **The picker hands the photo over "Location Included"** (iOS 27's own
  label). The stored picture is re-drawn, so it should carry no metadata;
  that is now proven, not assumed: a test writes a JPEG with a GPS
  dictionary, checks the input really carries it, and finds none in the
  stored picture. Android re-encodes through `Bitmap.compress`, which writes
  no EXIF at all.
- **An explicit label colour hides Material's disabled state**: Android's
  "Save name" looked tappable with nothing to save; the label now dims.
- **Seen**: iOS 27 — initials "T" in the top-right, the profile card, the
  fox chosen, the system picker's "Private Access to Photos", a photo
  cropped round, and the photo in the top-right. API 34 — the profile card,
  the fox in the top bar, the system picker ("This app can only access the
  photos you select"), and a 640 x 400 image cropped to its centre.

**Why.** The founder, 2026-09-21: the account section should have
"anything like an about section about an app and things an actual app
usually has, so research and add those". What such a page carries: the
version, who makes the app, how to report a security problem, the legal
position, and the open-source licences, which the licences themselves
require the app to show.

**What was built (both shells).**
- **Settings → About**: the version line and "About SKIPTI".
- **About page**: "SKIPTI", "Made by Vardr Labs", "Version 0.1.0 (1)" on
  iOS (CFBundleShortVersionString, CFBundleVersion) and "Version 0.1.0
  (1000)" on Android (versionName, versionCode: D-116's scheme), and "Core
  0.1.0" (`skiptiCoreVersion()`). PROMISES: GUARANTEES.md 1–7 shortened.
  PRIVACY: five sentences, each passing SPEC §14.6 with its limit next to
  it: the ledger is in an encrypted database, and anyone who can unlock the
  phone can open SKIPTI (there is no app lock yet); without an account the
  ledger leaves the phone only when you export it (the FX fetch is still a
  stub, so nothing else is sent); with an account the data is encrypted
  before it is sent, and the server learns that the account exists, the
  device count, roughly how much is stored, when you sync and your internet
  address (THREAT_MODEL.md's metadata table); Google or Apple learn that
  you use SKIPTI and never see the ledger (ADR-0035); no ads, trackers or
  analytics. SECURITY: SECURITY.md's address and its 48-hour
  acknowledgement, a "Report a security problem" button that opens a mail
  draft, and, when no mail app is set up, "No email app is set up on this
  phone. Write to security@vardrlabs.com." (seen on both: neither the
  emulator nor the simulator has one). LEGAL: SPEC §13.5's disclaimer, and
  Licences. The copy is identical on both shells: both pin one SHA-256 of
  it, derived in Python separately from either shell.
- **Licences page**: an intro line, then groups (fonts, icons and words;
  shared core; Android), each entry with its version and the licence
  SKIPTI takes it under; tapping one shows its notice and the licence
  text, re-flowed for a phone (hard-wrapped lines joined, paragraphs and
  list items kept; a test proves no word moves).
- **The inventory**: `scripts/licences.py` writes
  `native/licences/licences.json` (204 components, 26 distinct texts, 111
  KB), which iOS bundles as a resource and Android reads from its assets.
  Rust: `cargo metadata --offline` for aarch64-apple-ios and both Android
  targets, every crate reachable from skipti-core through normal
  dependencies, proc-macro crates left out (they run in the compiler); the
  list is otherwise conservative (crates only the bindings generator uses
  are listed). C: SQLCipher 4.14.0 and SQLite 3.51.3 from libsqlite3-sys's
  bundled sources, OpenSSL 3.6.3 from openssl-src (Android only, D-91).
  Android: each flavour's `ReleaseRuntimeClasspath` from Gradle (offline),
  BOMs and the per-platform halves of multiplatform modules dropped,
  licences read from each POM (its parent's when it has none). Where a
  crate offers a choice SKIPTI takes Apache-2.0 (one shared copy of the
  text covers them all), then MIT; MIT, BSD, Zlib and similar texts are the
  crate's own file, since each carries its own copyright line, and a file
  without the licence's own wording is refused. iOS shows 104 core entries
  and 5 others; play 106 + 89 + 5; direct 106 + 78 + 4 (no Google art, no
  Play services, no googleid).
- **Gate leg 20**, "licence inventory (regenerate == committed)", last in
  the Android block: `licences.py --check` runs its self-test, regenerates
  and compares, and names what was added or removed. A new kind of licence
  stops it until a person has looked.

**Findings.**
- **NOTICE was missing what the apps ship.** SQLCipher is BSD-3-Clause,
  whose second clause requires its notice "in the documentation and/or
  other materials provided with the distribution" of every binary; it was
  not in NOTICE and the apps showed nothing. Also missing: OpenSSL
  (Android), both fonts (in the tree since `c989f5b`, 2026-08-24), and
  Lucide's MIT notice for the icons it took from Feather, `plus` among
  them. NOTICE now names them and points at the inventory.
- **The generator's self-test caught two bugs of its own before any
  output depended on them**: with `(MIT OR Apache-2.0) AND Unicode-3.0` the
  tie-break took MIT (both alternatives ranked equal on their worst
  licence; the sum now decides), and a truncated expression crashed
  instead of refusing.
- **IBM Plex Mono's upstream licence** (google/fonts `ofl/ibmplexmono/
  OFL.txt`) declares Reserved Font Name "Plex". The OFL counts a subset as
  a Modified Version, and a Modified Version may not use a reserved name;
  the bundled subsets keep "IBM Plex Mono". Asked (2026-09-22), the
  founder chose to ship IBM's unmodified files; that is a unit of its own
  (§4).
- **Three MIT crates ship licence files with no copyright line**
  (`cargo_metadata`, `winnow`, `zmij`); they are shown as shipped.
- `androidx.biometric` is already in both flavours, pulled in by
  `androidx.credentials` (relevant to D-147).
- **Seen**: API 34 play, light — Settings' About card, the About page
  (three screens), the mail fallback, the Licences list, SQLCipher's text,
  system Back to the list; dark — SQLCipher's text re-flowed; the end of
  the list (Play services, googleid, JNA, Kotlin). Direct — the list has no
  Google button and ends with no Google entries. iOS 27, light — Settings,
  About, the mail fallback, Licences (no OpenSSL, no Android section), IBM
  Plex Mono's re-flowed OFL.

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** SPEC §3.4: the kit is "re-viewable later behind a fresh
biometric prompt". iOS has had that screen since D-80 and a Settings link
since D-144; Android showed the twelve words once, at setup, and never
again. The WORKLOG queued it as the next Settings item.

**What was built (Android).**
- **Settings → Your data → Recovery Kit**, the twin of iOS's card: "Your
  twelve words, the only way back into this ledger. Your fingerprint or
  face first, every time."
- **The kit screen** (route `kit`, system Back to Settings): locked, with
  "Re-viewing needs your fingerprint or face, every time." and Reveal.
  Reveal builds a NEW platform `BiometricPrompt` ("Re-view your Recovery
  Kit", Cancel) for every attempt: strong biometrics only on API 30+
  (`BIOMETRIC_STRONG`), biometric by default on 28–29, no screen-lock
  fallback, matching iOS's biometrics-only rule. The vault is read only
  after that attempt passes, and the words live in memory only for the
  screen's life. A non-matching finger is not terminal (the system says so
  and stays open); only an error ends the attempt, and each has its own
  message: not set up (1, 11, 12), locked out (7, 9), no screen lock (14),
  cancelled (5, 10, 13), and "not recognized" for the rest. Android 8 has
  no BiometricPrompt, and the screen says "Re-viewing needs Android 9 or
  later." rather than offering something weaker.
- **FLAG_SECURE**: `SecureWindow()` sets it while the kit screen, or
  setup's kit display, is on screen and clears it on leaving, so the words
  stay out of screenshots, screen recordings and the Recents thumbnail.
- **No new dependency.** `androidx.biometric` is already in both flavours
  (pulled in by androidx.credentials) but using it directly would make it
  a dependency of ours without CONTRIBUTING rule 4's review; the platform
  API does the job. USE_BIOMETRIC was already merged in from credentials;
  the app's own manifest now declares it, and the Play manifest allowlist
  check passed unchanged.

**Findings.**
- **The emulator reports a strong sensor** (`dumpsys biometric`: strength
  15), so `BIOMETRIC_STRONG` accepts its emulated fingerprint; with
  nothing enrolled the prompt ends at once with error 11.
- **Seen on API 34** (skipti-shots, with a test PIN and one emulated
  fingerprint, which the founder approved for this check): before
  enrolment, Reveal says "Biometrics are not set up on this device."; after
  it, Reveal raises the system prompt ("Re-view your Recovery Kit", "Touch
  the fingerprint sensor", "Cancel"); an unenrolled finger leaves it open;
  the enrolled finger shows "Created 28 Aug 2026", all twelve words and
  "This is the only way back in…"; Cancel shows "Re-viewing was cancelled.
  Nothing was shown."; system Back returns to Settings. The kit screen's
  window carries `SECURE` and `screencap` fails (exit 1), so the only
  screenshots are of Settings; the flag is gone again once Back reaches
  Settings. Text was read with `uiautomator dump`.

**Sabotage 7/7**, expected red sets fixed before the run (the reasoning for
each set is in the local runner). D1 was run by hand on the emulator,

| K1 | the vault is read before the prompt | `KitRevealTest.a_missing_or_unreadable_kit_is_said_plainly`, `KitRevealTest.every_attempt_prompts_afresh_and_the_vault_is_read_only_after_a_pass` only |
| K2 | a failed prompt still reveals | `KitRevealTest.every_attempt_prompts_afresh_and_the_vault_is_read_only_after_a_pass` only |
| K3 | a cancel reads as not recognized | `KitRevealTest.each_platform_error_gets_its_own_message`, `KitRevealTest.every_attempt_prompts_afresh_and_the_vault_is_read_only_after_a_pass` only |

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** D-146 found that IBM Plex's licence (the release's LICENSE.txt:
"Copyright © 2017 IBM Corp. with Reserved Font Name "Plex"") reserves the
name, that the SIL OFL 1.1 forbids a Modified Version from using a
reserved name, and that the bundled files were subsets (Modified Versions)
of the Google Fonts build that kept "IBM Plex Mono". Asked, the founder
chose to ship IBM's unmodified files rather than rename a trimmed copy.

**What was done.**
- **Downloaded, with the founder's yes**: github.com/IBM/plex release
  `@ibm/plex-mono@2.5.0` (2026-06-11), `ibm-plex-mono.zip`, 6,940,652
  bytes, SHA-256 `6d23f012…481c` (in full in `native/fonts/README.md`).
  Font data only: nothing in it was run; only
  `fonts/complete/ttf/IBMPlexMono-{Regular,Medium}.ttf` and LICENSE.txt
  were extracted.
- **Copied unchanged** to `native/fonts/` (iOS) and Android's
  `res/font/`: 173,052 and 174,008 bytes, version 2.005, 1,049 code points
  (the subsets had 245), with every character the app needs (₹ ₽ € − · Á
  é). Each app grows by about 257 KB.
- **iOS lookups through one name each.** IBM's files call their PostScript
  faces `IBMPlexMono` and `IBMPlexMono-Medm`; the Google Fonts build said
  `IBMPlexMono-Regular` and `IBMPlexMono-Medium`. iOS resolves faces by
  that name in the type system, the Recovery Kit PDF and a Dynamic Type
  test, and an unknown name falls back to the system font without any
  error. `TypeRole.plexRegular` / `plexMedium` now hold IBM's names and all
  three sites use them. Android loads the faces by resource file and needed
  no change.
- **Guards**: `scripts/licences.py` (the licence inventory gate leg) pins
  both files' SHA-256 and refuses a Plex that is not IBM's file, and refuses
  if Android's copy of any of the three faces differs from iOS's. A test on
  each shell pins the same hashes; the iOS test also resolves every face by
  its PostScript name and checks the family.
- NOTICE, `native/fonts/README.md` (rewritten: sources, hashes, "do not
  subset these"), `web/fonts/README.md` (its Plex subsets must be replaced
  before the web build) and the Licences page (IBM Plex Mono 2.005, "IBM's
  unmodified Regular and Medium") say the same.

**Findings.**
- **The swap alone would have broken iOS silently**: the PostScript names
  changed, and `UIFont(name:)` returns nil for a name no bundled face has,
  so numbers would have rendered in the system font. Only a force-unwrap
  of the Regular lookup in `BalanceLineTests` stood in the way, and
  nothing checked the Medium face at all. The new test resolves every face
  and names the one that is missing.
- **Seen**: iOS 27 Expenses (₹1,200.00, "Sep 16, 2026") and API 34
  Expenses (₹1,200.00, $8.40, "21 Sep 2026") in IBM's Plex Mono.

**Sabotage 4/4**, expected red sets fixed before the run (the
reasoning for each set is in the local runner). F1, F3 and F4 copy the old
trimmed file back over the new one.

| Row | Sabotage | Red |
|---|---|---|
| F2 | iOS asks for the old name IBMPlexMono-Medium | `AboutTests.testTheBundledFontsResolveAndPlexIsIBMsOwnFiles` only |
| F1 | native Regular is the old trimmed copy | `licences.py --check` exits 1: "IBMPlexMono-Regular.ttf is not IBM's unmodified file" |
| F3 | Android's Medium is the old trimmed copy | `AboutTest.plex_is_ibms_own_files_and_both_shells_ship_the_same_fonts` only |
| F4 | Android's Medium is the old trimmed copy (through --check) | `licences.py --check` exits 1: "android res/font/ibmplexmono_medium.ttf differs from native/fonts/IBMPlexMono-Medium.ttf" |

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget). **The hosted relay is
not changed by this commit**: it runs `9952f95` (its `/version`, read
2026-09-22) until the founder deploys.

**Why.** SPEC §4.4: account deletion has a "7-day grace with a cancel link,
clearly stated, then irreversible". The relay deleted everything in one
call (D-62), and THREAT_MODEL said the grace, its mitigation for a stolen
Google or Apple sign-in, was not built. Asked before the in-app screen, the
founder chose to build the grace first.

**What was built (relay).**
- **The request** (`POST /v1/account/delete`, bearer-gated as before):
  every session family of the account ends at once, including the caller's;
  the request is written to a new table, `r_deletions` (schema v4: subject
  id and wall-clock milliseconds, in the same transaction as the surviving
  session set); the answer is **202** `{"delete_after_ms": …}`, seven days
  on. It used to be 204 with everything gone.
- **The cancel**: every sign-in (email code, passkey, Apple, Google, and
  the dev mint, which shares the email path) looks for a pending deletion
  of the account it resolved, removes it, and says `"deletion_cancelled":
  true` in its response. The field is omitted when false, so no other
  response changes, and both apps' decoders already ignore unknown fields.
- **The purge**: `purge_due_deletions(state, now)` completes every request
  older than `DELETION_GRACE_MS` (7 × 24 h), removing the account record,
  device bindings, logs, escrow, passkey credentials, envelope rows, the
  pending row and the sessions in one vault transaction, then memory. The
  relay binary runs it at boot and every hour on a blocking thread and
  prints only how many it completed.
- **Recovery across a restart**: pending requests load at boot with their
  original timestamps, so a restart neither forgets a request nor restarts
  its week.

**Findings.**
- **The passkey path would have skipped the cancel.** `passkey_auth_finish`
  minted its session through a copy of `mint_verified_session`'s body; the
  edit that added the cancel to the two shared tails found three session
  constructions where it expected two and refused. The passkey path now
  calls `mint_verified_session`, and a test proves a passkey sign-in during
  the grace keeps the account.
- **The old purge changed memory first**, then wrote the vault, and called
  a retry safe; but `remove_subject` had already emptied the registry, so a
  retry after a failed write would have run with no identifiers and no
  devices, and left the passkey and envelope rows behind. With an hourly retry that path is real; the purge
  now reads the registry without changing it, commits the vault, and only
  then changes memory.
- **A race, closed by design**: a sign-in at the deadline could have
  rescued an account between the sweep choosing it and removing it. Both
  hold the deletions lock throughout (taken first everywhere, so no lock
  order inverts).
- **SPEC's "cancel link"** assumes an email address, which SKIPTI never
  requires; signing in again is the cancel, and THREAT_MODEL now states its
  limit (an attacker holding your sign-in can also cancel, or ask).

**For the founder: deploying it.** DEPLOY-ORACLE §7.1, with `9952f95` as
the commit being replaced. The new relay migrates the database from schema
v3 to v4 on first start, and the old binary cannot open the result, so the
backup in step 4 is what makes a rollback possible. Afterwards `/version`
must name this commit, and §10.4's restore drill runs once the backup timer
has a v4 snapshot.

**Sabotage 8/8**, expected red sets fixed before the run (the
reasoning for each set is in the local runner).

| Row | Sabotage | Red |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | an email-code sign-in does not cancel | `signing_in_during_the_grace_keeps_the_account` only |
| G2 | a passkey/Apple/Google sign-in does not cancel | `a_passkey_sign_in_during_the_grace_also_keeps_the_account` only |
| G3 | no grace: due as soon as asked | `deletion_removes_every_trace_survives_a_restart_and_spares_the_survivor` only |
| G4 | the request does not end the sessions | `deletion_removes_every_trace_survives_a_restart_and_spares_the_survivor` only |
| G5 | the purge leaves the pending row | `deletion_removes_every_trace_survives_a_restart_and_spares_the_survivor` only |
| G6 | pending deletions are forgotten at boot | `deletion_removes_every_trace_survives_a_restart_and_spares_the_survivor` only |
| G7 | a cancel is not written to the vault | `a_passkey_sign_in_during_the_grace_also_keeps_the_account`, `signing_in_during_the_grace_keeps_the_account` only |
| G8 | an ordinary sign-in reports deletion_cancelled=false | `signing_in_during_the_grace_keeps_the_account` only |

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget). **The hosted relay runs
D-149** (`/version` = `03e6abf…`, and `/v1/dev/session` = 401, read
2026-09-24 after the founder deployed it).

**Why.** SPEC §4.4 (and Apple, §12.2) require deletion inside the app: "One
screen, reachable from Settings in two taps", no repeated "are you sure",
"7-day grace … clearly stated", and "a full export **before** deletion, in
the same flow". D-149 built the grace on the relay; no app could use it, and
Android had no deletion call at all.

**What was built (both shells, twins).**
- **Where**: Settings → Account, a "Delete account" card among the account
  controls, which exist only with a session (GUARANTEES #5: no account, no
  card). Tap 1 opens the screen; tap 2 is its red Delete account.
- **The screen**: WHAT IS DELETED (everything the server keeps for the
  account; the ledger on this device stays), 7 DAYS TO CHANGE YOUR MIND (all
  sessions end at once; deleted 7 days later; signing in before then keeps
  it; then it cannot be undone), EXPORT FIRST (the existing export, one tap,
  above the Delete button). One confirmation, because the grace is the undo.
- **The answer**: 202 → "Your account will be deleted on {day}. Sign in
  again before then to keep it."; 204 (a relay older than D-149) → "Your
  account has been deleted."; a 202 without a positive `delete_after_ms` is a
  bad response, never a success. Afterwards the device drops its session
  and keeps its ledger (never auto-delete user data).
- **An expired access token** (15 minutes) answers 401: the app rotates once
  and **stores the rotated pair before retrying**, because the refresh token
  it replaced is single-use and already spent; a second 401 says "This
  device's sign-in is no longer valid. Sign in again, then delete." without
  claiming nothing was deleted. Other failures are not retried.
- **The cancel**: every sign-in path (email code, Apple, Google, passkey;
  both shells) now builds its session through one `SessionCreatedBody`
  conversion that carries `deletion_cancelled`, and Settings shows "Your
  account deletion was cancelled." The flag is never stored: iOS leaves it
  out of `RelaySession`'s `CodingKeys` (a non-optional key there would have
  made every session stored before D-150 fail to decode, and a failed decode
  reads as signed out); Android marks it `@Transient`.
- **`--deletion-proof`** on each shell: signs this device in through a dev
  relay's mint (D-65, which shares every sign-in's tail on the relay, the
  cancel included) and opens Settings. The live relay refuses the mint.

**Seen, end to end, against a local dev relay** (`SKIPTI_DEV_UNSAFE_SESSION_MINT=1`,
a throwaway vault; the server code is the deployed commit's): iOS 27
(iPhone 17) and API 34 (`skipti-shots`), light and dark. Card → screen →
Delete → the relay's `r_deletions` holds one row and the screen says "deleted
on Oct 1, 2026" (Android "1 Oct 2026"; asked on 2026-09-24) → Done → Settings
reads "No account" with the account controls gone. Launched again, the same
account signs in: `r_deletions` is empty and Settings says "Your account
deletion was cancelled." Export opens from the flow and its Back returns to
the deletion screen.

**Findings.**
- **A latent sync failure, not D-150's.** With the local relay up, the iOS
  suite ran its relay tests, and `SyncE2ETests.testRoundTripThroughTheRelayIsByteIdentical`
  failed: "kv bytes diverged at ledger/expenses". With this unit's changes
  stashed, HEAD fails identically (166 executed, 1 failure). It had been
  hidden as one of the 8 skips. Recorded in §4, not fixed here.
- **Storing the flag would have signed people out.** Swift's synthesized
  decoder uses `decode`, not `decodeIfPresent`, for a non-optional property
  with a default value, so adding `deletionCancelled` to `RelaySession` the
  obvious way breaks every stored session. Row I6 proves the test catches it.
- **The rotated refresh token.** The sync engine already persists a rotated
  session; a deletion path that refreshed without storing would have left
  the device holding a spent refresh token after any failed retry.

**Sabotage 13/13**, expected red sets fixed before the run (the
reasoning for each set is in the local runner). No relay ran, so the relay
tests skipped in every iOS row.

| Row | Sabotage | Red |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | a 202 is read as deleted now | `AccountDeletionTests.testAnExpiredAccessTokenIsRotatedStoredAndRetried`, `AccountDeletionTests.testTheGraceAnswerDecodesItsDeadline` only |
| I2 | a zero deadline is accepted | `AccountDeletionTests.testAGraceAnswerWithoutADeadlineIsABadResponse` only |
| I3 | the rotated session is not stored | `AccountDeletionTests.testAnExpiredAccessTokenIsRotatedStoredAndRetried` only |
| I4 | any failure spends a refresh | `AccountDeletionTests.testAServerFailureIsNotRetried` only |

| I6 | the flag is stored with the session | `AccountDeletionTests.testTheFlagIsNeverStoredAndOldSessionsStillDecode` only |
| A1 | a 202 is read as deleted now | `AccountDeletionTest.an_expired_access_token_is_rotated_stored_and_retried`, `AccountDeletionTest.the_grace_answer_decodes_its_deadline` only |

The gate ran on the working tree over `03a6885`. The commit adds only this
BUILD-LOG record and `docs/WORKLOG.md` to the tree the gate saw.

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** D-150's end-to-end check started a local relay, the iOS suite ran
its relay tests for once, and `SyncE2ETests.testRoundTripThroughTheRelayIsByteIdentical`
failed: "kv bytes diverged at ledger/expenses". HEAD failed identically. This
is the proof that a lost device gets its ledger back from sync.

**Diagnosis, one cause at a time** (each shown by printing both byte strings
into the proof's detail, temporarily):
1. **iOS: same data, different bytes.** BEFORE began `{"currencyCode":…,"note":…`
   and AFTER `{"timestampMs":…,"paidMinor":…`, every value equal. Swift's
   `JSONEncoder` promises no key order. A relay-free test written first
   (`ProjectionBytesTests`) failed on the old code: 1156 bytes against 1156,
   differing on every other rebuild, and the sorted-keys check found the
   keys unsorted. Fix: `LedgerStore.kvEncoder()` (`.sortedKeys`) for every
   write of `ledger/expenses`, `ledger/settlements` and `ledger/groups`,
   including `GroupStore.write`. Record blobs (the sealed payloads) and
   non-ledger keys are unchanged.
2. **Both shells: groups do not sync.** With (1) fixed, the next divergence
   was `ledger/groups`: BEFORE held the "Goa Trip" group, AFTER was `[]`.
   Groups are per-device kv, not records (D-121 (3), in §4 since). The
   proof was written for D-67's snapshot sync, which carried groups, and was
   not updated when records replaced snapshots. Both proofs now assert the
   set record sync carries, expenses and settlements, and say why.
3. **Android: the proof never cleared the records.** Its live test, run with
   the relay, failed with AFTER `[]` for expenses. iOS's proof cleared kv AND
   records (D-121); Android's cleared only kv, so every pulled record was
   already present, `applied` was 0, the rebuild never ran and the ledger
   stayed empty. A real lost device has no records, so restore itself was
   not at fault: the proof simulated the wrong loss. It now calls
   `clearRecords()`.
4. **iOS: once per relay.** A second run on the same relay ended "push did
   not confirm (offline)": the fixed account's log already held the first
   run's entries, sealed with a key the new vault did not have. It now mints
   a fresh identifier and device id per run, as Android's has since D-117;
   two further runs on one relay passed.

**Proven with the relay up:** iOS 179 executed, 0 skipped, 0 failures (the
whole hosted suite); Android `SyncProofLiveTest` passing in both flavours;
then this gate.

**Sabotage 6/6**, run with the relay up, expected red sets fixed before the
run (the reasoning for each set is in the local runner). P1 reads "23
failures": XCTest counts failed assertions, and the 20-round rebuild loop
fails in many rounds.

| Row | Sabotage | Red |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | the kv encoder loses sorted keys | `ProjectionBytesTests.testAnAppendAndARebuildWriteTheSameBytes`, `ProjectionBytesTests.testRebuildingFromRecordsGivesTheSameBytesEveryTime`, `ProjectionBytesTests.testTheLedgerIsWrittenWithSortedKeys`, `SyncE2ETests.testRoundTripThroughTheRelayIsByteIdentical` only |
| P2 | the rebuild writes expenses with a plain encoder | `ProjectionBytesTests.testAnAppendAndARebuildWriteTheSameBytes`, `ProjectionBytesTests.testRebuildingFromRecordsGivesTheSameBytesEveryTime`, `SyncE2ETests.testRoundTripThroughTheRelayIsByteIdentical` only |
| P3 | the iOS proof asserts groups again | `SyncE2ETests.testRoundTripThroughTheRelayIsByteIdentical` only |
| P4 | the iOS proof uses a fixed account again | `SyncE2ETests.testRoundTripThroughTheRelayIsByteIdentical` only |
| A1 | Android's proof stops clearing the records | `SyncProofLiveTest.the_dev_mint_round_trip_proves_the_whole_chain_end_to_end` only |
| A2 | Android's proof asserts groups again | `SyncProofLiveTest.the_dev_mint_round_trip_proves_the_whole_chain_end_to_end` only |

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** D-151 proved that a restored device gets its expenses back but not
the groups they belong to, or who "you" are: both lived only in each
device's kv (D-121 (3); D-135 (b): "the `ledger/self` record must travel
with them"). Sharing groups between people needs the same thing first.

**The founder's decision (2026-09-24, asked before building):** "One you,
merge": each account has one "you"; a new device adopts it; two devices that
each already had their own "you" with expenses become one person
automatically. Built in stages: this unit (records and projection, core
only), then the shells, then the merge.

**What was built (core).**
- **Operations** (JSON, `op` first, fields in declaration order, absent
  names omitted; unknown kinds and fields refused): `create` (group, name,
  settlement currency, members with optional names), `addMember`,
  `renameMember`, `renameGroup`, and `you` (id, optional name). Ids are 32
  lowercase hex; names follow `ffi::member_name`'s rules exactly (a test pins
  the shared 64-character limit); currencies must parse.
- **Record type 0x03**, `GroupOperation`, reserved in the header format and
  unused until now. A new type (0x06) was the first design and was dropped:
  `ffi_record_pack`/`unpack` refuse unknown types, so every shipped build
  would have failed its whole pull. "You" rides 0x03 with PERSONAL scope,
  group operations with the group's scope, so "you" can never be shared into
  a group's log when groups are shared between people.
- **One projection**, pure and order-independent: per-field last writer wins
  by `VersionId` (millis, counter, device: ADR-0034, no clock precision
  assumed); the earliest create fixes the settlement currency (§5.2) and the
  group's creation time; members are a union in first-written order (renames
  that arrive before their member's add still land); "you" is the earliest
  `you` record and its name the latest written for that id, with other ids
  reported; unreadable records are listed in `rejected`, operations on a
  missing group or member in `pending`, none dropped.
- **Told apart for display**: two OTHER members who end up with one name
  (compared case-insensitively, as `named_group` does) show as "Rahul" and
  "Rahul (2)", fitted to 64 characters. Without it, two devices each adding a
  "Rahul" offline would make `ffi_named_group` refuse the group and the
  shells fail to load every group. "You" may share a name, as `named_group`
  allows. The records keep what each device wrote.
- **FFI**: `GroupOpIn` (a UniFFI enum), `ffi_encode_group_op`,
  `ffi_decode_group_op`, `ffi_project_groups` → `GroupsProjectionOut`
  (`GroupWire` plus names, "you", other ids, rejected, pending). Bindings
  regenerated; no shell calls them yet.

**Tests.** Codec: six operations to exact bytes, written by hand and
re-derived independently in Python from the wire rules
(`.drafts/d152/golden.py`: 6/6); twelve bad operations refused on encode AND
decode; unknown kinds and fields unreadable. Projection: each rule on its
own, ties by counter then device, and every one of the 720 orders of six
records that exercise all rules at once projecting identically; a record
delivered twice counts once. FFI: every kind round-trips; the projection's
groups validate through `ffi_named_group` (two "Rahul"s included); a bad
device id is refused at the boundary.
