**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** D-152 gave core group and "you" records; neither app wrote or read
them, so groups still did not sync and a restored device got none back.

**What was built (twins).**
- **One write path.** `save` (iOS `GroupStore`, Android `saveNamed`) takes the
  groups before and after a change, turns the difference into operations
  (`LedgerStore.operations`: create for a new group, rename group, add member,
  rename member; nothing when nothing changed), appends them as records, and
  rebuilds `ledger/groups` from the records. `ensureSelf` writes a `you`
  record when it first mints "you"; `setYourName` writes one with the name.
  Group operations take the group's scope; `you` takes personal scope
  (`groupId` nil) and so can never enter a group's log.
- **Reads.** `rebuildProjection` (after every pull that applies a record, and
  every expense revision) now also rebuilds groups and "you" from core's
  `ffiProjectGroups`.
- **Adoption** (the founder's "one you per account"): the rebuild writes the
  account's "you" (the earliest `you` record) as this device's, keeps any
  other ids as `aliases`, and carries this device's own name over when the
  records name none. `namedGroups` shows as "you", in each group, this id or
  else an alias that is a member.
- **Safety** (D-122 #3's trap: a rebuild that runs before old data has
  records erases it):
  - a **content-based, idempotent backfill** mints a create for every kv
    group with no create record and a `you` for a kv "you" with none; it
    runs before every push and every group rebuild, so every pre-D-153 vault
    and every import syncs its groups; an operation core refuses is skipped;
  - the **union rule**: a rebuild keeps every kv group that has no create
    record after the projected ones, so nothing the records lack is erased;
  - an unreadable group list throws and is never overwritten;
  - a group with no create record is saved whole, as a create, so an edit to
    it cannot wait forever in `pending` and vanish.
- **The proofs** assert `ledger/groups` again on both shells (D-151's (a)).

**Seen.** The iOS 27 simulator's vault predates D-153 (its group lived only
in kv). It loaded normally (Balance: Goa, 3 members, ₹500.00 owed); People in
Goa → "Amit" → Add person saved through backfill, diff and rebuild, and Amit
appears in the list.

**Tests (twins, 9 per shell).** The scopes of what naming yourself and
creating a group write; only an add and a rename for an add and a rename; a
restored device gets groups and "you" back byte for byte; a second device
adopts the account's "you" and makes new groups under it; a group made under
another "you" still loads, shown as "(You)" (without the alias it would fail
to load); kv-only groups and "you" are backfilled once and never erased (with
a damaged group that only the union rule keeps); an unreadable group list is
never overwritten; two devices' offline renames converge byte for byte on the
later one; the diff on its own.

edits a legacy kv-only group. The edit waited in `pending`, the union rule
kept the old group, and the edit was lost, which is exactly the loss the
whole-create rule exists to stop. The prediction was incomplete, not the
code. The expectation was corrected in the runner with a note, the two rows
re-ran (2/2), and both runs are kept (`results_d153_run1.json`). The table

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** The founder chose "one you, merge" (2026-09-24). D-153 made a device
adopt the account's "you" and keep its own earlier id as an alias, so its
groups still loaded; but expenses it paid under that id still counted as a
different person, and a group holding both read as you owing yourself.

**What was built.**
- **Core, `straumr::identity::Yous`**: the account's "you" and the other ids
  its devices wrote as "you" (both from D-152's projection). An id reads as
  "you" if it is one of them; shares collapsing onto "you" are **added**, in
  the position of the first, so they still sum to the amount paid; a
  settlement whose two ends both read as "you" is dropped.
- **Groups**: the projection maps member ids through it (first position;
  named by "you"'s own name in that group if it has one, else the merged
  id's), so a group holding two of your ids holds one.
- **FFI**: `ffi_merge_you_expenses` (payer, shares, "added by", "last edited
  by", every money-conflict value) and `ffi_merge_you_settlements`. Both are a
  no-op with one "you" and refuse malformed ids.
- **Shells (twins)**: the ONE expense projection (`Sync.project` /
  `project`) merges after core projects, so the kv ledger, the list, the
  balance and the detail screens agree; the settlement rebuild merges too.
  Records are never rewritten.

**Finding (both shells, caught by the new test on its first run).** B's
expense came back twice. The legacy backfill (D-121/D-141) runs once per
vault and mints a record for every kv row with no equal record. The test's
rebuild merged B's row (payer now the account's "you") before the backfill
had ever run on B, so the row no longer equalled its record and was minted
again: a duplicate expense. Real pulls and edits already ran the backfill
first, so no shipped path did this, but only by call order. `rebuildProjection`
now runs it first on both shells; row S1/A1 proves the test catches its
removal, and the test now also counts one expense per device.

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** Neither app could leave an account except by deleting it (D-150
(f)), and the relay's owner-scoped revoke (SPEC §4.3, D-34) had no caller.

**What was built (twins).**
- `IdentityService.revokeSession`: `POST v1/auth/session/revoke`
  `{"family_id": …}` with the bearer; 204 is success, and 401, 429 and 5xx map
  as on every gated route.
- `AccountSignOut.endSession`: revoke this device's family; on a 401 rotate
  once, store the rotated pair before retrying (a refresh spends the old
  token), and revoke again; any other failure returns "not confirmed" without
  throwing. The Settings action then calls `LedgerSync.signOut()` whatever the
  answer, and reloads.
- Settings → Account: a card in every signed-in state (active or waiting for
  approval) with the note and a secondary "Sign out"; no confirmation.

The gate ran on the working tree over `fe8978b`. The commit adds this BUILD-LOG
record and `docs/WORKLOG.md` to the tree the gate saw.

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** ADR-0037 (the founder's decisions of 2026-09-24) needs four things of
the relay before any app can share a group between people: a shared log per
group, invites a person can accept later, admission of the joiner's devices,
and an in-app inbox limited to people who already share a group.

**What was built** (`server/src/shared.rs`, a child module of `lib.rs`):
- **Group logs**, `POST/GET /v1/groups/{G}/log`. The account log's append and
  read were factored out unchanged (`append_to_log`, `read_log`), so both logs
  share one code path: client-chosen indices, 409 when two writers race (the
  apps already pull and retry). Rows go in `r_logs` under `group:<G>`.
  Authorisation is ADR-0022's: the caller's account owns a device in G's
  envelope set. Otherwise the answer is the uniform 401, byte for byte the
  answer for a group that does not exist.
- **Invites.** `POST /v1/groups/{G}/invites` (members only): the SHA-256 of
  the token as hex, a payload of 1–4096 bytes, and an expiry within 30 days,
  with at most 64 live invites per group. A repeated hash gets 409.
  `POST /v1/invites/open` takes the token and returns the group id, payload
  and expiry. It takes no group id because the joiner learns the group only
  from the sealed payload. It does not burn the invite.
- **Admission**, `POST /v1/groups/{G}/admit`. Every recipient must be the
  caller's own device, and the admitting device must be among them. The group
  must still exist. The new envelope set and the burned invite are written in
  ONE vault transaction (`RelayVault::admit`, which also refuses when the
  invite is no longer there), then memory is updated. The envelopes lock is
  held throughout, so no push interleaves.
- **Inbox.** `POST /v1/inbox` is refused unless EVERY recipient device's
  account shares a group with the sender. `GET /v1/inbox` returns the entries
  for this session's device; a session without a declared device gets its
  account's devices, as envelope reads do. `POST /v1/inbox/{id}/done` removes
  an entry, and to anyone but its device the entry reads as absent. No sender
  is stored. Limits: 16 entries per request, 32 per device, 4 KiB each, 30-day
  expiry.
- **Deletion and expiry.** The purge computes, under the invites lock, the
  groups whose every recipient is the deleted account's device, so no
  admission can race it. Their shared logs and invites go in the same vault
  transaction as the rest of the account (`delete_account` gained
  `emptied_groups`), and inbox rows addressed to the deleted devices go too.
  The binary's hourly sweep now also drops expired invites and inbox rows
  (`shared::purge_expired_shared`), and logs only a count. Boot never loads
  an expired row.
- **Schema v5**: `r_invites` and `r_inbox`. `RelayVault` gained
  `in_transaction` and `write_group_envelopes` (the latter shared with
  `replace_group_envelopes`, whose behaviour is unchanged). The v3 → v4
  migration test pinned `user_version = 4` while 4 was current; it now pins
  the current version.
- Lock order, written at the top of `shared.rs`: deletions → invites → inbox
  → store → envelopes → registry → vault.

**Tests.** `shared_groups_http` (6), through the real HTTP surface:
- the log is shared, strangers get the nonexistent group's answer, 409 on a
  race, and group writes leave the account log untouched;
- an invite: refused for a stranger, four bad shapes, a duplicate hash, the
  kept hash is not a token, four refused admissions that leave the invite
  live, then an admission of both of Bob's devices with the inviter's row
  untouched, then burned both ways;
- expiry is refused before the sweep, and the sweep removes only what expired;
- the inbox: strangers, unknown devices and one stranger in a list, shapes,
  per-device reads, removal only by the recipient device, and the 32 bound;
- the last member takes a solo group, its log and invite, while a shared
  group keeps its log and invite for the survivor, and inbox rows go with the
  deleted devices;
- everything survives a real reopen, and a burned invite stays burned.

`persist` (1): v4 → v5 with rows intact; an admission for the wrong group
rolls back; a burned invite cannot admit twice; inbox writes are all or none;
expired rows are not loaded and are swept; the last member's deletion takes
exactly the emptied group's rows.

The code was committed first (`641b6e0`), because the bindings freshness leg
compares against HEAD. This record commit adds only BUILD-LOG and
`docs/WORKLOG.md`.

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** ADR-0037's invites need core pieces before any screen can exist: the
link and its secret, the token and key derived from it, the payload the relay
keeps sealed, the in-app entry, and a way for a joiner to become the member
the group already has, without anyone evading their share.

**What was built** (`core/src/straumr/invite.rs`, `groups.rs`, `ffi.rs`):
- **The link.** `https://skipti.vardrlabs.com/join#` + unpadded base64url of the
  32-byte secret. The codec is written here (≈40 lines) rather than adding a
  dependency. It refuses padding, other alphabets, impossible lengths and
  non-canonical trailing bits, so every secret has exactly one spelling.
  `parse_link` forgives surrounding whitespace and nothing else.
- **Derivations.** `token` and `key` come from `hkdf_sha256(s, "skipti",
  info)` with the labels `skipti/v1/invite-token` and `skipti/v1/invite-key`;
  the relay receives `hex(SHA-256(token))`. Goldens for the link, token, hash
  and key were re-derived with Python's stdlib (`hmac`, `hashlib`, `base64`;
  `.drafts/d157/golden.py`), never read back from Rust.
- **The payload.** JSON `v:1` with `deny_unknown_fields`, sealed with
  AES-GCM under `key`, a random nonce (the key seals one message) and AAD
  `skipti/v1/invite-payload`. It is validated when sealed and again when
  opened, so a payload sealed by a build that did not check is still refused,
  and anything over the relay's 4 KiB cap is refused before it is made.
- **In-app entry.** `0x01 ‖ ephemeral public key ‖ sealed secret`, keyed by
  `HKDF(DH(eph, recipient), "skipti/v1/invite-inbox" ‖ eph ‖ recipient)`.
  Every entry uses a fresh ephemeral key, so there is no nonce state and the
  relay learns no sender.
- **`claim`** (group operation, group scope): group, member, the claimer's
  "you" id, and 1–16 devices (32-hex id, 64-hex lowercase agreement key; no
  device listed twice). Projection, after the member set is complete:
  - the first claim of a member, by record identity, stands;
  - the same account claiming again adds devices;
  - another account's claim goes to `contested`, reported and never applied;
  - a claim of a missing group or member waits in `pending`;
  - a member THIS account claimed joins `other_you_ids`, so D-154's merge reads
    the group's "Rahul" as the joiner: in Rahul's place, named as the group
    names him, and in balances.
  `ProjectedGroup.claims` lists the claims in member order for everyone else
  (linked to an account, with the devices whose six words can be compared).
- **FFI.** `GroupOpIn::Claim`, `ClaimDeviceIn`, `ClaimOut`,
  `GroupsProjectionOut.contested`, `ffi_group_key_generate` (keys born in
  core), and `ffi_invite_new`, `_is_link`, `_token`, `_open`,
  `_seal_for_device` and `_open_from_device`. The shells hold the LINK string
  and never see the secret.
- **Shells.** A claim takes its group's scope in `groupOpRecord` (Swift
  `switch`, Kotlin `when`; both are exhaustive and needed the case to compile).

**Tests.**
- invite (7): goldens; base64url round trips for lengths 0–40 and refuses
  five bad spellings; the link round-trips and eight near-misses are refused;
  token, key and hash all differ; a payload opens only with its own link, not
  after a bit flip, not truncated, not under another label; ten bad payloads
  are refused both ways, and an unknown field is unreadable; an inbox entry
  opens only on its device, with a fresh ephemeral key each time, and not
  after a flip, a version change or a truncation.
- claims (5): "you" for the claimer and linked for everyone else; the first
  claim stands in all 120 arrival orders (with a device added and one
  contested); a claim waits for its group and its member; the encoded bytes
  are pinned by hand; six bad claims are refused both ways, and 16 devices is
  the limit.
- FFI (3): a claim crosses the boundary and feeds the merge; an invite
  round-trips (token hash checked with `sha2` independently of `token_hash`);
  an in-app entry opens only on its device.

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** D-156 gave the relay group logs and invites, and D-157 gave core the
invite link and the claim. Nothing yet used them: groups still synced only
between one person's devices.

**What was built.**
- **Core.**
  - `GroupOp::GroupKey { group, epoch, key }` is a personal record; the
    projection lists every held key by group, then epoch, then first written.
  - A revision record carries its `scope`: an edit or delete whose scope
    differs from its expense's group is rejected and reported, never applied.
  - Per-group `aliases`: in every group, another account's claim makes that
    account's "you" id read as the member it claimed. `Yous` gained
    `with_aliases`, `id_in`, `shares_in` and `settlement_in`.
    `ffi_merge_you_expenses` and `ffi_merge_you_settlements` take the aliases,
    and renames of the joiner's "you" land on their member.
- **Shells** (`GroupSync.swift` / `GroupSync.kt`, twins):
  - `ensureGroupKeys` gives every group a key.
  - `ensureMembership` writes one envelope row per account: D-123's payload,
    a proper wrap of the key to this device, with the wrap counter persisted
    before use.
  - Each group's log is pushed with its own 4-byte session, seal counter,
    index cursor and pushed-HLC cursor; a 409 means pull and retry, up to
    three times.
  - `pull` opens each entry with every key held for the group and applies
    only what `refusal` allows (below).
  - `syncAll` never throws. `createInvite` registers with the relay and returns
    the link; `open` checks the relay's group id against the one sealed inside
    the payload; `redeem` admits the device, then writes the key record and the
    claim, then syncs the group.
- **What a group's log may bring in** (`refusal`, and the clock rule in
  `pull`). A pulled record is refused when:
  - its scope is not the group;
  - the group in its payload is not the group (expense, settlement, a
    revision's new money, and every group operation);
  - it is personal ("you", a key);
  - it claims to be written by this device (it would otherwise be pushed on
    and could stall this device's pushes);
  - its type is unknown, or its payload unreadable.
  A record stamped more than 24 hours ahead is applied but never fed to the
  clock, because core's `Hlc::receive` has no drift bound and group logs are
  written by other people.
- **Hooks.**
  - After a confirmed account push, and when there was nothing to push:
    `GroupSync.syncAll`.
  - On restore: the account log first (it carries the keys), then every group.
  - `LedgerSync.refresh()` when the app comes to the front: iOS `scenePhase`,
    Android `onResume`, skipped for the headless proof launches.
- **Docs.** ADR-0037 gained a refinements section (keys through the account
  log; the account log as backup; the acceptance rules; the aliases).
  THREAT_MODEL gained a bullet on what a member cannot do and a metadata row.

**Found along the way (and fixed):** the two-person test as first written had
Bob pay with the member id. Rewriting it to use Bob's own "you" id, which is
what his screens write, showed that Tim's device would name a stranger. That
is the core aliases above. A pull test was also added: without it, a
sabotage that skipped the refusal check stayed green, because the live test
sees only well-behaved records.

**Spotted, not fixed (pre-existing, offered as a separate task):** Android's
`HttpUrlConnectionTransport` builds a GET query as the literal
`?${query…}`, because the dollar sign is escaped. No caller passes a query
today.

The code was committed first (`ef2878a`), because the bindings freshness leg
compares against HEAD. **Correction:** that commit's message says "JVM 216 per
flavour". The gate counted 215: D-158's 212, plus `your_own_place_is_claimed_once`,
plus `InviteJoinTest`'s 2. The message miscounted, and the gate's number stands. This record commit adds BUILD-LOG, `docs/WORKLOG.md` and the
screenshots.

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** D-158 made inviting and joining work, but only in tests. People need
screens, and a QR code for when they are together (the founder, 2026-09-24:
QR together, link apart; invite a named person; in the ledger whether or not
they join).

**What was built.**
- **QR, in core** (`core/src/qr.rs`, `ffi_qr_encode`): byte mode,
  error-correction level M, versions 1–6 (up to 106 bytes; a link is 77, so
  version 5). The steps follow ISO 18004: bit stream, Reed-Solomon over
  GF(256)/0x11D, block interleaving, finders with separators, timing, one
  alignment pattern, the dark module, zig-zag placement skipping column 6,
  all eight masks scored by the four penalty rules, and BCH(15,5) format bits
  XOR 0x5412. Placement and format positions were checked line by line against
  a reference implementation. The shells draw the modules with a four-module
  quiet zone, dark on white in every mode.
- **Screens (twins, same copy and order):**
  - People gains an INVITE section: members other than you who have no claim,
    shown only with an account (GUARANTEES #5).
  - `InviteScreen` (7-day link) shows the QR, "Send the link" and "Copy link",
    and says the person joins as the named member and is already in the
    ledger.
  - "Join a group" on the Groups list, with an account, leads to
    `JoinPasteScreen`, then `JoinScreen`: offer, Join, joined; on failure,
    plain copy.
  - An opened link lands on `JoinScreen`: iOS `onOpenURL` into a sheet;
    Android a VIEW intent, on first launch and in `onNewIntent`.
- **Link plumbing:**
  - iOS: the `applinks:skipti.vardrlabs.com` entitlement.
  - Android: an `autoVerify` filter for `https://skipti.vardrlabs.com/join`,
    and `launchMode="singleTop"`.
  - The domain side is a founder deploy (runbook §8.2): the AASA `applinks`
    block, `handle_all_urls` in `assetlinks.json`, and `deploy/join/index.html`,
    served at `/join` for people without the app. That page loads nothing, and
    its CSP allows only its own script, by hash. The invite secret stays in the
    fragment, which browsers never send.
- **Proof launches** (not user flows): `--invite-proof` signs in through the dev
  mint, makes "Goa" with Rahul, syncs, and opens People; it also writes a link
  for another device. `--join-proof <link>` signs in as Bob and opens the
  join screen.

**Found while looking at it running (and fixed):**
1. On the Android joiner, People offered "Invite Tim". Nothing linked the
   creator of a group to their member; only joiners wrote claims. Now every
   account claims its own place in each group it is in (`ensureOwnClaims`,
   run by every group sync and before every invite), so everyone sees who has
   joined, and D-161 gets each member's device keys.
2. Designing the invite screen showed that a stale access token gets the same
   401 as "not your group" or "invite used", so an expired token would have
   silently stopped group sync after a quiet spell and shown a false "already
   used". `LedgerSync.freshSession` probes a cheap gated read and rotates once
   on 401, storing the rotated pair first. It runs before group sync when
   nothing was pushed, and on refresh, invite and join.
3. Android splits launch arguments on spaces, so the first join proof passed
   `--relay-local` as the link. The proofs now take whichever argument is an
   invite link, and a malformed link now reads "That is not a SKIPTI invite
   link." instead of "offline".

**Seen, against a local relay** (screenshots `ios/artifacts/d159-*`,
`android/artifacts/d159-*`):
- the iPhone's invite with its QR, and its People screen with "Invite Priya"
  and no Rahul once Bob had joined;
- Android (a fresh account) opened the iPhone's invite: "Tim invited you to
  Goa. You join as Rahul." → Join → "You are in Goa.";
- another fresh account joined as Priya, in dark mode, and its People screen
  lists Tim, Rahul, "Priya (You)" with nobody left to invite;
- the used link reads "This invite was already used or has expired."

No bindings change and no relay change: the relay routes are D-156's, and the
core seal and open are D-157's. **No deploy is needed.**

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** ADR-0037 decided that an in-app invite reaches only people you
already share a group with: their account is known through that group, so
there is no directory and no lookup by email or phone. It arrives as a banner
inside SKIPTI, with no push service (GUARANTEES #6). D-156 built the relay
inbox and D-157 the sealing; nothing used them yet.

**What was built (twins, same copy and order).**
- **Who can be reached** (`GroupSync.knownPeople`): other accounts' claims in
  your other groups, minus you and anyone already in this group, one per
  account, named as the first group that knows them, with every device their
  claims list.
- **Inviting** (People → FROM YOUR OTHER GROUPS, only with an account):
  - "Add Rahul": `member(for:)` / `memberFor` adds them. If an unlinked member
    already has that name (case-insensitively, core's clash rule), the row
    reads "Send Rahul an invite in SKIPTI" and uses that member. They are in
    the ledger from that moment, whether or not they accept.
  - Then `sendInApp`: D-158's `createInvite`, the link sealed to each device,
    and `POST /v1/inbox` once per device. Sent to at least one device: "Rahul
    is in Paris. They see your invite the next time they open SKIPTI."
    Otherwise: full (every device 429), no longer shares a group (401), or
    offline.
- **Receiving** (`pollInbox`, at the end of every group sync, only when the
  account has a group):
  - Only this device's entries, and only ids of the relay's shape (a relay
    that returned "../.." would otherwise choose the path this device posts
    to).
  - Each entry is opened with this device's key (`ffi_invite_open_from_device`),
    then the invite with the relay. An entry that will not open, a used or
    expired invite, or a group already here is marked done; offline waits.
  - Entries the relay no longer lists are dropped. A refused read throws and
    changes nothing.
  - What is kept goes in the vault (`invite-inbox/pending`: the link is a
    secret).
- **Banner** (every tab, under the title): "Tim added you to Paris." / "You
  are Rahul in its ledger. Accept to see it and add to it."
  - **Accept** (`GroupSync.accept`): joins, marks every entry for that group
    done, selects the group and returns to Balance. A used invite is cleared
    and says so.
  - **Not now**: hides it until the next launch.
- **New devices**: `ensureOwnClaims` adds this device to its account's
  existing claim when missing, so an invite reaches it too.
- **Proof launches** (not user flows):
  - `--in-app-proof [Group]`: signs in through the dev mint, makes the group,
    syncs, and opens its People screen.
  - `--inbox-proof`: signs in or keeps the session, syncs, and shows the real
    tabs.

**Seen, across platforms, both directions, against a local relay**
(screenshots `ios/artifacts/d160-*`, `android/artifacts/d160-*`):
1. The iPhone (Tim) made Goa with Rahul, and Android (Bob) joined through the
   link.
2. On the iPhone, the People screen of a new group, Paris, offered "Add Rahul /
   In Goa". A tap added Rahul and said "Rahul is in Paris. …".
3. Android's banner read "Tim added you to Paris. You are Rahul in its
   ledger. …". Accept took Balance to Paris.
4. Reversed, in dark mode on Android: Bob's new group Lisbon offered "Add Tim
   / In Goa". The iPhone's banner read "Bob added you to Lisbon. You are Tim
   in its ledger. …". Accept took Balance to Lisbon.

so each tab's own stack was nested and lost its bar. The proof now routes
outside it, and the banner moved from an inset on the TabView to each tab's
screen, under its bar.

No core, bindings or relay change: **no deploy is needed.**

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** SPEC §3.2: "Verify your peers or the ECDH is theatre." A relay that
substituted its own key for a member's could read the group. Each device key
has six words; unverified members show UNVERIFIED in the WATCH colour on the
group screen. ADR-0037 adds that the joiner learns the inviter's key from the
link itself, and that in person both screens show their six words side by
side, with one tap to confirm.

**What was built (twins, same copy and order).**
- `GroupSync.peers(store, group)` lists everyone in the group who joined from
  another account, from their claims, with the devices whose words have not
  been compared on this phone. You are never listed.
- `markVerified` stores `verified/<device id>` = the key's hex, in the vault
  only. `isVerified` needs the stored key to equal the claim's, so a changed
  key reads as not verified. A device someone adds later (D-160) makes them
  UNVERIFIED again.
- Joining marks the inviter's device verified with the key sealed in the link
  (`redeem`, D-158; the in-app accept goes through it too).
- On the People screen:
  - UNVERIFIED (WATCH) sits on the member's row.
  - The SIX WORDS section has "Compare six words with <name>" with its state,
    and SPEC §11's sentence for the first unverified member (with "their").
  - **Verify <name>** shows their words, one block per device, then "YOUR SIX
    WORDS" (this device's own key, never the relay's copy), then how to
    compare. "They match" stores it; "They don't match" says: "Then this may
    not be Rahul's device, or someone is in between. Do not add expenses to
    this group until the words match."
- Token `watch`: ADR-0023 §4 defined the text-safe light variant `#8a6d1f`
  for small WATCH text, and SPEC §11.2 gives `#E8C170` for dark. It is added
  to both token sets and to the Night contrast tests (4.5:1 on every surface).

**Seen, across platforms, with fresh accounts, against a local relay**
(screenshots `ios/artifacts/d161-*`, `android/artifacts/d161-*`):
- Android (Bob, joined through the iPhone's link) shows "Compare six words
  with Tim · Verified". Its compare screen shows Tim's words "eyebrow wave way
  category final blossom" and its own, "switch rail flat utility decrease
  refuse".
- The iPhone (Tim) shows Rahul UNVERIFIED in the WATCH colour, with the
  sentence. Verify Rahul shows "switch rail flat utility decrease refuse" as
  Rahul's words and "eyebrow wave way category final blossom" as its own:
  the same twelve words, crossed.
- "They match" turns the row to Verified and removes the label.
- **Not seen by eye:** Android's own "They match" path. Its side was already
  verified from the link; the JVM tests cover the store underneath.

No core, bindings or relay change: **no deploy is needed.**

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**The decision (the founder, 2026-09-25: "do a deep research and take what's
the best step for it for speed and security").** SPEC §4.3 says access tokens
live in memory only and refresh tokens in the Keychain or Keystore. Since
D-155's residue (c), both have been stored in the SQLCipher vault. The
research:
- **At rest, a Keychain item protects no better than the vault.** The vault's
  key is a Keychain item (`kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly`,
  `KeychainKeystore.swift`) or an AndroidKeyStore AES-GCM key
  (`AndroidKeystore.kt`). A refresh token in its own Keychain item would get
  the same protection class on the same device.
- **A memory-only access token costs a refresh on every cold start.** Refresh
  tokens rotate, and the relay revokes the whole family when a rotated token is
  replayed (`auth.rs`,
  `refresh_rotation_and_family_death_on_replay`). Two refreshes racing at
  launch (the foreground refresh and a push) would therefore sign the person
  out. Today one probe usually proves the stored access token instead
  (D-159's `freshSession`).
- **What actually exposed the vault was backups**, not the vault itself. SPEC
  §2.3 A7 and §3.7 require the vault to be excluded from backup, "enforced with
  backup exclusion flags rather than left to defaults". It was not: the Android
  manifest never set `allowBackup`, so Google cloud backup and device transfer
  were on, and the iOS vault folder carried no exclusion. The keys never leave
  the device, so a restored vault could not be opened. That sent ciphertext to
  Google or Apple, and landed the person on D-127's "vault will not open"
  screen on the new phone.

So: keep the tokens in the vault, amend §4.3 with this reasoning, and build
§3.7.

**What was built.**
- **iOS:** `VaultBackup.exclude` sets `isExcludedFromBackup` on
  `Application Support/ledger`. It is the folder, so SQLCipher's side files
  are covered. It runs in `LedgerStore.defaultStore()` and at launch
  (`loadGate`). A failure is logged and retried on the next open, never
  fatal. `isExcluded` reads from a fresh URL, because Foundation caches
  resource values per URL: the first test run read a stale "false" that way.
- **Android:** `android:allowBackup="false"`, `android:fullBackupContent="false"`,
  and `android:dataExtractionRules="@xml/data_extraction_rules"`. On Android 12
  and later, device transfer ignores `allowBackup`, so the rules exclude root,
  file, database, sharedpref and external from both `cloud-backup` and
  `device-transfer`.
- **SPEC §4.3** gains an "As built on iOS and Android" bullet with the
  reasoning above; the web rule is unchanged.
- **Gradle** (`build.gradle.kts`): the unit-test tasks now declare as inputs
  the manifest, `res/xml` and `target/debug/libskipti_core.*`. See below.

**Seen:**
- On the Android emulator, `dumpsys package` flags read `DEBUGGABLE HAS_CODE
  ALLOW_CLEAR_USER_DATA`, with no `ALLOW_BACKUP`, and `bmgr backupnow` answers
  "Backup is not allowed".
- On a fresh iOS simulator install there is no ledger folder. After one
  ordinary launch, `xattr` shows `com.apple.metadata:com_apple_backup_excludeItem`
  on it.
- Evidence files: `.drafts/d162/android-flags.txt` and `ios-xattr.txt` (not
  committed).

**Sabotage: run 1 2/4, run 3 (full) 4/4**, expected red sets fixed before
the run. In run 1, both Android rows (allowBackup on; device transfer takes
the database) stayed green. The runner deletes the results first, and the
files were fresh, but Gradle had restored a cached pass: the test reads the
manifest at run time, and Gradle's inputs for a unit test are classes and
classpath only. **Every gate's JVM leg would have missed a manifest
regression the same way, and a core change without a Kotlin change could
reuse old goldens.** CLAUDE.md §7 describes the symptom; this is the cause.
With the inputs declared, a targeted rerun (run 2) and the full run 3 went
red exactly where expected.

| Row | Sabotage | Red |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | the vault folder is marked for backup | `VaultGateTests.testTheVaultFolderIsNeverBackedUp` only |
| I2 | opening the vault no longer sets the flag | `VaultGateTests.testTheVaultFolderIsNeverBackedUp` only |
| A1 | allowBackup on | `LedgerStoreTest.the_vault_is_never_backed_up` only |
| A2 | device transfer takes the database | `LedgerStoreTest.the_vault_is_never_backed_up` only |

No core, bindings or relay change: **no deploy is needed.**

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** SPEC §2.3 A6 says someone who picks up your phone must not be able to
read the ledger: "released only on biometric or device credential, with an
app-level auto-lock". §3.7 adds "Default 2 min background, configurable,
never 'off' without a warning", and a task-switcher blur. None of it existed.

**What was built (twins, same rules and copy where the platforms allow).**
- `LockTimeout`: Immediately, After 1 / 2 / 5 / 15 minutes, Off. The default
  is 2 minutes, and a stored value this build does not know reads as the
  default, never Off.
- `AppLockRules`:
  - `lockedAtLaunch` is true only when the lock is on and possible.
  - `locksOnReturn` locks once the time in the background reaches the timeout
    (`>=`). A clock set backwards locks too.
- `AppLock`:
  - The setting lives in iOS `UserDefaults` or Android `SharedPreferences`.
    It is not sensitive, and D-162 keeps the preferences out of backups.
  - It is locked before the first render of the ledger, and only when the
    launch gate finds onboarding done, so a new person is not locked out of
    the flow they are in.
  - Background and front transitions come from iOS `scenePhase` and Android
    `onStop`/`onStart`.
  - Unlock uses a fresh system prompt each time: iOS
    `.deviceOwnerAuthentication`; Android `BiometricPrompt` with
    `BIOMETRIC_STRONG | DEVICE_CREDENTIAL`, the platform class, no library.
  - Proof launches skip it (they are not user flows).
- **Lock screen:** "SKIPTI is locked. Unlock with Face ID, Touch ID or your
  passcode." (Android: "…your fingerprint, face or screen lock."), with an
  Unlock button (primary), "Not unlocked. Try again." after a cancel, and the
  prompt raised on appear.
- **Switcher:**
  - iOS draws a plain SKIPTI cover whenever the scene is not active, so the
    switcher snapshot has no ledger. A solid cover is stronger than SPEC's
    blur.
  - Android calls `setRecentsScreenshotEnabled(false)` on 13+ while the lock
    is on.
- **Settings → App lock:**
  - iOS uses a menu picker and Android chips, like Appearance on each.
  - A line says what the setting does. Off asks to confirm. With no
    passcode or screen lock: "App lock needs a passcode on this phone…".

**Seen.**
- **iOS**, iOS 27 simulator, with a simulated Face ID enrolled for the check
  and removed after:
  - no lock straight after onboarding, and Settings → App lock "After 2
    minutes";
  - Off raises "Turn off app lock?"; Keep it on stores nothing (the default
    stands);
  - a relaunch opens locked with the Face ID prompt, and a match goes to
    Balance;
  - set to Immediately, then Home and back: locked again. A face that does
    not match, then Cancel: "Not unlocked. Try again.";
  - the app switcher shows only the SKIPTI cover.
- **Android**, emulator, with a test PIN set for the check and cleared after:
  - a relaunch opens locked with the system prompt. The credential screen is
    secure, so its screenshot is empty, and the dump reads "Unlock SKIPTI";
  - Back shows the lock screen with the failure copy. Unlock and the PIN go
    to Balance;
  - SKIPTI's stored Recents card is blank.
- Screenshots: `ios/artifacts/d163-*`, `android/artifacts/d163-*`.

No core, bindings or relay change: **no deploy is needed.**

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**The decision.** SPEC §3.7 says screenshots are blocked on ledger screens.
Asked (2026-09-25), with the cost stated (people screenshot balances to send
to the group; blocking also stops testers capturing bugs), the founder chose
**"Setting, default off"**. SPEC §3.7 gains an "As built" paragraph saying
so.

**What was built.**
- **Android:** `ScreenPrivacy`, in prefs, off by default, adds or clears
  `FLAG_SECURE` on the window in `onCreate` (before the first frame) and on
  toggle. Settings → Privacy: "Block screenshots and screen recording",
  "…Leave this off to screenshot a balance for your group."
- **iOS:** `CaptureWatch` follows `UIScreen.capturedDidChangeNotification`,
  and `isCaptured` on the scene's screen. With "Hide during screen recording"
  on, the D-163 cover hides the ledger while captured. The copy says:
  "iPhone does not let apps block screenshots."
- **Clipboard:** the invite link, a secret for 7 days, is the only thing
  either app copies.
  - iOS: `Clipboard.copySecret` uses `.localOnly` and
    `.expirationDate = now + 120 s`. The test proves an expired item is gone.
  - Android: `ClipDescription` extra `android.content.extra.IS_SENSITIVE`.
- **Root and jailbreak:** `DeviceIntegrity` checks known signs and nothing
  else. Android: a `test-keys` build, and su or Magisk paths. iOS:
  Cydia/Sileo/Zebra, `/var/jb`, apt, sshd, `/bin/bash`; compiled out on the
  simulator, whose host is a Mac. A WATCH-coloured line in Settings →
  Privacy; nothing blocked, logged or sent.

**Seen.**
- **Android emulator:**
  - Settings → Privacy with the switch off and the rooted warning (the
    `skipti-shots` image reports `test-keys`, a true positive).

both apps offered only the nine promoted codes. No founder fork: a default
that follows the phone's region, changeable in Settings, is the obvious one.

**What was built.**
- **Core:** `money::all_codes()` and `ffi_currency_codes()`, the codes
  `Currency::parse` accepts, sorted. 164, counted independently in Python
  from `ZERO_DECIMAL`, `THREE_DECIMAL` and `TWO_DECIMAL`.
- **Default currency** (`DefaultCurrency`, both apps): stored on this phone
  only (iOS `UserDefaults` `money.default-currency`, Android prefs
  `skipti-money`/`default-currency`). A stored code core does not know is
  ignored; unset, the region's currency if core knows it, else USD. It
  pre-selects New group and a fresh Add form (a loaded group's currency
  still replaces it on Add).
- **Pickers:** the nine in SPEC's order, then the default and the current
  choice once each, then "All currencies": COMMON, then ALL CURRENCIES,
  searchable by code or the phone's name for the code, ignoring case and
  accents. Names are presentation, from the platform
  (`Locale.localizedString(forCurrencyCode:)`,
  `java.util.Currency.getDisplayName`); the codes come from core.
- **Settings → Currency** on both apps, above App lock.

are unchanged; the relay did not change: **no deploy is needed.**

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** WORKLOG's loose ends named "import UI". SPEC §9.5: "Importers are
how you win users from a competitor, so build them first". The engine
(D-69 to D-74) and a review screen existed; nothing a person could tap led to
them, and Balance's empty state promised an import it could not start.

**What was built.** See the D-row. In short: Import from Balance (no group
yet) and Settings → Your data; source, file, new group (name, currency,
people, which one is you), review, apply; nothing saved before apply; the
group and the expenses written after core accepts the merge, the expenses as
sync records in one vault session. No new FFI, no new dependency.

**The Splitwise sign convention, corrected.** D-69 pinned "positive owes,
negative paid". Splitwise's help page ("How can I double check my
balances?", read 2026-09-25): "When they pay for an expense or make a
payment, the number is positive. When they borrow money for an expense or
receive a payment, the number is negative." kennethxu/splitwise2spliit's
README agrees (a single positive value is the payer). Seen first on the
simulator: a hand-written three-person sheet in Splitwise's convention had
three of its four rows refused as "2 payers". Core now takes the one positive
cell as the payer and the negative cells as the others' shares. Every
fixture row's member cells were negated by a script
(`.drafts/d166/flip_fixtures.py`: 24 rows in `splitwise.rs`, 5 in
`ledger_port.rs`, 4 each in `ImportReviewTests.swift`, `ImportProofScreen.swift`
and `ImportReview.kt`, 5 in `LedgerPortTests.swift`; every changed line was
read), so each old test keeps its meaning and all of them pass unchanged. The
new golden is worked by hand from Splitwise's sentence: Bob pays a 90.00
cabin for three, his cell +60.00, the others -30.00; payer Bob, 9000 minor
units, 3000 each.

**Found while looking, and fixed.**
1. The review's include switches took no taps on iOS 27 (a `Toggle` in a row
   whose children were hidden from accessibility) and did not redraw on
   Android (a plain field). The whole row is now the switch, with a check
   circle (iOS) or checkbox (Android), and VoiceOver/TalkBack read
   "Included" or "Left out".
2. Refusals printed participant ids ("2 payers recorded (d7fc…, d662…)"):
   the review now names people.
3. A row dated 20 Sep showed as Sep 19 in the US: the importers read dates as
   UTC wall times and iOS showed them in local time. The review shows the
   file's date (Android already did); saved expenses keep the file's wall
   time in the phone's zone, date-only rows at local noon, so the UTC day
   (the duplicate key) is unchanged from UTC−12 to UTC+12.
4. Group names from file names kept the export's date and "export":
   numbers and "export" are dropped and the first letter capitalised.
5. "Import 1 expenses"; system section headers in the review.
6. The per-group empty lines on Balance and Expenses said "or import from
   another app", but an import always makes a new group: they now say "Add
   your first expense."
7. `make android-core` is needed after a core change: an APK built with
   `assemblePlayDebug` alone still read the old signs (CLAUDE.md §7.2).

**Seen.**
- **iOS 27 simulator**, a three-person sheet placed in Files (On My iPhone):
  Balance's Import button; the source choice; the file read (3 people);
  "Tahoe trip", USD; Tim chosen; the review with four expenses on the right
  dates, the second Groceries flagged, the two-payer row refused naming
  "Tim, Asha", the summary row listed; the duplicate left out; "3 expenses
  added to Tahoe trip."; Show the group: $35.00 owed, Asha +15, Rahul +20
  (worked by hand: Tim paid 90 split three ways, Asha paid 45, Rahul paid
  30); Expenses lists each payer and date. The file was removed after.
- **Android emulator**, the same sheet in Downloads: Settings → Import; the

  which also shows the saved dates kept their day. Emulator closed after.

**Sabotage 9/9 over two runs (run 1: 5/9)**, expected red sets fixed before the run. C1 is a

**Run 1 scored 5/9, and the four misses were real findings about the tests.**
I1/A1 (plan the file without the unsaved group) stayed green because core's
merge check tests only a group id's shape, not that the group exists or that
the payer belongs to it (§4). I4/A4 (write no sync records for imported
expenses) stayed green because the test counted ALL records, and saving the
group and your name write records of their own, while a rebuild's one-time
legacy backfill re-mints records for kv-only expenses. Both tests were
strengthened: the plan's ledger must contain the new group, and exactly two
records of the expense type must exist before any rebuild. Run 2 of those
four rows: 4/4, the tree byte-identical after each run.

  and delete the file." / "The PDF could not be made."

No core, bindings or relay change: **no deploy is needed.**

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**The decision.** Asked with three options (one account per phone; move the
ledger into the new account; one ledger per account), the founder chose **one
account per phone**, the recommendation. SPEC §4.3 gains the rule.

**What was built** (both apps; see the D-row).
- `AccountOwner`: the pure rule (`owns`: no owner yet, or the same subject),
  and the vault key `account/owner`.
- `LedgerSync.signIn` → `signedIn` / `otherAccount` / `failed`, the owner
  checked before the session is stored; `restoreSession` records the owner of
  a phone signed in before this unit. Android adds `admits(session)` so the
  sign-in route decides before starting the push it used to start at once.
- A refused sign-in: iOS shows the notice on the sign-in screen itself;
  Android goes to its own screen with the same words and actions. Both end
  the refused session on the relay (`AccountSignOut.endSession`).
- `LedgerErase.erase(vaultPath, keystore)`: the vault's files, then the key;
  the app's erase first forgets the session and ends it on the relay, then
  goes back to setup (iOS: a notification the app scene handles; Android: a
  counter AppRoot watches).
- Settings → Your data → "Erase this phone", after the Recovery Kit on both.
- Proof surface `--other-account-proof` on both (not a user flow).

**Seen.**
- **iOS 27 simulator**, local relay: `--other-account-proof` showed the notice
  with Export and Erase. Its first run left the phone owned by a dev
  account; the rerun's fresh "owner" mint was refused too, which is the rule
  holding through sign-out (the proof now keeps an existing owner). Settings
  → Erase → the confirmation → Erase → setup with new words; a new vault file
  was created by setup.
- **Android emulator**, the same proof: the same notice. Settings → Erase →
  the confirmation → Erase → setup with new words. Emulator closed after.
- Screenshots: `ios/artifacts/d168-*` (2), `android/artifacts/d168-*` (2). The
  iOS erase confirmation was captured before the card moved below the Recovery
  Kit; Android's shows the final order. No screenshot of setup's words is
  committed.

**Sabotage 8/8** on the first run, expected red sets fixed before the run.

| Row | Sabotage | Red |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | another account is let in | `AccountOwnerTests.testAPhoneSignedInBeforeOwnersBelongsToItsAccount`, `AccountOwnerTests.testAnotherAccountIsRefusedAndNothingIsKept` only |
| I2 | a phone signed in before owners gets none | `AccountOwnerTests.testAPhoneSignedInBeforeOwnersBelongsToItsAccount` only |
| I3 | the erase keeps the key | `AccountOwnerTests.testTheEraseTakesTheFilesAndTheKeyAndLeavesAFreshLedger` only |
| I4 | the first sign-in records no owner | `AccountOwnerTests.testAnotherAccountIsRefusedAndNothingIsKept` only |
| A1 | another account is let in | `AccountOwnerTest.a_phone_signed_in_before_owners_belongs_to_its_account`, `AccountOwnerTest.another_account_is_refused_and_nothing_is_kept` only |
| A2 | a phone signed in before owners gets none | `AccountOwnerTest.a_phone_signed_in_before_owners_belongs_to_its_account` only |
| A3 | the erase keeps the key | `AccountOwnerTest.the_erase_takes_the_files_and_the_key_and_leaves_a_fresh_ledger` only |
| A4 | the first sign-in records no owner | `AccountOwnerTest.another_account_is_refused_and_nothing_is_kept` only |

**Found.** Asked whether the server was up to date, Claude checked from
outside (live `/version` `4cf79fd`; nothing under `server/` or in

`lykill::random_bytes`, unchanged; AASA, assetlinks and `/join` served and

relay healthy and **no backup timer, no `/var/backups/skipti`**: no backup
had ever been taken in production, and no restore drill had run since the
D-156 schema migration, which §10.4 requires.

**The failure, and its cause.** Installing the timer and starting the first
backup failed before the backup folder existed. Both scripts began
`#!/bin/sh` and set `-o pipefail`. Here:

```

exit 2        (no backup folder created)
```

**The fix, run here.** Both scripts now start `#!/bin/bash`, with a comment
saying why. Against the local relay's vault: `skipti-backup: ok … (2347008
bytes …)`, then the drill: 4/4, `REPORT: BACKUP RESTORABLE`, the restored
relay answering `/version`.

**In production** (the founder, 2026-09-25 23:48–23:49 UTC):

No core, bindings or relay change: **no deploy is needed.** Three gate runs:
the first was stopped during clippy to add the new G mark to NOTICE and the
Licences entry; the second **failed 2 legs (18 passed)**: renaming the entry
to "Sign in with Google button and G" broke the test on each shell that pins
that name (`AboutTests` iOS, `AboutTest` Android), which were updated; the
third, above, is the tree committed here. The first two ran with macOS
scanning every build again (clippy 603 s): Claude Code had updated to
2.1.281, a new inner-app path outside the founder's Developer Tools exemption
(CLAUDE.md §13); the founder was asked to add it.

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Where this came from.** The founder installed the TestFlight and Play
internal builds on his own phones on 2026-09-26 and listed what was wrong,
before the web build. This unit is the concrete bugs; the redesign he asked
for (research-led, friendlier, five tabs with a raised +, a Groups tab, an
all-groups Balance) follows as its own units, from a proposal first.

**The decision.** Join a group was hidden without an account (D-159). Asked,
the founder chose to show it always, the recommendation: without an account,
the join screen says why joining needs one, in answer to that tap only
(GUARANTEES #5), with a secondary Sign in that comes back to it.

**Root causes** (each found before its fix):
- **Dark phone, light app (iOS).** `window.traitOverrides.userInterfaceStyle
  = .unspecified` is an override, and the window resolved it as light. System
  now removes the override. Reproduced first: the simulator in dark mode drew
  the app light; after the fix, dark.
- **The Sign in screen stayed open (iOS).** `SignInScreen` returned the
  outcome to Settings and did nothing on success. It now becomes a
  confirmation; Done returns.
- **Settings opened before the session existed (Android).** The route
  launched `signIn` in the background and changed route at once. It now waits
  for the save; the key bootstrap, which is network, runs after it in the
  background (`signIn(bootstrapNow = false)`, `bootstrap()`).
- **Add kept the last expense (iOS).** A tab root keeps its `@State` across
  tab switches, and nothing reset the form after a save. A save now gives the
  form a new identity; a half-filled form is still kept.
- **No way to remove a person (both).** The rows were a list of strings with
  no remove control. `PeopleDraft` gives each row an id; removing one takes
  exactly its name.
- **Google's sheet closed with no word (Android).** Credential Manager returns
  the same `GetCredentialCancellationException` for a dismissed sheet and for
  a sign-in Google refused after an account was picked; the app treated both
  as silence. Google's refusal itself is configuration (the Android OAuth
  client's package and app-signing SHA-1, the consent screen's test users),
  which is the founder's to check; the app now says the sheet closed and logs
  Google's reason.

**Seen.**
- **iOS 27 simulator** (dark, then light): before/after dark mode; the empty
  state with Create, Join and Import; Join without an account; the
  `--signed-in-proof` confirmation for Google (dark) and Apple (light) against
  the local relay, then Settings showing the G and "Signed in with Google";
  New group with two rows, one removed; Add empty again after a save.
- **Android emulator** (dark): the confirmation and Settings for Google; the
  empty state; Join without an account, Sign in, Back to Join; New group's
  rows with ×, the first removed.
- Screenshots: `ios/artifacts/d172-*` (10), `android/artifacts/d172-*` (6).

**Found while looking, not fixed here.**
- **The email code can never arrive.** The relay generates the code and sends
  no email (D-149 (c) recorded "no email"); the apps still offer "Send a code".
  For the founder: hide the email path until a sender exists, or add one.
- **iOS onboarding's three-word check** rejected the right words on the first
  Confirm and accepted them on the second, in 3 of 3 simulator runs typed by
  the simulator tool; the keyboard's suggestions were stale, which points at
  the tool's text injection. Not reproduced by hand or on a device; asked.
- The group list says "1 people".

**Sabotage 10/10** on the first run, expected red sets fixed before the
run, the tree byte-identical after (diff and status hashes compared).

No core, bindings or relay change: **no deploy is needed.**

**The first gate failed one leg (19 passed): the licence inventory.** Cargo's
automatic cache clean-up had deleted the unpacked sources of the `spdx` crate
(`~/.cargo/registry/src`), keeping its downloaded archives (`registry/cache`);
`scripts/licences.py` reads the SIL Open Font License text from those sources
and stopped with "not found". It now falls back to reading the same file out
of the newest cached `.crate` archive (read with Python's `tarfile`, never
unpacked or built); the regenerated inventory is byte-identical to the
committed one, which is what the leg compares. **The second gate failed the same leg for a
second cache:** Gradle's periodic clean-up had deleted the cached POM of
`androidx.activity:activity:1.13.0` (its folder changed mid-gate) while
keeping the metadata Gradle resolves from, so no build fetches it again.
Re-fetched with `./gradlew :app:dependencies --configuration
{play,direct}ReleaseRuntimeClasspath --refresh-dependencies` (the same locked
versions from Google's Maven; nothing added); the script's error now says
how, and CLAUDE.md §7 records both caches and the Claude Code update that
moved builds outside the Developer Tools exemption. The gate above is the
third run. All three ran with macOS scanning every build (cargo test 957 s in
the first): the founder has not yet added Claude Code 2.1.281.

**CI was not run, by instruction** (Actions budget).

**Why.** `auth_otp_request` on the relay issues and hashes a code and sends
it nowhere: there is no email sender (D-149 (c)). The apps offered "Send code"
to every user. The founder chose to hide it (and the passkey, which only joins
a session the code proved, D-102) until a sender exists.

  font; they use the app's `label` role now.

  new SHA-1s, while installed copies of 0.1.0 carry the previous key.

No core, bindings or relay change: **no deploy is needed.** CI was not run,

**iOS: why the kit step moved.** The founder, asked, said the words and
buttons moved, not only the glow. The glow's drift was the only animation in
the app that never ends, and it was started as a `withAnimation(.repeatForever)`
transaction in `onAppear`; that transaction animates whatever layout changes
in the same update. The kit step appears as the sign-in form's navigation
title goes away, so the page's position was caught and looped. The drift is
now an `.animation(_:value:)` on the blooms alone. **Not reproduced on the
simulator** (iOS 27 and 26.5; the standalone kit, `--signed-in-proof google`
on a local dev relay, and a temporary hook on the real Settings → Sign in
path inside the tab bar, with and without a sheet closing): the page held
still in every frame there. The fix is proven by mechanism and awaits the
founder's iPhone on 0.2.1. (Corrected D-179: the fix was incomplete. It moved the repeat onto
`.animation(_:value:)` over the backdrop's whole `ZStack`, which still animates the blooms' size and place when they
change in the same update as the drift; the new Groups tab showed its glow growing from a corner and swinging.
D-179 lays size and place out unanimated and repeats only the drift offset, inside `animation(_:body:)`. 0.2.1 was
never shipped; 0.3.0 carries both.)

**Android: Google's refusal, traced on the LG** (USB, the founder's
permission, 2026-09-29):
- Android 12 (API 31); SKIPTI 0.2.0 (2000) installed by Play; one signer, no
  past signatures; `apksigner` on the pulled `base.apk` (v3 only) gives the
  SHA-1 the founder registered and the About screen shows.
- The app asks for the Web client `403030719865-7bic…`, package
  `com.vardrlabs.skipti` (read from the tree).
- Play services, all three attempts: `[GetTokenResponseHandler] Server
  returned error: This android application is not registered to use
  OAuth2.0, please confirm the package name and SHA-1 certificate
  fingerprint match what you registered in Google Developer Console`,
  `status=UNREGISTERED_ON_API_CONSOLE`, surfaced to the app as
  `TYPE_USER_CANCELED: [16] Account reauth failed.`
- So Google's project `403030719865` has no Android client for that package
  and SHA-1. The founder's registration is elsewhere or differs; the fix is
  in the console.

**Seen.**
- iOS 27 simulator, dark: the kit step with the glow drifting (sampled
  colour changes frame to frame) and the primary button's rows fixed across
  six frames (`ios/artifacts/d177-kit-still.png`).
- Android emulator (skipti-shots, no Google account): "No Google account is
  available on this device. / Google's reason: No credentials available on
  this device." (`android/artifacts/d177-google-reason.png`). The emulator
  first wedged (ANR dialogs naming a dead process's window) and was
  cold-booted; not an app fault.

**Relay changed: the founder deploys it** with the 0.3.0 release (`deploy/ship-relay.sh`). CI was not run, by
instruction (Actions budget).

**Why the Android phone saw nothing.**
- Apple, Google and the email code sign in with `sync_device_id: null` (GoogleSignIn.kt, GoogleSignIn.swift,
  AppleSignIn.swift), on purpose: D-168's check that the phone is not already another account's runs before anything
  is bound to it. The relay's session therefore had no device, and `agreement_key_put` answers 401 without one;
  `DeviceKeyService.bootstrap` swallowed that. Each phone went on syncing under the random `sync/secret` it made at
  sign-in, so each saw only its own records, and D-123/D-124's key sharing could never start.
- **The live test found the second cause.** `GroupSyncTest.a_second_phone_on_the_same_account_gets_its_groups_and_expenses`
  against `skipti-server` on localhost (dev session mint) still failed with "skipped 5 log entries": the relay
  answered **415** to every PUT, because `HttpUrlConnectionTransport` and `URLSessionRelayTransport` wrote the body
  and `content-type: application/json` for POST only. Every agreement-key publish since D-123 was refused in
  production; the in-test relays never read headers. Both transports now send them for every method but GET, and a
  wire test on each (a JDK `HttpServer`; a `URLProtocol`) reads the bytes.
- A pull stopped at the first entry it could not open, so one entry sealed under a phone's old key blocked every later
  one. Once a phone holds the account key it now skips such entries and counts them; a phone never authorised still
  fails closed (D-123's test is unchanged).

**The founder's decisions (2026-09-29, AskUserQuestion):** new phones get the data automatically by default; a notice
on the phone that shared ("Yes, a notice"); Maximum security, off by default, restores the six-word approval; sync
"every few seconds" (10 s in front) and pull to sync. He accepted amending GUARANTEES #7 for phones with Maximum
security off: ADR-0039, GUARANTEES #7 and its Amendments entry, THREAT_MODEL "a new phone joins automatically",
SPEC §3.5 "As amended".

**Seen** (local relay with the dev mint; `--join-account-proof <name>` on both shells signs in to one test account):

  (`android/artifacts/d178-waiting.png`), then the iPhone's group in its Balance (`d178-joined-group-arrived.png`).
- iOS 27 simulator: "Your data was shared with a new phone" with the SAME six words (`ios/artifacts/d178-shared-notice.png`);
  the group "Weekend" made on Android appeared on the iPhone with no tap (`d178-group-from-android.png`); Settings →
  Privacy & security → Maximum security (`d178-maximum-security.png`).
- iOS 26.5 simulator as a third phone: with Maximum security on, the iPhone asked with the third phone's words.
- **Found by looking:** the switch was per phone, so the Android phone (off) shared with the third phone while the
  iPhone (on) asked; it is now the account's record. The third phone also announced the two phones already there as
  new; the key envelope now carries the giver's list of phones it shares with.
- Found by sabotage run 1: the new 10 s poller ran inside the XCTest host and an erase test failed with "disk I/O
  error"; the poller does not start under XCTest.

tab on the iOS 27 simulator showed the Aurora glow filling only a corner and moving: three frames two seconds apart
showed it shrinking toward the top left. D-177 moved the repeating animation from `withAnimation` to

update as `drift`, and a tab's first layout (the blooms' frames going from zero to full size) is exactly such a change.
Balance happened to lay out before its drift started, which is why D-177's looks were still. Now each bloom's size and
base position are laid out with no animation, and only the drift offset repeats, inside iOS 17's `animation(_:body:)`.
After the fix, three frames of the Groups tab show the glow filling the page. The founder's Recovery Kit step (D-177)
may have been this same path; 0.3.0 carries the fix.

**Core's sums, re-derived.** `.drafts/d180/golden.py` works the overview (Goa: you +650.00; Flat: −45.00; INR total
+605.00; EUR −32.00; Meera +355.00 across two groups) and the stats (INR 2,033.00 spent; food 5903, stay 3443, none
654 basis points after the largest remainder) independently of the Rust. On the seeded proof the screen's numbers
were checked by hand again: Goa +7,400.00 (9,000 − 1,200 − 400), Flat 4B +1,350.00, ₹8,750.00 in all; Meera
₹3,050.00 = (3,000 − 400) + (900 − 450); Goa's spend ₹18,400.00, your share ₹4,600.00, Stay 65% / Food 26% / Travel 9%.

**Found by looking.**
- **iOS: the last rows could not scroll above the new bar.** D-179 placed the bar as a `safeAreaInset` of the
  `TabView`; with the system bar hidden, that inset never reached a tab's scroll views. Replacing the `TabView` with a
  `ZStack` of the four stacks changed nothing, and neither did `safeAreaPadding` on each `NavigationStack`; a
  temporary `safeAreaPadding` on Balance's own scroll view did. So each tab's ROOT keeps the room itself, a page
  pushed on a tab hides the bar (iOS's own pattern for detail pages; their bottom buttons can never sit under it), and
  a group's page keeps it, as the canvas draws it (`ShellChrome`).
- Android's stat boxes clipped "₹18,400.0" and "You'll get"; labels now wrap and long amounts step down a size.
- The hero's chips: white on an 18% white film measured 4.35:1 over the gradient's rose stop
  (`.drafts/d180/chips.py`); 12% gives 4.9:1 over every stop, and a test on each shell measures it.
- D-179's Android seam: the new Balance draws on the shell's glow only.

**The founder, during the unit (2026-09-29):** "move the group tab to the place of expenses" (done: Balance ·
Expenses · + · Groups · Settle up); "give an option to edit the expenses from the groups section" (done: a group's
recent expenses come from core's projection and open the expense, with Edit and Delete, on both shells); "group the
expenses in groups" and a two-step category picker: D-181.

(`ios/artifacts/d180-balance-{dark,light}.png`, `android/artifacts/d180-balance-dark.png`), scrolled clear of the bar

**What each row says.** "you owe ₹400.00" on Scooters (Meera paid ₹1,600.00 for four: your share 400.00); "you lent
₹9,000.00" on the villa (you paid 12,000.00, your share 3,000.00); "not involved" when your share is nothing and you did
not pay. Core computes it (`ffi_your_effect`: what you paid less your share, in the currency the expense counts in, a
converted one included); the shells only format it.

**Found while building.**

  re-indenting; both were fixed before the first build (a compile error, never a runtime state).

  date); it is one line of text now and wraps as a sentence.
- The emulator's first run failed with "undefined symbol uniffi_skipti_core_fn_func_ffi_your_effect":
  `assemblePlayDebug` alone had packaged the previous core library (CLAUDE.md §7); `make android-core` fixed it.

**The keyboard, root cause read off the device.** `dumpsys window` on the skipti-shots emulator (API 34):
`sim={adjust=pan}` for MainActivity. Typing into the New group form moved the first person row from y = 1043 to
1092 px on the first key. After the fix the same dump reads `sim={adjust=resize}`, and the row stayed at 1043 px
through six keystrokes (`android/artifacts/d184-keyboard-api34.png`: the field sits above the keyboard). On the API 37
emulator (Pixel_10_Pro_XL), before: the account glyph over the battery icon and the tab bar over the gesture handle
(`d184-bars-before-api37.png`); after: both clear (`d184-bars-after-api37.png`); dark mode draws light bar icons
(`d184-dark-bars.png`).

**The split goldens, worked by hand** in `.drafts/d184/golden.py` (en-IN grouping, independent of core): the
tester's 500 + 4,500 + 10,000 + 10,000 = 25,000 rupees of 30,000 → "₹25,000.00 of ₹30,000.00. ₹5,000.00 is still to
assign."; 35,000 → "₹35,000.00, ₹5,000.00 more than the ₹30,000.00 spent."; items 4,000 of 6,400 → "₹2,400.00 is
still to assign."; basis points 9000, 9050, 9005, 12345, 0 → 90%, 90.5%, 90.05%, 123.45%, 0%. The Android test runs
the tester's exact numbers through `AddExpenseUi.buildExpense` and the real core; the iOS twin through
`ffiSplitCompute`. Core accepts a zero exact entry and refuses on the sum, which is what lets the live line count an
empty field as nothing (both shells' tests show ₹15,000.00 of ₹30,000.00 with one field empty).

**Seen**: Android emulator, Paris (EUR 100, Exact): "The amounts add up to €30.00 of €100.00. €70.00 is still to
assign." (`android/artifacts/d184-live-line.png`), then "…€110.00, €10.00 more than the €100.00 spent."
(`d184-too-much.png`), then with 30 + 70 the line gave way to "You’ll get back €30.00". iOS 27 simulator: the line
with both fields empty (`ios/artifacts/d184-live-line.png`). The erase on both phones: the question first (it was
always there), then the new notice (`android/artifacts/d184-erased.png`, `ios/artifacts/d184-erased.png`).

**Found by looking**, fixed before the gate: (a) the live line never showed while any amount was still empty, since
an empty field fails to parse before core compares sums (now counted as nothing for the line only); (b) on iOS the
erase left Settings open over an erased ledger, so nothing visibly changed; the root now takes a new identity after
an erase.

CI was not run, by instruction (Actions budget). **No relay change**: the name is an ordinary sealed record.

**The root causes, read in the code.** `DeviceApprovalScreen` (both shells) set `isAuthorised` from
`listOwnEnvelopes`, a `GET v1/envelopes/{subject}`; the relay's `envelope_list` returns, for a session with a device,
ONLY rows whose recipient is that device (ADR-0022). No other phone's row can come back, so no other phone could
read as approved; this phone's own row is addressed to it only when it received the key, never when it founded or
gave it. The same screen called `restoreSession()` and never `freshSession()`; `ACCESS_TTL` is 15 minutes; on a 401
`listAgreementKeys` returns an empty list, so a list opened after the token expired showed no other phone.

**Seen** (local relay with the dev mint, `--join-account-proof family5 --relay-local` on the iOS 27 simulator, then
the skipti-shots emulator): Android "Your phones": this phone "Android SDK built for arm64" (the emulator's own
Device name), its words and the new note; "iPhone 17", "Has your data" (`android/artifacts/d185-android-phones.png`).
iPhone: "iPhone 17 · This phone · Has your data" and the Android installs by name (`ios/artifacts/d185-ios-phones.png`).
With Maximum security turned on from the Android and the Android reinstalled as a new phone, it waited with "tuition
obtain gown tired banana scorpion"; the iPhone asked with the same six words (`d185-ios-asks.png`); after "They match,
share" the new phone read "Has your data", first as "A phone", then by name once it had synced
(`d185-ios-shared-named.png`). The emulator's earlier installs stay listed: removing a phone is SPEC §12's revoke,
still owed (§4).

**The founder's second ask, mid-unit.** The first build showed a photo as the 48-point tile; the founder asked for
the whole card to be the photo, with words that do not blend in. The words are white on a black gradient that is
25% at the top, 55% from 56 points down, and 72% at the bottom. White over 55% black on a pure white photo, the
brightest a photo can be, is 4.759:1 (WCAG); over 25%, 1.834:1, which is why only the "Showing" chip sits in the top
band, on its own 55% capsule. A photo is kept at 768×512 (3:2) rather than a 256 square so it covers a card sharply,
and `PICTURE_MAX_BYTES` went from 40,000 to 64,000 before anything shipped.

**Measured, and why a photo steps down.** The simulator's own photos at 768×512, JPEG quality 40 (sips): 42–68 KB
for five, 90 KB for the field of flowers (`IMG_0006`); at 640 wide, 66 KB; at 512, 46 KB. The first build refused
the flowers ("That photo could not be made small enough"); a photo now steps down through 768, 640, 512 and 384 wide
before it is refused, and a pinned-noise image (the busiest there is) proves it on iOS.

**Seen**: iOS 27 simulator (`--groups-proof`): the chooser (`ios/artifacts/d187-ios-chooser.png`); 🏖️ on Goa trip's
page; the flowers across the top of the page (`d187-ios-page-photo.png`) and filling the Groups card
(`d187-ios-groups-photo.png`); the New group row with ⛰️; dark mode. Android emulator (API 34, `-gpu host`): the
chooser (`android/artifacts/d187-android-chooser.png`), the system photo picker with no permission asked, the page
(`d187-android-page-photo.png`), the Groups card in light and dark (`d187-android-groups-photo.png`,
`d187-android-groups-dark.png`).

**Found by looking**, fixed before the gate: (1) on iOS the photo band took no taps: its backdrop was marked not
hit-testable inside the button, so the button had nothing to hit; the backdrop now keeps its taps to its own frame.
(2) On Android the card's second line was clipped: a weighted column inside a scrolling list; the card is now a
column that puts the chip at the top and the words at the bottom. (3) Choosing a large photo took about five seconds
with no sign of life; "Choose a photo" shows a spinner meanwhile.

**Google's rules, read on 2026-09-30** (developers.google.com/identity/branding-guidelines): the button may be scaled
for different screens with its aspect kept; a custom button must use Google Sans Medium, the standard "G" on white,
and Google's fill and stroke colours. SKIPTI carries no Google Sans and adding a font is a dependency, so the page uses
Google's own pill artwork from the bundle approved in D-138 (`Shape=Pill`, light and dark, unmodified), shown larger.
The art's natural sizes are 188 × 44 pt (iOS) and 180 × 40 dp (Android); shown at 231 × 54 pt and 234 × 52 dp, each
screen scale takes the next-larger file (iOS @2x/@3x/@4x into the 1x/2x/3x slots; Android @2x/@3x/@4x/@4x into
mdpi/xhdpi/xxhdpi/xxxhdpi), so no scale is drawn from fewer pixels than it shows, except xxxhdpi screens (936 px
from 720). Apple's `ASAuthorizationAppleIDButton` takes any size and corner radius (HIG); it is the same size, with
radius 27, so the two read as a pair.

**Seen**: iOS 27 simulator, light and dark, before and after the founder's note (`ios/artifacts/d188-ios-signin.png`,
`d188-ios-signin-dark.png`); Android `play` on API 34, and on API 37 (edge to edge) in light with the pill (`android/artifacts/d188-android-signin-37.png`)
and in dark before the founder's note, with the old square button (`d188-android-signin-37-dark.png`); Android `direct`, which has no way to sign in: the hero and "Signing in is not
available in this version of SKIPTI yet." (`d188-android-direct.png`).

deletion is recorded, else the addition), listed only when someone other than you made it. The test's eight
expenses were worked by hand: an edit by Rahul of your expense is listed as changed; your edit of Rahul's is not
listed at all (you made the latest change); a deletion by Priya is listed; a personal expense and one added under
your old "you" id are not; a blank note reads "an expense".

**Lucide `bell`**, read from upstream main on 2026-09-30 (`icons/bell.svg`): two paths, verbatim. Lucide's LICENSE,
read the same day, does not list `bell` among the icons derived from Feather: ISC only. Its outline uses cubic
curves, which the iOS parser did not read (it refused them, by design, rather than draw part of a glyph); `C` and `c`
are added, and the outline's bounds (x 3.001 to 21, y 2 to 17) come from `.drafts/d189/bell_bounds.py`, which samples
the path independently of the parser.

**"Every few seconds", answered.** While SKIPTI is open it already syncs every 10 seconds (D-178). Neither phone lets
an app run every few seconds in the background: Android runs a periodic job at most every 15 minutes, when it
chooses; iOS runs a background refresh when it judges the app is used, which can be hours. The setting says so in
those words.

**Seen, Android** (API 34 emulator, `-gpu host`, the play build with `--groups-proof`'s ledger): the job scheduled
("waiting"); run by hand (`cmd jobscheduler run -f`), it posted "New activity in Goa trip", "… in Flat 4B", "… in
Paris" under the bell icon (`android/artifacts/d190-android-notifications.png`); run again, it posted nothing.
**Found by looking:** the first build crashed when the app opened: a job with a network constraint needs
ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, which SKIPTI does not ask for. The constraint is dropped (offline, the sync fails quietly and
nothing new is said) and scheduling is wrapped so it can never stop the app opening.

**Seen, iOS** (iOS 27 simulator, signed in against a local dev relay): Settings → Notifications, off
(`ios/artifacts/d190-ios-setting.png`); switched on, iOS asked (`d190-ios-ask.png`); "Don't Allow" left it off with
"Notifications are off for SKIPTI in your phone's settings." (`d190-ios-denied.png`). `--notify-proof` (a new proof
surface): permission granted, the first check posted three (`d190-ios-proof.png`; the system logged each
"NotificationRequest: Completed"), the second posted none. **Not seen on iOS:** a notification on screen. iOS keeps
no notification an app posts while it is in front, and a proof waiting for the app to leave was suspended with it;
starting the real background task through the simulator's debug hook (`_simulateLaunchForTaskWithIdentifier` in
lldb) hung on attaching. iOS's background launch is unproven here (§4).

byte-identical:

below removed the fix: 1 crash in 3 launches; with it, 0 in 8. The race predates this unit, so the 0.3.1 Android
build carries it.

phone. Your ledger stays here.", its Settings read "No account", its two groups stayed; the iPhone's row read "Signed

2026-10-19T20:46:08Z and `deletionRequestedAt`, both phones `signedOut` with `signedOutAt` and no `fcmToken`. That
first pass found findings (1)–(4); after the fixes, from the start again: signing in remade both phones' entries
without the flag; Settings showed "Your account will be deleted on October 19, 2026." with Keep my account (iPhone and
Android), and Keep cleared `deleteAt` and `deletionRequestedAt` on each; Sign out everywhere on the iPhone signed it
out without a notice while the Android showed the notice; Delete on the iPhone with the Android's Settings open gave one
alert on the iPhone (the screen closed) and the notice on the Android, whose Settings dropped to "No account" with no

**Root cause, read live (gcloud, read-only, then the founder's yes for the field-names-only Firestore read):**
`get-ancestors-iam-policy` shows `skipti-functions` held `datastore.user`, `eventarc.eventReceiver`,
`firebaseauth.admin`, `firebasenotifications.admin`, `run.invoker` and nothing at organization level;
`gcloud iam roles describe` shows `firebasenotifications.admin` = `firebasenotifications.messages.*` only, while
`firebasecloudmessaging.admin` holds `cloudmessaging.messages.create`. Firestore's shape: the shared group had two
members, its expense records carried `notice`, and both members' phones held 142-character `fcmToken`s: every step
before the send held. The FCM APIs were enabled (the 2026-10-12 disable was Remote Config x2 and App Distribution).

**Live after the IAM swap and the deploy (16:59Z):** `onGroupRecord: push` {phones 1, delivered 1, failed 0} at
17:06:58Z and 17:08:38Z (account lKEToh to the other member's Android), {phones 2, delivered 2, failed 0} at
17:14:41Z (to lKEToh's iPhone (TestFlight, production APNs) and Android); the founder saw both. The emulator check
signed in as a new account (okjPwA, one phone), so `onDeviceCreated` correctly had no other phone to tell.

**Sabotage 2/2** (`node --test firebase/tests/push.test.mjs`; `push.js` restored from `.drafts/d204/push.js.bak`, `cmp`
identical each time):

| S2 | any string accepted as an error code (the `messaging/…` shape check removed) | `the outcome counts each send and names each failure, never a token` only |

Task 4 the Android renderers, Task 5 the iOS heroes, the ground tokens and the moving-art floors, Task 6 the Android
twins, Task 7 the controller's: an Opus whole-branch review, fix waves, performance and look, sabotage, the gate, the
records. A fresh Sonnet implementer and Sonnet reviewer per task; every task reviewed clean (Task 1 took one fix for
the founder's Aurora hero decision, made mid-task). **Whole-branch review** (Opus, `final-review.md`): With fixes, 0
Critical, 3 Important (F1 iOS bar items over the Aurora light art, F2 the stacked floor into the gate, F3 Android above
30 fps on 100 and 165 Hz), 11 Minor (F4 to F14), and the 33 Minors the tasks logged (N1 to N33) triaged into Must fix,

(`fix-wave-rereview.md`: 0 Critical, 1 Important, R1 the iOS 17 to 25 back button, 6 Minor). **Fix wave 2** (eb8af6d,
