**The founder's decisions** (all 2026-10-15; popups over the demo `.drafts/d214/curtains-demo.html`, and two more during
the review): (1) Aurora pages hold text 7:1 and labels 4.5:1 over the art; faint and accent text sitting on the Aurora
page ground take `groundFaint` / `groundAccent`. (2) The Aurora hero is at full strength, 1.0 / 1.0, today's layout,
not floored: about 1.7:1 at the curtains' lowest swing accepted (the bright band lives in the hero's top third; below 37%
of its height every line keeps 7:1); a 66% text shade was rejected. (3) Strengths: dark page curtains 0.26 and stars
0.16, light page 1.00, Norse hero 1.00, Vardr Labs dark hero signs 0.54. (4) Norse page runes 0.79 (the peak silver rune
against textFaint). (5) The 8-bit rule: floors hold on 8-bit pixels, which moved only Norse page runes 0.80 to 0.79 and
Vardr Labs light hero signs 0.61 to 0.60. (6) He tests the full art on an emulator himself before 0.5.0 (his words; a

**Findings that shaped it** (reports in `.superpowers/sdd/e2m/`):
- **N27, stacked curtains** (controller, after Task 5): the floor tests measured each curtain alone and the three
  overlap where a title sits (curtains span -0.10 to 0.60, 0.30 to 1.00 and 0.55 to 1.25 of the page width, their green
  stops near y 0.02 to 0.12). The worst stack of the brightest stops read Aurora dark textDim 2.71:1 and light 3.42:1;
  that is pessimistic (no streak factor, blur, geometry or source-over), so the controller wrote `stack.py`, which holds
  every floor as drawn. Consequence: the light page must not move to a true multiply at strength 1.00 (N8, N16), and the
  stacked walk became a gate test (F2).
- **F1, the bar tint**: SwiftUI toolbar items (Cancel, Done, Save, the account glyph) take the accent over the bar band,
  where the Aurora light curtains' pink and green stops sit: 4.00:1 as rendered there (3.79 on the page at y 0.07), the
  founder's 4.5 broken, groundAccent 4.98. On iOS 27 `UINavigationBar.appearance().tintColor` and `bar.tintColor` do not
  reach SwiftUI toolbar items, and `.tint(groundAccent)` on a sheet's stack turned a card's picker grey too; a toolbar
  item takes the tint of where its `.toolbar` is declared, so `barTint()` (`tint(Tokens.groundAccent)`) sits on the item's
  control: 18 items in 11 files (Profile's Done, explicit white on its own black bar, is exempt). Measured on the look
  device: a sheet's Cancel #4D615E, a card's Category picker and Security toggle #0B7A5F. iOS 26 and later draw the back
  chevron in the label colour in its glass (measured near black, not #4D615E), so the code comment says so. R1 (iOS 17 to
  25): SwiftUI's environment tint likely overwrites a bar tint, so the back button is made deterministically through
  `UINavigationBarAppearance` copies (title colour attributes, an always-original chevron) and made again on a light and
  dark flip; proven only by code and a test on real `UINavigationBar` objects on the iOS 27 host. The `groundAccent`
  count moved 2 to 3 on purpose (the third is `barTint()`'s definition).
- **N28 and the 8-bit rule**: the Norse peak silver rune against textFaint is 4.5013 in doubles and 4.4987 on the pixel
  `(31, 32, 35)` at 0.80; at 0.79 it is 4.5028 on 8 bits. Compose colours hold 8 bits a channel, which is how Task 6 saw
  it while iOS's exact-double test read 4.5013. The floor tests on both shells now round every composite to 1/255 before the
  ratio. Vardr Labs light at 0.61 measured 4.498 against `motion.py`'s dim line, so it moved to 0.60.
- **S1, the hero dim line** (found while writing the sabotage runner): the shells measured dim text composited over the
  art (5.33 at 0.61) while `motion.py` measures `over(onHero, 0.82, hero stop 0)` against the sign composite (4.498 at
  0.61), so the shells did not enforce the 8-bit 0.60. Both shells now use `motion.py`'s definition; 0.61 goes red.
- **F3, R2 and P2, the frame cap**: Task 4 accepted a frame at 90% of 33.3 ms (about 33 fps on 100 and 165 Hz). Wave 1
  used a minimum interval of 31.33 ms (60, 90 and 120 Hz 30 fps, 100 Hz 25, 144 Hz 28.8, 165 Hz 27.5); the re-review
  showed 61 Hz drawing 30.5 and 62.5 Hz 31.25; wave 2 made it a due time with a resync (no burst after a stall); the
  look then found Aurora windows drawing 60 frames a second, because the page art and the hero each started their own
  cadence and about half the launches landed on alternating vsyncs (603 frames in 10 s, 14 launches seen on API 34 and 37).
  Wave 3: every `FrameGate` keeps the first vsync in each slot of one grid (`floorDiv(now + 2 ms, 33.33 ms)` from the
  frame clock's zero) with a 20 ms minimum gap; simulated at 48, 50, 60, 61, 62.5, 75, 90, 100, 120, 144, 165 and
  240 Hz, every rate 30.0; proof by `dumpsys gfxinfo` on Overview in Aurora (page art and hero): 18 of 18 launches at
  30 a second (API 34 light 301 x 6, dark 301 x 5 and 300, API 37 light 302 x 5 and 301). iOS: the old
  `.animation(minimumInterval:)` schedule was measured first on a probe build: 6 of 8 launches drew two canvases per
  frame at 30 a second, 2 drew one canvas only (not explained); the new `ArtSchedule` (a `TimelineSchedule` on multiples
  of 1/30 s from the reference date, empty when paused) drew two per frame in 6 of 6.
- **F4, the arched hem**: the "faint rounded box edges" Tasks 3 and 5 saw on Aurora light and in the hero's lower right
  were not blur clipped at a layer's bounds: the Look Book's `.curtain` is `border-radius: 0 0 50% 50% / 0 0 30% 30%` and
  neither the plan nor `motion.py` listed it, so the low-alpha tail kept square corners that read as nested boxes under
  the blur, with 1 to 2 level banding. Both shells now fill and clip to a path whose lower corners are quarter ellipses
  (0.5 w by 0.3 h from `hemTop` 0.70, two cubics with kappa 0.5522847498), `.dithersResult` on iOS's blur and a dithering
  paint on Android; `stack.py` with the arch prints the same values (the arch only removes area).
- **F5, the streaks**: neither shell shows the spec's vertical ray streaks: both blur the layer after the 11 pt bar
  pattern, so it averages to its mean (0.60); in the Look Book the filter runs before the mask and the bars are crisp.
  Crisp bars would break the floors (`stack.py` with the factor raised: Aurora dark textDim 4.27 screen and 4.35
  source-over at 0.80, 3.71 and 3.79 at 0.95; Aurora light source-over textDim 4.43 at 0.95), so the pattern stays blurred
  and a visible ray is a strength re-derivation (section 4).
- **F6, the bolt's spring**: the Look Book's `.45s cubic-bezier(.3,1.4,.5,1)` is response 0.45 and damping 0.55; iOS
  shares the press spring (0.25 and 0.5) for the scale and takes its own `.spring(response: 0.45, dampingFraction:
  0.55)` for the rotation only (the modifier order is pinned); Android `spring(dampingRatio = 0.55, stiffness = 195)`,
  (2 pi / 0.45) squared being 194.96. The + glyph turns with the hex, as the Look Book's `.plus:active` does; at 30
  degrees it is not an x.
- **F7, F8, F10**: Android's `pageArt` and `heroArt` end in `.graphicsLayer()` and a `CurtainCache` keeps the hem
  paths, brushes, bars path, one Matrix and one Paint; iOS draws the three curtains in one `drawLayer` with a single
  dithered blur (six blur passes became one; the stars are no longer screened by the curtains and are veiled by the green
  band, now the same as Android); `HeroArt` is one `Group` with `.accessibilityHidden(true).allowsHitTesting(false)` and the
  clip moved to the art alone (`.background { HeroArt().clipShape(...) }`, so nothing in the hero's content is cut).
- **N8 and N16, the blends**: a SwiftUI `Canvas` blends only within its own transparent backing, and Android's curtains
  sit in one offscreen layer; Screen and Multiply therefore act among the curtains and the layer lands source-over on the
  ground, the same on both shells. That is the contrast-safe direction (a true multiply would break the light floor, see
  N27).
- **P1, full bleed** (look, API 34 and 37): the Android Aurora art stopped at the status bar and drew a hard edge across
  the top of every Aurora page, and API 37's gesture bar showed a flat band. Cause: D-184's root box carries
  `windowInsetsPadding(WindowInsets.safeDrawing)` and paints `Tok.bg`, so each page node stops at the bars, and D-214's
  grounds draw `drawRect` and a node-sized layer, where D-213's blooms were unclipped circles. Fix: `Bleed.of` carries a
  node edge that lies within the safe-drawing inset to the window's edge, measured with `onGloballyPositioned`, and every
  ground draws through `bled(...)`. Largest per-row channel change in rows 0 to 200: API 34 light 34 at y 61 before, 3
  after (paired reading 2.0); API 37 light 20 before and 2 after, dark 19 and 2; gesture bar 20 at y 2336 before and 1
  after. The container is now the window, as on iOS, so the curtain fractions are fractions of the window; Vardr Labs'
  grid now also runs under the bars (it already did on iOS).
- **P3, iOS main thread**: Vardr Labs 20.3% and Norse 16.3% against the 12% line, from 22 sign and 16 rune `Text`
  resolutions every frame. `ArtCanvas` is now generic over Canvas `symbols` (each rune and each sign a symbol resolved
  once, redrawn only when its view changes) and the draws call `resolveSymbol(id:)`. Figures in the performance table.
- **P4, the Norse watermark glyph on Android** (no code change): it is U+16A0 in the system's Noto Sans Runic, whose Fehu
  has curved branches where Apple's are straight, the same shape as D-213's tab rune. The plan forbade a bundled font, so
  this unit pins today's behaviour (`the_norse_watermark_is_fehu_in_the_system_runic_font`); the founder then ruled
  (2026-10-15) that both phones must look identical, type included: D-215 bundles our own Vardr Runes and IBM Plex Sans
  (section 4 (i)).
- **Ground tokens by shell**: the count tests pin iOS `Tokens.groundFaint` 14 and `Tokens.groundAccent` 3, Android
  `Tok.groundFaint(` 10 and `Tok.groundAccent(` 18, with the site-by-site classification in the Task 5 and Task 6
  reports (the reasons are in section 4).

ms. Every art frame completes near 17.2 ms against a 16.67 ms deadline while frames sit exactly 33.33 ms apart, so
nothing is dropped; the metric is read as an artefact of the 30 fps cadence on this AVD, and a phone needs the real check.
Idle CPU on Home with motion on (iOS simulator process, one core, mean of 6 samples; Android `top`, 3 samples; before
wave 3): iOS Aurora light 13.5, dark 13.1, Norse 19.1, Vardr Labs light 25.0, dark 25.7; Android Aurora light 24 to 27,

light), 3.3 (dark), 2.0 (Norse), 3.2 (Vardr Labs). iOS Aurora's main thread is mostly `CA::Transaction::commit` (1061 of
1608 ms in 15.6 s), not the draw closure. Performance was measured on the simulator and the emulator only; the founder
judges it on his phones at 0.5.0.

  Space Grotesk in Vardr Labs; typography is built from the theme's body face (`materialTypography(theme)`, remembered per
  theme). The final review's I1 then found it kept Material's letter spacing (bodyLarge 0.5 sp and others), so every
  Material-drawn text tracked on Android only; every style now copies `letterSpacing = 0.sp`, asserted per theme. Material's
  sizes and line heights stay (they belong to components iOS draws differently).
- **The twin mechanism for runes** (an **accepted asymmetry, not residue**; recorded, not faked). iOS (deployment target 17)
  makes Vardr Runes the first Core Text cascade fallback of every text face (`TypeRole.descriptor`; one place, every face,
  weight and Dynamic Type size, Latin never reaches it, `testTheCascadeOnlyCatchesRunes` proves both directions). Android has
  minSdk 26, `Typeface.CustomFallbackBuilder` needs 29 and Compose has no per-glyph fallback, so a `SpanStyle(fontFamily =
  Type.runes, fontWeight = Normal, fontSynthesis = None)` goes on each rune character through one helper, with the accent
  split as iOS's attributed separator. Same pixels, different mechanism; an Android source guard fails a rune that reaches a
  `Text` as a plain String. The final review confirmed the rune font's vertical metrics (hhea 900 / -250) sit inside Plex Sans
  (1025 / -275) and Cormorant SC (924 / -287), so a rune never makes a line taller on either shell.
- **The licence leg's hole.** B3's planned red did not hold: `licences.py --check` compares the regenerated JSON with the
  committed file and walks explicit tables only, so a bundled font with no inventory entry stayed green. The red was made by
  the About tests on both shells and the hole was closed as B3b before B4, which moved the Vardr Runes entry into B4. The leg
  now also fails a native font with no `ANDROID_FONT_COPIES` entry, a `SpaceGroteskX.ttf` lookalike, and pins Space Grotesk's
  sha256 (the review called that file a D-174 subset; git shows it unchanged since c989f5b, its introduction, so what is
  pinned is what ships).
- **The D-162 hole again** (a runner prediction, controller-verified, fixed in F2). `TypeThemeTest` and others read iOS files
  (`AccountHubScreen.swift`, `People.swift`, the `ios/Skipti/App` directory) and `native/licences/licences.json` that
  `build.gradle.kts` did not declare as inputs, so Gradle would reuse a cached pass after those files changed. F2 declared the
  directory and the json as one input each and proved it by touching `People.swift` and seeing the class re-run.
- **A twin difference older than D-215** (B5's review): the Add expense group line was an iOS `LabeledContent` (label left, name
  right, no separator) and Android's `Group <sep> Name`; Android now matches iOS (`ae6bd31`). The look's description of that row
  needs a second reading (section 4).
- **Twin size gaps found by the final re-review and fixed in F2**: the Appearance card's segment titles (iOS 13 pt, Android 14
  sp) and its detail line and text-size caption (iOS 14, Android 16); both now 14 on both shells and pinned against each other
  (`AppearanceCopy.detailSize` / `DETAIL_SIZE`).
- **G1**: matching Lucide's ink height under-sized the Norse tab runes by eye; the founder's judgement came first and the
  value is 34 (ink 0.70 em = 23.8 pt, rune centred by its ink, the slot still 52 by 30 so the bar does not grow). Norse
  buttons, form-action-bar backing, hero Settle up and the Invites paste field take `controlShape`; about 14 panel sites per
  shell, the group stat tiles included, take `panelShape` (chamfer 8 above 40 high, else 6, cut by the measured height on both
  shells). Aurora and Vardr Labs are unchanged by construction.
- **The Plex Sans copyright year.** The shipped Regular file's name record 0 says Copyright 2018 IBM; IBM's `LICENSE.txt`
  and the Plex Mono files say 2017. NOTICE and the inventory print 2018, as read from the file (the rule for Plex Mono too).

**Mistakes, recorded plainly:**
- B2's implementer truncated `Tokens.kt` with its own sabotage runner and redid the edit; the controller checked the file
  (303 to 339 lines, +42 / -6, tree clean) before the review.
- B3's planned red did not hold, and the licence leg had missed a bundled font with no inventory entry until B3b (above).
- A3 drafted `outline.py` and `build.py` before writing the tests; its RED was made afterwards by moving them out of the tree
  (the report says so).
- B5's own first test counted three rune-producing sites in `BalanceScreen` where the file has four (the test's fault,
  corrected).
- A3 changed glyphs outside SKIPTI's 25 after the founder had approved the block (four dot positions and ᛀ, ᛂ, ᛳ, ᛷ) and said
  so as a concern; the review confirmed SKIPTI's own 25 (the 24 Elder Futhark runes and U+16EB) are unchanged, and the
  founder was shown the changes and kept them (decision 7).
- Two agents' scratch pages (127.0.0.1:8765, runes at large size) sat in the browser pane the founder was looking at, and he
  called them messy; closed. Every dispatch now says to close one's own pages and servers.
- The D-211 regression above reached main with every gate green for lack of a test that ran the proof.

**Look** (Sonnet, throwaway devices only: iOS 27.0 simulator `d214-look`, an AVD `d215-look` API 34, deleted after;
`--groups-proof` data on both, plus one long-name group and one long note made through the apps' own flows; report
`.drafts/d215/look/look-report.md`, 65 screen pairs and 6 zoom pairs in `.drafts/d215/look/`, side-by-sides in `pairs/`;
at HEAD 0d9cf8f, before G1's last two commits, which have their own pairs in `.drafts/d215/g1/`). Results: no wrong face (no
system face in app text on either phone, no Roboto in Vardr Labs), no seams at joins, no fake bold, no tofu; Vardr Labs'
unstyled text is Space Grotesk on both; Android dialogs and menus draw the theme's body face; iOS's segmented control follows
the theme after a switch with the card open; Norse runes (tabs, ornament, section mark, separator, drift, the 92 pt
watermark) are the same carved shapes on both. Dynamic Type at iOS AX5 against Android font scale 2.0 (not the same
magnification: iOS scales per text style to about 3.1 times for body, Android linearly 2.0). **Time Profiler**, Norse with the
drift running (attach by pid; by name failed): main thread 8.8 percent busy over 16.2 s, no Core Text, cascade or font
descriptor frames at all; about 2 percent of wall is glyph rasterisation of the rotating runes (prerender to bitmaps if an old
phone shows it). **Size table**: 16 size families differ between the phones, none caused by D-215 (section 4). **Not reached**:
Vardr Labs dark's expense detail, group page, Settle up, Add expense and dialog; Aurora dark's Add expense, About, Licences;
Vardr light's Add expense, About, Licences and group page; a real-account Groups screen; iOS 26.5 and 17 to 25; some Aurora
light shots (03, 07, 08, 18 to 20) were taken with taps that raced the screen and only 02, 04 to 06, 09 to 12, 15 to 17 and 21
were rechecked by eye.

inventory, runes font, rune sites and spans, the cascade, bar buttons, the segmented control, root font, tabular figures,

**The founder's decisions** (2026-10-16; the Look Book fixes canvas and chat):
(1) **titles Option A, iPhone's way on both phones** ("title and one type scale (iPhone way) looks better"; this overrode the
recommendation of B): tab roots a large 34 title that folds into the bar, every other screen an inline 17 centred title,
and Android draws iOS's bar; (2) every size family takes iOS's value; (3) the type roles fold in (Q13 a); (4) section
headings take the theme's section label (Q1 a); (5) Norse keeps sentence case (Q14 a); (6) Q6 ray streaks C, keep as today,
and every other Look Book question as recommended; (7) **onboarding is not touched** (deferred to 0.5.1 or the public
build); (8) **the two D-210 leftovers go into 0.5.0**, right after this unit (hide zero-net loops on People cards, which
is core; refuse invites for a place a member already holds, app, `createInvite`, `inviteUser` and `inviteKnown`; they
deploy with 0.5.0); (9) **speed tricks are a standing rule** (CLAUDE.md section 4, "Speed rules", and memory). L06 (the
Vardr Labs kicker at 12.4 against 13) was left as it was, by the spec. Decisions that were the controller's: the Norse
ornament's placement under the large title only (spec); Join a sheet on both phones, locked once a join starts; the
push-only pages as sheets with Close (Android) as on iOS; the people-list chevron colour recorded, not changed; the 48 dp
target as a guard; the back chevron in the label colour on Android (measured on iOS 26 and 27); the final review's triage
accepted as written; the sabotage matrix sized to risk (120 rows planned, not D-215's 413).

**Findings that shaped it:**
- **Android had no navigation bar to adapt.** The inventory (46 rows) found every title a `Text` in the scrolling
  content, every back a hand-built `TextButton`, and several twin differences nobody had listed (Sign in with no on-screen back;
  the Expenses title only in its data state; Import review, Export and Join paste titled differently). The plan grew to
  nine tasks for it.
- **Hit testing is limited by the parent** (T4, measured). A back button drawn 48 dp inside a 44 dp bar is hit only inside the
  bar, so the 2 dp above and below were dead; `requiredSize(48)` and `minimumInteractiveComponentSize()` both failed with
  taps 60 px off centre. The fix is a 48 dp node (flush with the bar's top, 4 dp over its bottom) holding the button, an unbounded
  ripple of 18 dp so the square is not clipped to a circle, and a source guard; the final wave gave the Cancel and Done pills
  the same node (T4 Minor 4).
- **The two phones' back arrows are not the same thing on iOS 26 and later.** iOS draws the back chevron itself inside its
  glass button, in the label colour (D-214 measured it; the T2 look agreed), so `BarTint.backIndicator`'s Lucide chevron
  reaches only iOS 17 to 25. Android's round button takes the Lucide drawing and, after the final wave, the text colour.
  Section 4 records the rest.
- **Money must shrink, not clip** (final review I2, then the look). iOS has `.minimumScaleFactor(0.6)` on the hero amount and the
  stat tiles; Android stepped once at nine characters and the hero did not shrink at all (44 sp from 40 made it worse), so
  digits of a balance disappeared at font scale 2.0. Both now use `amountAutoSize` (floor `AMOUNT_MIN_SCALE` 0.6, min sizes
  26.4 and 9.6, one line, no wrap); the look's `$123,456,789.50` still did not fit a three-across tile at 60 percent, and
  past the floor Android cut digits silently where iOS's `lineLimit(1)` ends the amount in an ellipsis, so 2b added the
  ellipsis (a3a3dc6).
- **Join** (final review I1, from T5's concern). The Cancel T5 added at the two iOS sheet sites stayed visible in the joined
  state and skipped `onJoined`, so the caller's dismiss and reload never ran; Android drew Join as a pushed page with a back
  button and no `BackHandler` on the opened-link route. Now `JoinScreen` takes an optional `onCancel`, `Phase.locked`
  (joining, joined) hides Cancel and the back and disables the interactive dismiss, and on Android a sheet on both entries,
  a pushed page only inside Join paste, with a `BackHandler` that calls `onJoined` once locked.
- **TalkBack** read the bar after the whole page (the content column fills from y = 0, so Compose's geometric sort put it
  first); `traversalIndex = -1f` on the bar's `isTraversalGroup`, pinned by a test, **not verified with TalkBack** (the
  throwaway image has none; installing it would be a download).
- **The account glyph reloaded on every tab switch** (HomeShell composes only the selected root). The shell now holds the avatar
  and name and one `LaunchedEffect`, provides them through a `CompositionLocal` (`LocalAccountFace`), and each root's glyph is
  stateless; the look's first frame after a switch shows the initial.
- **The ornament's distance** was measured, not argued: on iOS 27 it sits 15.7 pt under the large title's glyph bottom (the
  system's own layout; `TitleOrnament.titleBottomInset` 15 is a measured constant); Android reads the title's baseline and
  measured 16.0 dp. The empty states' negative padding (T2 Minor 3) was looked at in T6's fix.
- **The Appearance twin, once more:** `AppearanceCopy.detailSize` stays the literal 14 on iOS because D-215's Android test
  parses it with a regex; moving it to `TypeScale.detail` needs both shells in one commit (T2, T3).
- **Guards moved stricter, not looser** (final review): each count that moved carries its reason (groundAccent 18 to 4 as
  the Back buttons went, groundFaint 10 to 14, section labels 31 to 35 and 42 to 47, kickers 17 to 19 and 24 to 26).
  The final wave anchored the `TypeScale` parity regex, banned `lineHeight =` in every main Kotlin file (scan floor 40),
  made the iOS display-mode guard fail a `.navigationTitle(` that does not start its line, and removed a vacuous assertion.

**Mistakes, recorded plainly:**
- **The near miss: a T5 agent ran `git stash` and `git stash apply` in the shared tree** while the T4 agent had uncommitted Android
  work. The apply was clean and the stash dropped at once; the controller checked afterwards (stash empty, both commits
  intact, nothing lost), but it was luck that the two agents' files were disjoint. The rule now: no subagent in a shared checkout
  runs `git stash`, `reset`, `checkout -- <file>` or `restore`, each refuses to commit if the index holds a file it did not
  stage, and the controller dispatches a committing agent only when `git diff --cached --name-only` is empty (CLAUDE.md
  section 4, item 4, and memory). (T5's own brief already said to refuse a commit if the index held a file it had not staged; the no-stash rule was added to the dispatches and memory after the incident.)
- **Tests after code.** T1 did not run its iOS red step; T2 ran no separate red step; T3 wrote its pure-style tests after the
  APIs; T8 wrote its tests after the code; the final wave's iOS Join guard was written after the edit. In each case the
  sabotage row is the proof the guard goes red for the right reason (the reports say so).
- **T2 moved the sites its brief listed and left two group names (Expenses group header, Settle up) on `label`**: the review's one
  Important, fixed in 916d1a4.
- **The plan's "recorded, not changed" list missed the sheet roots T5 and T8 did not reach** (the removal review, and the
  push-only pages), and Join as a pushed page on Android: the final review's I1 and I7.
- **T4's back target** was first built as 48 dp inside a 44 dp bar and described as 48 x 48; the review doubted it, the fix
  measured it with taps and rebuilt it (above).
- **A plan deviation, recorded by T8 but not as one:** the plan said row 45, All currencies, becomes a pushed page; it stayed
  the same full-screen `Dialog` with a `PushedBar` inside, which keeps the system scrim strips (section 4).
- **Near-duplicate guards.** The final wave discarded one sabotage row (a `SheetBar(name, onCancel = onCancel, ...)` change turned
  two tests red because the listed-sheets guard pins the same line) and replaced it with a caller-side row.

**Process, the speed work** (CLAUDE.md section 4, "Speed rules", c66d60e): D-215's 413-row matrix took 2 h 14 min. This unit
used the booted-simulator rule (every runner and dispatch says to boot AFAF4221 before a series of `xcodebuild test` calls and
shut it down after: 15 s a row against 68), sized the matrix to the risk (120 rows planned), and built the runner
(`.drafts/d217/sabotage.py lanes`) to run the iOS and Android lanes in parallel in their own git worktrees outside the
checkout (`/private/tmp/skipti-d217-ios` and `-android`, own DerivedData, `android/local.properties` copied, the iOS lane with
`-clonedSourcePackagesDirPath` pointing at the main checkout's `ios/build/SourcePackages` so nothing is fetched). Per task, the
parallel dispatches were on disjoint files (T2 with T3, T4 with T5, T6's fix with T7).

and deleted by each agent that used it, `pgrep -f qemu-system` empty after each; the iOS look on the `d214-look` simulator;
`--groups-proof` data, no sign-in, no cloud, no `--emulators`): T3 (Groups, Balance, Expenses in Norse), T4 (Aurora light and
dark: the status-strip seam before and after, the 48 dp target by `adb` taps), T6 (every root and the group page and expense
detail in Aurora light, Aurora dark and Norse, scrolled and not, Norse's empty Expenses), T6's fix (the empty states centred),
T7 (You, About, Licences, People, Add a person, the nested system Back), T8 (Add and Edit expense, New group, Add a person,
the currency list, side padding measured 20.2 dp and 16 dp, in Aurora light and Norse), and the final wave (a long title at
font scale 1.0 and 2.0 clears Cancel, Done and the back button; the hero at 2.0; the glyph after a tab switch; an opened
invite link as a sheet; Invitations and a pushed expense with Close; the currency dialog's scrolled bar). **Not looked at in
the build, proven by tests only:** Join's offer, joining and joined states on either phone (need an account and a live invite),
the removal review's Cancel, the scrolled person sheet (cloud groups only), Your name, Pick or Change username, TalkBack
order, and Vardr Labs' group page and expense detail. The full look follows.

The look (`.drafts/d217/look/look-report.md`, 63 pairs: 29 Aurora light, 8 each in Aurora dark, Norse, Vardr Labs light and dark, 4 at the largest text size, 2 empty states; iPhone on the throwaway d214-look, Android on a throwaway AVD, deleted): the size table D1 to D16 reads 0 DIFF (every ratio 0.98 to 1.01). Its DEFECT items were fixed in the look fix waves (aea6892, e4bce27, ce3290d): the content start under the bar now within about 0.5 dp of iOS on the measured pages, the "D17" 16 sp leftovers at iOS's 13 and 14, the bar pills (43.5 dp, growing with the text, about 57 dp at font scale 2.0) and glyphs at iOS's sizes, expense detail's actions pinned. The rest is routed (section 4 and the audit's "Found in the D-217 look").

**The founder's ask** (2026-10-16, WORKLOG session 3, and D-210 residue (b)): "hide zero-net loops on People cards (core
removes equal cycles from the pairwise view; totals unchanged); refuse invites for a place a member already holds (the
app never offers it; createInvite, inviteUser and inviteKnown refuse with a clear message; a refusal test in
firebase/tests, a CLOUD-SECURITY row the same day; it deploys with 0.5.0, not before)."

**Decisions made for the founder** (the controller's, WORKLOG NOW items 2 to 4; each overturnable in one line):
1. **The loop rule.** A zero-net loop is any directed cycle in the pairwise matrix, cancelled by its smallest edge until
   none is left. The founder's words, "equal cycles", read narrowly (only cycles whose edges are all equal) fail a
   realistic Settle all: A owes B 10 and C 10, B and C each owe D 10, Settle all says A pays D 20; pairwise is then
   (A,B) 10, (A,C) 10, (B,D) 10, (C,D) 10, (D,A) 20, everyone at 0, and no cycle has equal edges, so five cards stay on
   screen. Cancelling by the smallest edge clears it in two rounds. Cancelling a cycle changes no one's net, so the
   totals, `viewer_net_minor`, the Settle all plan and Balance are unchanged by construction (tested), and every entry
   left was in the matrix before, in the same direction, for the same or less: no new pair, so SPEC 5.6's objection to
   simplification ("you owe Carol" when you never dealt with Carol) cannot arise and no toggle is needed.
2. **Deterministic, ascending participant id, after the collapse.** Order matters (golden G4: descending order gives a
   different matrix), so core takes the first cycle a depth-first search finds in ascending id, a fresh search after each
   cancellation; the matrix is per group and currency and never depends on the viewer, so A's card always mirrors B's
   and both phones agree. Not "fewest cards" (an optimisation with its own ties). After D-210's collapse, which keeps
   D-210's goldens exactly (G6 pins the order: cancel then collapse gives (1,5) 3, (4,5) 2 instead of (1,4) 1, (1,5) 2,
   (4,5) 3).
3. **ALREADY_EXISTS for the refusal**, message "Someone has already joined as this person." (acceptInvite's existing
   words, now the constant `HELD`). The phones map refusals by status, never by text; FAILED_PRECONDITION already means
   "They are already in this group." for inviteUser and inviteKnown and "already used or has expired" in
   `InviteCopy.failure`, so only a distinct status lets the phone say the right thing. None of the three Functions
   returned ALREADY_EXISTS before; T3 re-read every caller of `InviteCopy.failure` and none other can receive it.
4. **"Held" is what acceptInvite's check reads**: a current member whose own participant id is the place, an accepted, not
   ended invite of a current member, or two such accounts (contested is held, not CHANGED: the Function only refuses).
   The check runs after each Function's existing target checks (every old refusal keeps its status) and before anything
   is written or charged (a refused invite costs no daily quota).
5. **The CLOUD-SECURITY "row the same day"** is an "Also pending at 0.5.0 (D-218, 2026-10-16: merged, NOT deployed)"
   paragraph and the section 4.2 lines, not a dated section 2 row: the document's own rule is no section 2 row until a
   change is live, and D-210 and D-211 recorded their merged changes the same way. The section 2 row is written the day
   0.5.0 deploys, with D-210's and D-211's.
6. Smaller calls: no FFI signature change and no core version bump (the version marks export and wire changes; the
   doc-comment-only bindings change of 8d58bfa is neither); no new
   callable listing held places for phones (residue); the loop twin tests on the shells are not sabotaged (they guard
   core's behaviour through the library, C1 covers it); one commit per shell in T3 (accepted).

**Findings that shaped it:**
- **A doc comment is part of the bindings** (gate run 1): UniFFI copies Rust doc comments on exported types into the Swift
  and Kotlin it generates, so editing the comment above `BalanceLineOut` made the committed bindings stale with no API
  change. Task 1's "no bindings regeneration" was wrong for this reason; 8d58bfa regenerated them and run 2 passed.
- **JVM tests load `target/debug/libskipti_core.dylib`, which `make android-core` does not refresh** (T3): the library was
  stale from 2026-10-14 until `cargo build -p skipti-core`; a JVM test of a core change after `make android-core` alone runs
  the old core. `run-common.md` now says so for every agent of the run.
- **The plan's sabotage row C2 is an equivalent mutant** (T1, the review agreed): subtracting m - 1 leaves 1 on every edge of
  the loop and deletes none, the next search finds the same cycle with smallest edge 1 and removes it, so the result is
  identical. C2b (clear the edge entirely) replaced it. The plan's C2 expected-red list (G1, G2, G3, property) is wrong and
  is corrected in the table below.
- **The look had no button for a Settle all plan transfer**: Settle up draws the Fastest plan as text and records per card
  ("I paid Bo"), so Look 1 built the same pairwise ledger with a third expense ("Paid Cy", you paid, split only to Cy).
  It proves the cards hiding, not the Settle all flow.
- **A 0.4.0 phone reads the new refusal with the wrong sentence** once the Functions are deployed (final review I2; section 4).
- **The held check can be made by a copied participant id** (final review I1): a member whose account was made with
  someone's place id makes that place held, as acceptInvite already refused joining it (D-210); the record now says so.
- **The new read cost on createInvite** (M2): 1 + 1 + N + K reads, K unbounded (section 4, CLOUD-SECURITY).
- **"Try again" on a permanent refusal** (the look): fixed in the fix wave, covered by tests and source pins only, not

**Decisions made for the founder** (the plan's DECIDED lines and WORKLOG NOW item 5; each overturnable in one line):
1. **The + glyph at stroke 2.8, every other Lucide icon at 2.4.** The Look Book's `svg.i` rule is 2.4 (LB 116), and its
   plus is drawn at `stroke-width:2.8` inline (LB 335), heavier than the other icons. One constant per shell
   (`LucideStroke.width` / `WIDTH`, `.plus` / `PLUS`); only the + reads the second.
2. **The solid ground is the existing `surface` token.** The Look Book's `--p-solid` equals `surface` in Vardr Labs light
   and dark and is 3/255 darker in Norse (#0F0F11 against #121214); every label and glyph pair on `surface` is already a
   measured pair (art.py section 11: text 13.89 or more, textDim 6.80 or more). C2, S1 or E3 may add a `solid` token
   through palette.py if Aurora dark's difference matters there.
3. **One 64 x 64 footprint for every + face, drawn centred and overflowing; the lift stays 18.** Found while planning L17:
   the face's own box set the bar row's height, so Norse's 70.71 diamond box made its bar 76.7 pt, taller than the 72
   (`ShellBar.reserved`) the pages leave clear, and its last row sat under the bar; side 64 would have made it 96.5. Every
   face's centre is now 50 above the row bottom and every bar in a shell has one height in every theme.
4. **The diamond at side 64, centred on the circle's centre** (the Look Book turns the circle's own square, LB 115 and
   238). Its box is 90.51; it stands 25.25 pt over the bar top (the circle 12) and reaches 45.25 from the + centre, short
   of the neighbour glyph's near edge at every width from 320 (49.72) up. A visible change by the Look Book's own
   proportions: the founder judges it at his look.
5. **The reticle at 32 pt** (LB 24 px on the 54 px bolt, x 72/54), stroked at `LucideStroke.width`, round caps and joins,

**Brief values corrected by measurement:**
- **iOS's back chevron is 10.667 pt wide, not 10.5.** The ink is 8.4 units x 1.25 = 10.5 pt = 31.5 px at 3x, which the
  renderer rounds up to 32 px. T2 asserts the width to one device pixel (0.34), as the height (18.0 = 54 px) always was;
  I1 and I3 still turn it red. The review offered `ceil(10.5 * scale) / scale` as a tighter form; not taken.
- **The bolt glyph's worst contrast golden is 3.85 on iOS and 3.868 on Android** (Vardr Labs light, onAccent on the
  bolt's #677B8C inside the 32 pt reticle box, t 0.261 to 0.739; was 4.08 and 4.094 at the 28 pt plus). iOS interpolates
  the gradient in float and tracks art.py's unrounded 3.85; Compose holds 8-bit colour, so Android measures art.py's
  printed #677B8C, re-derived in Python as 3.8683 (T3, and again by its reviewer). The same relation as D-213's pair; both
  clear 3:1 and both tests also assert the floor per colour.
- **"Every bar is 70 tall" is iOS's arithmetic** (6 above the row, 64 footprint). Android's row has 6 dp above AND below:
  76 dp in every theme (Norse's dropped from 82.7). Decision 8.

**Findings that shaped it:**
- **A + face outside its footprint takes the tap on both shells** (T3 feared Compose would not deliver it; its reviewer
  showed Compose stops only at a clipping layer, and the look tapped every tip and corner): the risk was the z-order.
  The diamond's side tips sit at the top edge of the neighbour items, whose hit areas are the full slot and about 50
  tall; the left neighbour comes before the + and sits under it, the right (Groups) comes after and hit-tests first on
  both shells (SwiftUI front to back; Compose walks `zSortedChildren` reversed). The overlap under the right tip is about
  4 pt on a 402 pt iPhone and about 8 dp at 360 dp; the bolt overlaps by 1.2 dp at 360 dp (I-1). `zIndex` fixed it.
- **Android's `Modifier.size` lets the slot squeeze a face** (planner): D-213's 70.71 diamond drew at 69.6 on a 360 dp
  phone. Every face is now `requiredSize`; the footprint Box itself can still narrow below 64 under 332 dp (section 4).

  system's glass button, which draws its own chevron (D-217 residue (b)); the look found its pixels identical to D-217's
  shot (coverage 71.64 against 71.66). Android's Lucide chevron was 7.6 x 13.0 dp against the glass chevron's 11.0 x
  18.7 pt, about 30 percent smaller: fixed by decision 9.

**Decisions made for the founder** (the plan's DECIDED lines and WORKLOG NOW items 6 and 7; each overturnable in one line):
1. **Norse pills notched at 4.** His 2026-10-15 rule ("anything rectangular follows the notch"); 4 on 19 to 33 pt pills is
   0.12 to 0.21 of the height, the button's proportion (8 on 52 is 0.15; art.py section 13). The Look Book's radius 2
   (LB 240) is the drawing from before the notch rule.
2. **Vardr Labs pills outlined** (LB 269: transparent, a 40 percent border in the tone's ink, square); selected and
   unselected filter chips keep a full border because they are controls; photo chips keep their film in every theme.
3. **An outlined pill on the page ground fills with `bg`** (the filter chips, the currency chip): accent words straight
   on the Vardr Labs light grid's darkest dot measure 4.12 (art.py 13a), so the page colour masks the dots under the
   words and still reads as transparent.
4. **Vardr Labs panels square everywhere** through the one `panelKind` / `panelShape` decision at `min(radius,
   cardRadius)` (LB 267, nothing round inside a Vardr Labs card; `buttonRadius` already followed the same `min`). Aurora
   is unchanged (every call site asks 10 to 18, under 20).
5. **Photo frames take the card's shape and edge**: Norse the notch with a 1 pt `norseEdge`, Vardr Labs square with
   `FrameMarks` in WHITE at `frameAlpha` (the photo's own words are white; `textDim` marks vanish on a dark photo),
   Aurora none. The ᛫ on the white lines over a photo stays white: gold over an arbitrary photo is not measured.
6. **Norse diamond tiles at the full tile size**: drawn at size x sqrt 2 (79.196 at 56, art.py section 15) centred on a
   footprint of the size, so layouts do not move; it overflows by 0.207 x size each side, clear of the neighbour at every
   call site art.py measured (6.21 to 11.60 against 10 to 14 of spacing). The letter is 0.42 of the size on every shape
   and the emoji 0.5 (D-217's 0.36 and 0.4 diamond branches are gone).
7. **Blue replaces violet in violet's slot** (`GroupTone.blue` / `BLUE`), so every group that was violet turns blue and no
   other group changes tone. OKLCH hue 264 in Aurora light, 27 degrees from sky, purple starting near 285; the wheel
   between amber and teal holds the money greens, so green was ruled out. Every letter holds 4.5 on its fill; Vardr Labs
   light's letter nudged by the generator to #4F6089.
8. **Android's Aurora bars blur at 20 dp under a 0.72 film** (iOS's tab-bar film), on API 31 and up; API 26 to 30 have
   no `RenderEffect`, so the content is cut out from under the bar and C1's 0.94 film stays.
9. **A2: the Vardr Labs light ground accent becomes #475B6B** (from #4C6172), 4.52 on the grid's dot pixel `#C8D0D6`
   measured on 8-bit pixels (was 4.13), asserted with bg, surface and surfaceRaised by the AppearanceTests on both shells.

**Findings that shaped it:**
- **Nothing was behind Android's tab bar**: it sat under the page in a Column, so a blur had nothing to blur. T5 made it
  overlay the page as iOS's does; each page HomeShell shows keeps the measured bar height clear (`LocalShellBarInset`),
  and the fix wave's guard `every_page_under_the_tab_bar_keeps_it_clear` lists the five (GroupPage, OverviewScreen,
  GroupsTab, ExpenseListScreen, SettleAllScreen). CLAUDE.md section 10.2 says so.
- **Android's form action bar had no backing**: at 0.45 alpha the rows would show through a dimmed button (iOS backs it
  with `bg`). Added in T5.
- **The render tests raced the host app**: `testAPillPaintsItsTableInItsShape` rendered Aurora unfilled once under load,
  as if `AppearanceApplier.sync()` reset the shared theme between a set and a render. A 1 s settle made it rarer; the
  fix wave's `render(_:_:scheme:size:)` helper sets the theme, renders, checks the theme held and retries only a reset
  theme (3 tries, never a wrong pixel). The tests at ThemeArtTests 1051 onward use their own `AppearanceState()`, which
  the host never writes, and are unchanged.
- **iOS 27's default and transparent navigation appearances are identical at run time** (T4's J10 survived until a
  source pin was added).
- **D-219's look item for C2 (A1)**: the account glyph a glass bubble on iOS and flat on Android. T5 drew iOS's glass
  (white film, hairline ring); the look then found the size and badge colours still apart (iOS 41 pt inset, a grey badge

  found V9 red in xcodebuild's "Failing tests:" block (its log lines had split the per-test "failed" line), fixed the
  runner (the block parsed, V16's anchor, `os.utime` after restore), re-ran V9 (EXACT) and ran V16, P1 to P4 and K1 to K6.
- **The runner lesson** (now in run-common.md): read xcodebuild's STDERR too, because `** TEST FAILED **` is printed
  there, and its "Failing tests:" block, because per-test lines can split; an anchor that matches 0 times must stop the
  run loudly. T2's runner captured stdout only, so every red row's raw line said "NOT OK"; `verdicts.py` recomputed each
  verdict from zero compile errors, the red set and passed plus red equal to the classes' count (no line lost), and the
  runner was fixed (`.drafts/d220/t2/sab.py`, reused by T4 and the iOS fix lane). D-219's iOS runner printed the failed
  lists for a person to judge and set no verdict from that marker.
- **T2's first sabotage attempt** (`sab.first-attempt.out`, 13:18) stopped at I1 with the render test red as well as the
  pill census; that is the render race above. The run was redone after the settle went in.
- **T3's A3 and A5 ran twice**: A3's expected set was one test and the run reddened two (`the_panel_chamfer_rule` also
  pins Vardr Labs' square, as T1's K3 had shown), widened and re-run; A5 first failed to COMPILE (the wrong red: T3 had
  removed the `clip` import the sabotage needed) and was rewritten as a `.background(..., RoundedCornerShape(50))`.
- **T4's J10 survived once** (the scroll edge set to the default background): iOS 27 cannot tell default from
  transparent; a source pin was added to `testTheBarGroundPerTheme` and J10 re-ran EXACT.
- **The plan's sabotage method was not followed as written**: it named one two-lane runner; each task ran its own (T1 in
  the checkout, one row at a time; T2, T3, T4, T5 and both fix lanes in throwaway worktrees under `/private/tmp`, removed
  after). Every row asserted its anchor, had zero compile errors at its final run and was restored and checked with `cmp`.
- **The fix wave's F7 row first ran BROADER**: renaming Expenses' scaffold call also reddened five older tab-root pins;
  replaced by GroupPage losing its inset (two reds, both guards that read the inset). Both runs are logged.
- **The Android fixer's first commit missed a pin** (a4366c8 ran only the guard classes; ThemeMotionTest still pinned the
  old rounded hero string): 1ac1173 moved it. The whole JVM suite ran green after.
- **The iOS fixer's first commit took more than it meant**: `git commit -- <paths>` committed the working-tree
  ThemeArtTests, which already held F9 and F10; it re-staged the intended blob and amended before anything else touched
  the branch, nothing pushed.
- **A near miss, not an incident**: T4's first look launch on the throwaway `d214-look` ran about 2 minutes WITHOUT
  `--emulators` while the app showed "Signed in" (an account from earlier looks). The app was uninstalled at once. After
  the founder's `gcloud auth login`, Cloud Logging for skipti-26 showed NO entries at all on 2026-10-16 (no Function call,
  no Cloud Run request; the same query returns the usual entries on earlier days), and an emulator-issued token cannot
  pass production's signature check: no production contact. run-common.md and CLAUDE.md section 10.2 now require an
  uninstall before a look that signs in and `--emulators` (or a proof arg) on every look launch.

**Decisions made for the founder** (the plan's DECIDED lines and WORKLOG NOW item 8; each overturnable in one line):
1. **The meter is money marked paid over money that had to move**, per currency, in core: "72% settled" means 72% of
   what was owed has been marked paid. It rises with every payment and reaches 100 exactly when nobody owes anybody; a
   group where everyone paid their own share reads 100%.
2. **One block per currency**, the settlement currency first, then by code; no FX, no combined percentage.
3. **The currency step counts only once a currency is stored**, though an unset currency resolves to the region's: the
   step is one tap, and counting it unset would make it a step nobody does. The app lock's default (two minutes) counts
   on a phone with a lock, so the endowed progress is real.
4. **Norse's 24 runes spaced evenly round the whole circle and centred on the radius** (his E4 board drew it so; the
   Look Book's 2.2 px spacing left a gap); lit = round half up of 24 x done / total, so 6 of 7 lights 21.
5. **The group's next card records in place** ("Settle", "Settling") through Settle up's own function, and prints the
   section 11.6 sentence "Marks this as paid here. It does not move money."
6. **A compact primary button** (no full width, label 15, padding 16 / 10, the same looks, shape and dim) for both next
   cards: the Look Book's button is a small trailing one and the style was full width only.
7. **A milestone shows for 14 days from its reaching**, no "seen" mark, no new stored state, every member's phone the
   same; the board's words "Since 2 Mar 2026. Rare, and only once."
8. **Celebration particles in the theme's `ring` colour** (the Look Book's fixed #45E6B0 / #5AD0F2 are `ring`'s dark
   values and vanish on the light dawn), and its second line in `text`: textDim measures 3.75 to 4.36 over the page
   dimmed to 0.22 (art.py 23).
9. **"Golden for Norse"** read as the approved board draws it: the number in bone #EDE6D3, the gold in the segmented
   silver-to-gold bar. One line to him in case he meant the number itself.

**Findings that shaped it:**
- **The double record**: Android's next card and Settle up both cleared their "settling" flag before the asynchronous
  reload, so a second tap in that window recorded the same payment again. iOS's Settle up reloaded in the same main
  turn but had no guard of its own. Both shells now hold one payment in a latch until the reloaded page moves on.
- **A negative settlement** (core's `money_make` accepts one; a synced record from another phone is the realistic
  source) gave negative basis points, `u32::try_from` failed with `Overflow`, and both shells' group page failed to
  load where it had loaded before E4.
- **Android closes the group when you switch tabs**, so a settle made in Settle up never played on return; iOS keeps
  the page alive and played it. Both now keep a per-group memory in the shell.
- **Compose drops a fully transparent node from the accessibility tree**, and the words' live region started at alpha 0
  and never changed text: TalkBack might never have announced it. An opaque node filled once per play replaced it.
- **The meter is on nets and the count on pairwise debts**: after Kiran's 900 Flat 4B reads "₹450.00 still to settle"
  beside "2 payments to go" (Meera to you 450 and Kiran to Meera 450). Both are true; section 4 and a line for the
  founder.
- **Settle up's "all settled" is the viewer's entries being empty** (D-182), so it can say "Flat 4B is all settled" while
  the group's meter reads 75%. Pre-existing; E4 made "settled" a defined word. Section 4.

**Findings that shaped it:**
- **Android dropped the first gesture on the slider** after Appearance opened (the look: a tap 3 of 3, a 150 ms press,
  a 500 ms drag, a tap after a tap on empty ground, a tap after changing the mode: 9 of 9 left `textSize` unchanged in
  `shared_prefs`; the second gesture always wrote; iOS took the first every time). The look suspected `focusable()` or
  the fixed-`Density` provider; the fixer reproduced it 2 of 2 with one scripted `adb input tap`
  (`.drafts/d222/fix/android/repro.sh`) and found neither: a `pointerInput` block starts lazily on the FIRST pointer event
  and gets that event as soon as it first suspends, and the block's `launch { detectTapGestures }` and
  `launch { detectHorizontalDragGestures }` were dispatched, so at that moment neither detector was waiting and the down
  was missed. Both now start `CoroutineStart.UNDISPATCHED`: the first tap after opening wrote 3 of 3 in Aurora and once
  each in Norse and Vardr Labs, the first drag wrote on every fresh open, and a slow 3 s first drag stepped -2, -1, 0, 1.
- **Android's drag ended at its first step** (T3's look): a step changes the root's font scale, `LocalDensity` changes,
  and Compose restarts a `pointerInput` handler on a density change, cancelling the gesture mid-drag. The slider now
  provides its own `Density(LocalDensity.current.density)` (everything in it is dp; its A's are fixed anyway). After it,
  five swipes ran end to end both ways. iOS's `DragGesture` is unaffected (T2: five full drags, each one gesture).
- **iOS's Norse mode control was dimmed twice** (look F1, Norse page box means): the chosen segment against the track
  1.00 on iOS against Android's 1.047 (the model: surface and accentSoft each at 0.45 over bg), the chosen word "Dark"
  1.84:1 against 3.68:1 on its segment, the other words 1.44:1 against 2.15:1. `.opacity` on the HStack was not a
  compositing group, so the surface pill at 0.45 lay over the track at 0.45 and vanished, and the disabled `.plain`
  buttons dimmed the words again. Only Norse differed (chosen against track elsewhere 1.169 / 1.169 Aurora light, 1.188 /
  1.166 Aurora dark, 1.121 / 1.121 Vardr Labs light, 1.055 / 1.055 Vardr Labs dark).
- **The slider's ends and thumb** (look F4): at -2 the accent fill ran from the track's start to the thumb's centre, so a
  gold tab showed beside the Norse diamond's left tip, about 2.5 pt either side of the tip at the track's edges, on both;
  at +3 the unfilled track showed past the right tip (iOS 0.67 pt on the centre row, 1.00 at the track's top edge;
  Android 0 and 0.38). The diamond measured 18.67 tip to tip on iOS against 19.43 on Android, the ring through the tip
  2.67 against 3.43; the round thumb 20.0 against 20.19.
- **The mode pill's inset** (review I-1): iOS padded the chosen pill 4 inside its third (`W/3 - 8`) and the words 8,
  Android padded the row 4 and filled each segment (`(W - 8)/3`), as the Look Book's `.mode` (padding 3 px, three equal
  columns, no gap): about 5 pt narrower on a 362 pt track, the outer words about 2.7 pt off.
- **The fixed Android track** (review I-2): Android drew the track at a fixed 40 dp with the segment
  `heightIn(min = 48)` and the pill `heightIn(min = 32)`, so past about 32 dp of text the row stopped matching iOS's
  `max(48, text + 16)` and past 40 the pill outgrew its track.

**Mistakes and corrections, recorded plainly:**
- **Two fixers' `git commit -- <path>` swept extra hunks of their own files.** `git commit -- <paths>` commits the whole
  working file and ignores a partial index. The iOS fixer's first commit took the S2, S7 and S8 hunks with X1 to X4, and
  the Android fixer's first commit took every hunk of its three groups; each caught it before any push and before any
  other commit, checked that HEAD was still its own, and amended to the intended hunks (the Android fixer rebuilt the
  index blob as HEAD~1 plus group 1's hunks, then staged groups 2 and 3 by hunk with `git apply --cached` and committed
  from the index). No other agent's work was swept. Each intermediate Android commit compiled and passed its classes in
  the throwaway worktree (c6a5b48 and 6d31a24: Appearance 27, You 8, TypeTheme 29). The lesson is now in
  `run-common.md`.
- **One iOS look launch went through the simulator tool's `launch` action**, which passes no arguments, so the fix
  wave's first look launch ran about a second without `--emulators` (a Debug build without it talks to production
  skipti-26) on a fresh install with no account: nothing signed in, no sign-in. It was terminated at once; every later
  launch used `xcrun simctl launch ... --emulators`, and `run-common.md` now forbids the tool's `launch` for looks.

  refinement; T2 and T3 built the refined rule and the guards ban a literal "INR" in `SampleLine` (iOS) and test the
  region goldens (Android, row A13).
- **The plan's sabotage premise for A12** was wrong for Kotlin (above).
- **T2's sample read INR** for the simulator's leftover preference, not a code fault (above).
- **The machine was overloaded during the fix wave**: the load average reached 300 to 600 while the iOS sabotage lane, a

**Decisions made for the founder** (each overturnable in one line):
- From the plan (its DECIDED lines, `plan-report.md`, WORKLOG item 10):
  1. **The who-owes line** names the first two people of `overview.people` in the hero's currency, in core's order
     (largest first, D-180), phrased by sign ("Meera owes you ₹3,050.00", "You owe Sam ₹560.00", lower case after the
     separator), not drawn in the settled hero. Reason: SPEC 11.4 asks the balance to decompose "sorted by magnitude";
     the People list right below names everyone.
  2. **The ledger card's line** reads "Owed", "You owe" or "Settled" with the amount from core in the money colour; the
     meter takes the line's currency's block, else the first (the settlement currency's); **no meter on a group with no
     expense or settlement**, because "0% settled" would describe a debt that never existed.
  3. **Lately shows the newest 3 entries** of D-189's feed, hidden when empty, never marking the feed seen; rows open the
     expense; the row gap 11, not the Look Book's 10, so stacked Norse diamonds clear (measured 10.3 pt / 9.9 dp).
  4. **One relative-time rule on both shells**: "now" (a negative delta too), "N min", "N h", "1 day", "N days", then the
     day and month; Recent activity uses it too. The two system formatters worded the same moment differently.
  5. **Two columns, one at accessibility text sizes** (iOS `isAccessibilitySize`; Android the app's existing switch,
     now `TextSize.stacks`).
  6. **A drawn Lucide `inbox`** on both empty states rather than dropping iOS's icon; Home's empty title at 20 / 600.

**Controller decisions** (from the reports, reviews and looks; `minors.md`, `views-extra.md`, the fix lists, the
ledger):
- **A1, A2, A3** as above; A2 resolves the plan's residue line on the shorter empty copy, A1 its "Lately has no See all".
- **Lately is read only when Home has groups, on both shells** (T4's `ensureSelf()` finding, sent to T3 as a twin note):
  every entry is a group's, so nothing is lost, and a fresh phone's Home never writes.
- **A Lately failure goes into Home's one read** on both shells (views-extra 2 allowed either): Home's error line, the
  last good Home kept, no state assigned before both reads succeed.
- **AM4 kept as an equivalent mutant**: Kotlin's `maxOf(nowMs - atMs, 0L)` cannot go red (a signed negative delta is
  already below a minute), kept as the readable twin of Swift's UInt64 guard, where it matters.
- **T4's M2 read as Home**: "Balance's own empty title" in the plan is Home's (the Balance tab), moved on both shells;
  `BalanceScreen`'s proof-only empty state stays body 20 on both (twins agree; section 4).
- **The card's accessibility label in core's spoken money** (SPEC 11.7, D-221), not Design 4's formatted example.
- **`LedgerCard(name:nets:blocks:) { size in tile }`** rather than Design 9's `(name:line:basisPoints:)`: the card still
  takes its tile as a slot and any ordered input, so "Just me" can be prepended later with no card change.
- **The text-size asymmetry kept**: iOS xxxLarge (about 1.35x) draws two columns where Android's 1.24 and above draws
  one; that is the house mapping (`TextSize.STACKS_AT` 1.15) and decision 5.
- **Routed, not fixed here**: the Aurora dark glass card stroke and the Android Aurora dark bar wash-out to D-226; the
  expense "Added by" stamp's wording to D-225; Android's Expenses, Groups and Settle up tabs losing their scroll offset
  (pre-existing) to D-225.

**Findings that shaped it:**
- **The shared read swallowed vault errors** (T1's review): `ActivityFeed.load` used `try?` on vault reads, and Home is
  the launch path, so a vault that will not open would read as "nothing yet" (CLAUDE.md 10.1). Both shells now throw,
  with a behavioural negative each (a corrupt group list on iOS, a store whose vault will not open on Android).
- **Reading Lately writes on a fresh phone** (T4): `store.activity` calls `ensureSelf()`. Gated on groups, both shells.
- **Android's Activity-to-expense Back** (review I2): the `"expense/"` route went back with `route = null`, so an expense
  opened from the whole-ledger Activity, or from a group's Recent activity since D-196, returned to Home.
- **Android's Home forgot its place** (look F6): the `ScrollState` lived inside Home, which leaves composition on a push;
  three new entry points below the fold made it show.
- **The Norse ornament hand-over** (look F5): iOS draws the ornament row in the scroll content with a negative top
  padding, and SwiftUI's padded frame never goes below zero height, so iOS's content starts max(15 + above, 24) under
  the title, then its stack spacing; Android's scaffold was linear (24 + above - 8, then 14). Measured: Balance empty
  32.0 / 34.67, Home with data +1.33.
- **"See all" in `groundAccent`** (look F1): #4D615E in Aurora light, exactly `textDim`, inside a card where "People in
  X" is #0B7A5F.
- **The Groups card** (T4, look F2): 136.0 pt against 140.19 dp in all five sets; the link's ink 2.4 lower on Android.
- **Android's empty state inset 32** (look F3): the scaffold's 16 plus `EmptyState`'s 16, so the text was 347 dp wide
  against 370 pt and "app." wrapped alone in Aurora and Norse.
- **Android's section labels** (look F4): iOS's `section()` adds 4 above Home's labels; hero to "Your ledgers" 21.67 /
  17.90, Lately to "People" 21.67 / 17.91.
- **The re-look** (R1 to R4): the photo card 190.67 / 176.76 (iOS a 2 pt stack between band, title and detail, then 10
  above the link; Android 12 above the title, 0, then 2); Norse Expenses with data 1.86 dp low (26.33 / 28.19 to the
  chips); Android's restore within 76 dp of Home's end lands 76.19 dp higher (the tab bar's height: `tabBarPx` a plain
  `remember`, 0 on the first frame back, so the kept offset clamps); iOS's Lately words stale while Home stays alive
  ("3 min" at 06:53 and 06:58 where Activity said "6 min").

**The founder's ask**: item 12 of his feedback round (2026-10-13), "a nice animation showing the confirmation of that
action like an animated check mark"; the Look Book's L48 (the Haptics row), L49 (the big check, Norse's turning Futhark,
his canvas pick Q12 a) and L50 (the toast); the feedback-round spec's E3 scope (the shared component in two sizes, wired
to every action the audit found silent; the three haptics); and his rule of 2026-10-15 that the two phones look
identical. No L-D217 row was routed to E3.

**Decisions made for the founder** (each overturnable in one line):
- From the plan (its DECIDED lines, `plan-report.md`, WORKLOG item 11):
  1. **Haptics on by default**: both platforms ship haptics on with the system switch as the master (UIKit's generators
     are silenced by System Haptics; Android's `performHapticFeedback` with no flag honours touch feedback), the Look
     Book's row describes a working feature, and the friction audit named haptics the cheapest "feels alive" fix.
     Turning the switch on plays one success; off plays nothing; Reduce Motion never silences a haptic.
  2. **The warning plays when a destructive or irreversible question OPENS**, never on the final tap (the only "before"
     with a pause in it); instant, redoable actions (sign out, remove a picture, "Use letter", dismiss an invitation,
     sync off, ask to remove) get none; the owner transfer and the username change count as irreversible.
  3. **The first group is an overlay that ends by itself** (E4's 3.6 s, the content dimmed, the bar and + bright), not a
     screen with a Done button: no tap added to creating a group. Signed in, joined and erased are screens (they
     already ended on a screen or an alert the person dismisses).
  4. **The erase alert becomes the big screen** with the same one-tap OK.
  5. **The check in `accent` in every theme** as the Look Book draws it (Vardr Labs' steel, not the ring's cyan), the
     circle from 12 o'clock like the completion ring (the Look Book's 3 o'clock is SVG's default).
  6. **The toast lasts 3.0 s**, replaced at once by a newer one, no queue (nothing waits: GUARANTEES #2).
  7. **Add expense closes at once**: the 0.6 s "Saved" hold goes and the toast confirms; Profile's never-resetting
     "Saved" label goes.
  8. **The check is 104** in E4's 137 ring box (the picture's size inside D-221's ring, so Norse reuses the ring's radius
     60 and size 14); the toast is the Look Book's px times 1.28 (S1's factor).
  9. **The big success at the pop** (0.7 s, the tick landed), at once in still mode; a success within 1.0 s of another is
     skipped (the last settle would otherwise buzz twice).
  10. **No milestone haptic** (the card shows on every visit for 14 days) and **no moment for the delete-account
      request** (a goodbye).
  11. **Android below API 30** plays CONTEXT_CLICK for success and LONG_PRESS for warning (CONFIRM and REJECT arrive with
      API 30, read in the installed SDK's `api-versions.xml`); no VIBRATE permission.
  12. **Lucide `vibrate`** for the Haptics tile, copied verbatim (the Look Book's six-ray drawing is not a Lucide icon).
- From this run (WORKLOG items 23 and 24):
  23. **The done overlay's dim covers the page's ground as well as its content on both phones, as iOS draws it**; the
      tab bar and the + stay bright. E4's celebration keeps its content-only dim, which is already the same on both
      (narrowed after the fix: iOS's `CelebrationDim` sits inside the Aurora background, so iOS's ground does not dim
      there either; the Android lane measured it and left it). Reason: the look found Android's bright Aurora ground and
      "Settle up" showing through the moment's words; iOS is the scale.
  24. **Where the shells behaved differently, both take the quieter behaviour**: the first-group buzz only when the
      overlay is seen, a check screen buzzes once per moment, a red-button removal screen warns once per presentation
      (not again on Back), one announcement per moment. Reason: twins must match, and a repeated buzz or warning is
      noise.

**Controller decisions** (from the reports, reviews and looks; `views-extra.md`, `sites-extra.md`, `fix-list.md`, the
ledger):
- **One success gate per shell, applied once** (views-extra 1): iOS in `DoneCenter.success`, made one per app by
  `SuccessGate.shared` (sites-extra 9); Android in `Haptics.play`, which is already one per app. Reason: the two shells
  had put the gate in different places, and a gate applied twice, or once per centre, buzzes differently.
- **Android converts its clocks in one place** (views-extra 2, `MomentFrames`), tested as pure functions.
- **Only the owner transfer warns among role changes** (sites-extra 1): making or removing an admin can be undone
  (Design 3).
- **The username toast posts only after a real save, outside the sign-in flow** (sites-extra 2): the two "already set on
  another phone" ways out saved nothing; inside sign-in the signed-in screen follows.
- **A declined removal request posts nothing** (sites-extra 3); **a blank expense note is left out of the toast's line**
  (sites-extra 4); **the joined page's check is centred above the heading** (sites-extra 5).
- **iOS's warning table lists its own files** (sites-extra 6): 10 iOS files and 9 Android files, every destructive
  confirmation on each shell in its table (the guards fail a new one); the briefs' 11 and 12 named more files than the
  tree has.
- **The erased screen is a cover on iOS and replaces the root on Android** (sites-extra 7, Design 8's "over the root"):
  same flag, same one tap; HomeShell leaves composition on Android while it shows (harmless: the vault is wiped).
- **The add-person toast clear of the keyboard** (sites-extra 8): measured in the look, 15.8 pt / 16.0 dp above it.
- **You's own overlay on Android** (T6): You is a route that replaces the tabs on Android, where on iOS it is pushed
  inside a tab's stack under the shell's overlay; without it a first group made from You would expire unseen.
- **iOS is the scale for measured layout** (fix-list), unless the plan's Design names a value: F5's toast lift, F8's
  flexible top and F10's gap all move Android.
- **F9 fixed for the erased title only**: `GreedyText` is there to reuse; a sweep of every multi-line title is its own
  unit (section 4).

**Findings that shaped it:**
- **Android's toast was silent to TalkBack** (review I1): its live region sat on the visible text inside a
  `graphicsLayer` whose alpha starts at 0, so Compose drops the node and the region first appears rather than changes;
  E4's S9 had fixed the same form on the celebration. Its first guard passed with the feature broken (a string check).
- **Gate placement differed** (T2 review): iOS gated success in the centre, Android in `Haptics.play`, so a local
  centre on iOS had its own gate (T3 review) and iOS's Haptics row bypassed it (review M1).
- **A big moment while HomeShell is away** (T4 review): Android dropped it after 3.6 s unseen; You's overlay closes it.
- **The first group's check under the closing sheet** (look F1): iOS posted while the New group sheet still covered the
  shell, and the first frame without the sheet already showed the finished check.
- **The dim** (look F2): iOS's whole page dims, ground included (light pages near white); Android's dimmed only the
  content (the ground behind the words #E9ECEB on iOS, #DCE5E2 on Android in Aurora light).
- **A second big moment** (look F3, F4): iOS showed it already drawn; both snapped the page bright for a frame (hero luma
  212 to 90 on iOS, 213 to 64 on Android).
- **The toast's gap to the +** (look F5): Android's bar row is 76 dp to iOS's 70 (D-219 residue), and the toast is placed
  from the row's bottom: Aurora 25.7 pt / 20.2 dp, Norse diamond 12.3 / 6.9.
- **Android's toast over Add expense** (look F6): the shell's toast drew on top of Add's primary button for up to 3 s
  where iOS's sheet covers it.
- **The last settle** (look F7): Android showed the settle toast for about 1 s and began the celebration at 1.35 s, iOS
  within about 0.2 to 0.4 s.
- **The check screens' place** (look F8): check top 316 pt (signed in) and 294 pt (erased) on iOS against 186 dp on
  Android: iOS centres between `Spacer(minLength: 40)` and `Spacer()`, Android had a fixed 24 dp.
- **The erased title** (look F9): "This phone's ledger / is erased" on iOS, "This phone's ledger is / erased" on Android
  with about 362 of room on both: iOS's text system pushes a word down so a last line never holds one word alone.
- **The Haptics row** (look F10): 56.3 pt against 53.3 dp, iOS's VStack spaced 2 where Android's Column had none.

Look Book's S2 rows L67 to L76 (L72 went to C2); the D-217 and D-218 looks' twin differences that no other unit owned;

**Decisions made for the founder** (each overturnable in one line; the plan's DECIDED lines, `plan-report.md`):
1. **A drawn switch on both phones** (`ThemeSwitch`, iOS's 51 x 31 proportions, the theme's pill and thumb shapes,
   Material's dim thumb when off so the off state holds 3:1 without colour alone), replacing every `Toggle` and Material
   `Switch` in scope, E3's Haptics row included (E3 left the switch to S2).
2. **Every choice a form makes opens a pushed choice page** (Category, Sub-category, Group, Split type, Paid by, and App
   lock per Q15 a): a popup menu is each platform's own window and can never look the same, and a pushed list is Apple's
   own pattern for form choices; the tap count is the same.
3. **The currency pill, Settles in and Default currency open C2's currency list page** directly; the quick menus, the
   chips and the "All currencies" buttons go (the list's "Common" section holds the same codes).
4. **The Erase row opens a page** holding today's explanation and button, whose alert is unchanged: one step added, none
   removed, and the chevron means a push as on every other row.
5. **The jailbreak or root warning moves to the top of Security**, in its own card, so it is not lost under a row.
6. **Six emoji columns**, not iOS's eight: eight gives 34 pt cells on an iPhone 17 and 29 dp on a 360 dp phone, under
   both platforms' minimums; six gives 48.3 pt and 41.3 dp (art.py 43).
7. **S1's `SettingsRow` is a call of the shared `ListRow`**; iOS footers at 13 move to the caption's 14.
8. **A licence's page has no body title** on iOS (the bar names it; D-217's rule that a pushed page draws no header).
9. **iOS's in-scope `Form`s become list cards** (Group settings, People, Add expense, New group, Your name): a system
   section cannot be notched or squared, and its 25 pt corners were a twin difference (A1).
10. **Summaries**: Your phones shows the active phones' names; App lock shows the timeout's own words or "Needs a phone
    lock" (no "Face ID": the kind differs per phone and the passcode also opens it).
11. **Decision 25**: the "Added by" time follows the phone's own 12 or 24-hour setting on both phones; it is the
    person's preference, apart from the en-US / en-IN date axis.
12. **Decision 26**: every section label takes `textDim` on both phones: a label names what follows and is not faint
    text; Android's shared `SectionLabel` already defaults to it; the two tokens are equal in Aurora, so no floor moves.
13. **Decision 27**: the recovery screen's confirmed erase signs out of the cloud session first on both phones, as the
    deliberate erases do: the account's owner key lives in the vault, so a session left behind would point at a ledger
    that no longer exists; the person signs in again afterwards. Both sign-outs are local, so it cannot block the erase
    offline (the follow-ups' review).

  its text line, about 20 high, because the padding sat outside the field. Fixed in the next task of each lane before
  any form used it (T4: `@FocusState` and a whole-area gesture; T5: padding inside the decoration box), each guarded
  (I23, AF1).
- **The swallowed pins** (T4 review): a comment added inside a Swift array literal took the two entries after it with it,
  so `testEveryPanelTakesTheShapeFromTheOneDecision` silently stopped checking ExpenseListView.swift and SettleScreen.swift.
  T6 put the comment on its own line and AXP proves the entries bite again.

  `try?` on iOS, so a failed erase looked like nothing happened on the one screen with no other exit. iOS fixed it in T6
  with A9; Android in the fix wave (final review I1).

  after boot, an I/O error) put a healthy ledger behind a screen whose only action erased it. The founder's A9 answers it:
  Try again first, erasing the last resort.

  in Aurora where the two tokens are equal; decision 26.

   colour). Every other floor holds at the Look Book's strength (text 11.38, textDim 5.31, accent 6.23; art.py 48).

6. **Decision 28**: every themed card border is drawn inside its shape on both phones, so a card's drawn size equals its
