7. **Decision 29**: the Norse hero's outer edge is drawn on the straight sides only, as every Norse card and photo frame,
   on both phones: Q18 read as one rule; lit diagonals on the hero beside cards without them would be two styles.
8. **A1** (the controller, after Task 0): iOS's glass is the reference and changes no pixel; Android renders iOS's
   measured #666C72-looking edge, `glassRimDark` 0.35 from art.py 53.
9. **A2** (the controller, after Task 0; kept at the final review and in the fix list; the dim replaced in fix wave 2,
   decision 13): Android dims the page's own pixels
   under its Aurora dark top bar to 0.4, the largest dim that holds the title at 4.5:1 over WHITE content (0.41 gives
   4.47; art.py 54). Over the same light button Android's title then reads 7.58:1 and iOS's 4.77 (the look's box; Task
   0's box read 4.99 over the same pixels): both hold the floor, and they differ because the floor is set by the worst
   content Android can scroll under its bar, while iOS's bar is the system's own material. Copying iOS's 4.77 here would
   fail over white.
10. **The watermark follows the Look Book: not clipped at the top** (the controller, at the fix list): the Look Book's
    `font: 92px/1` puts the ink about 10 px inside the hero, so it does not clip either; art.py 46's "clipped by the hero"
    line and the plan's look item were wrong (final review M5).
11. **T3's shared blur and the root placement of `LocalArtBackdrop`**: accepted by the T3 review and the whole-branch
    review on their measurements and reasons (above).
12. **Decision 30**: iOS's Norse page glow keeps its 1-step bands (visible only at x 16 contrast; Android's is
    dithered): four dithering attempts left the rings, and the two that would work cost 9 to 22 MB of memory for a
    difference invisible at normal contrast. Residue.
13. **F2, the Darken cap at iOS's band colour** (the controller, fix wave 2's brief, adopting the option the wave 1
    fixer found): it matches iOS's colour and keeps a floor (5.2:1 over every content), which was the reason for the
    dim; light content under the bar flattens to one colour, as iOS's material flattens it.
14. **Decision 31**: Android's Aurora scroll frame time stays about +4.5 ms at the 90th percentile over 87b1be8 on the
    emulator (28 against 23.5 ms), checked on a real Android at the 0.5.0 release gate. Two fixes were built and
    measured and neither moved it (the blur's own copy at 15 and 7.5 fps; 950dfe0 reverted in 389332b); the cost is
    each card drawing the blurred art while a scroll is in flight, and the remaining options cost memory (a bitmap per
    card) or freeze the art during a scroll. An emulator's software path is not a phone's GPU, so the real number decides
    whether a unit is owed.
15. **Decision 32**: Android's Aurora dark bar band stays the flat #53686A it was matched to. The re-look found iOS's
    band is not flat (#516567 at one end to #55716F at the other, #56706F beside the title); Android's colour lies inside
    that range, and the title holds 5.25:1 (iOS 4.78). iOS's band is the system material and moves with what scrolls
    under it; chasing its one pixel beside the title would cost Android contrast for no visible gain.

**Brief values corrected by the tree:**
- **`glassRimDark` 0.03** (plan, art.py 51): a wrong model of iOS's rim; 0.35 from the measured pixels (section 53).
- **The plan's per-card blur**: measured at 150 ms at the 90th percentile; replaced by one shared blur (T3).
- **`HomeShell` providing `LocalArtBackdrop`**: the activity root (T3 concern 3).
- **"content 4 pt lower"** (the plan's look item 1): true on Groups only (above 8: 24 to 28); on Balance, Expenses and
  Settle up the content does not move on either phone, iOS by its formula max(15 + above, 8 + row) + spacing and
  Android by `contentShift` -1 to -5 taking its scaffold's 4 back (T1 report, final review M11; the look measured it).
- **The watermark "clipped by the hero"** (art.py 46, look item 4): not the Look Book's drawing (decision 10).
- **`CssGradient.unitPoints(160, geo.size)`** (the brief): T1's API takes `degrees:width:height:`; no overload added.
- **`notchEdge` as a `drawBehind`** (the brief): `drawWithContent`, so a photo cannot cover its own edge.
- **The A2 amendment's "blurred tab bar"**: the collapsed title is in the top bar (Task 0).

**Findings that shaped it:**
- **The rim model** (T1, from Task 0's pixels): iOS's overlay-blended rim composites over the material and the page art,
  not over a flat card colour, so it reads as a normal-blend white 0.35; the generator now derives it from the measure.
- **The design's blur cost** (T3): a blur layer per card, re-recorded per art frame and per scroll frame, measured 150
  ms at the 90th percentile; the shared quarter-size blur brought it to +3 to 4 ms over the base on the emulator.
- **The stacked star reading** (plan, art.py 47): each alone, as D-214 recorded its convention, the curtains hold textDim
  at 4.61 and a star at 4.54; a star ON the curtain's brightest stop reads textDim 2.98 with Q7 a and 3.06 in the old
  order. Today's page already failed a stacked reading; A does not open the gap; a page star strength that holds stacked
  is 0.006 (invisible). Built as he chose; the stacked reading is his question (section 4).
- **Decision 29 landed after T2 committed** (T2 report item 1, T2 review M1): the iOS hero kept its whole outline while
  Android followed the decision; the whole-branch review's one Important, closed by the iOS fix lane.
- **The Aurora dark glass fill cannot be matched by a film** (T3, the look): a = (card - ground) / (surface - ground)
  gives 1.33 / 1.40 / 1.67 over iOS's ground, over 1, because iOS's material lifts the card above `surface`.
- **The frame-time cost** (fix wave 2): the cards drawing the shared blurred art during scroll frames, not the blur
  pass (a blur at 15 or 7.5 fps changed nothing; cards not drawing it measured as the base).
- **iOS's Aurora dark band is a gradient** (the re-look): #4B5E61 at its edge, #516567 to #55716F across the title's
  line, #56706F beside the title, falling to #284548 at its foot; the look's single value (#53696A) was its edge
  colour. Android's Darken cap is flat by construction (decision 32).
- **`testTheSwitchThumbSlides` (D-225) went red under load** in four sabotage runs (load 60 to 143 with the other lane
  or a Gradle run; green alone, in both full green runs and in every rerun): D-225's own residue item, seen again.

**Mistakes and corrections, recorded plainly:**

  changed source and then restored the unsabotaged outputs from its build cache. The runner now deletes the worktree's
  own `android/.gradle` and `app/build` and runs `--no-watch-fs --no-build-cache --no-daemon` (T3's ran `--no-watch-fs
  --no-build-cache`); V6 and V7 then went EXACT. A doubt left outside the repo: the user-level Gradle build cache may map
  V7's sabotaged source to base outputs; it matters only if exactly that text is compiled again, and nothing outside the
  repo was touched.
- **T1 did not watch the test simulator between rows** and found AFAF4221 shut down at its end; T2 found why (below).
- **T2's runner wrote "passed 0"** for every row (its pass pattern expected the parallel format); the table below reads
  each row's own log (153 tests per row).
- **The look's fresh AVD came up without a display cutout** (every Android screen 27.8 dp higher than Task 0's); the
  look enabled the cutout overlay and matched Task 0's positions exactly before taking any after picture.
- **The plan's 0.03 rim and the watermark line** (above) were the planner's; both corrected in art.py, not in the shells.
- **Wave 1's frame-time diagnosis was wrong** (the blur pass per art frame): corrected in place above, from fix wave 2's
  measurements. The 15 fps copy built on it was reverted.
- **These records' first drafts** described wave 1's colour dim as what ships and the 15 fps copy as the next option
  (fix re-review minor 2); rewritten before the record, the dim kept as history.
- **art.out printed the reverted `ArtBlurCopy.EVERY = 2`** as a live value (fix re-review minor 3); the controller added

**The founder's ask** (2026-10-15, popups and chat): the cut S (direction C, "mature it", approved as v9); one icon per
theme (Aurora the approved cyan and steel, the default; Norse gold and silver on its ground; Vardr Labs steel blue and
deep cyan on its light ground); an in-app icon picker in Appearance with "Match theme" on by default; the status-bar
glyph replacing the bell; the assets in `brand/skipti-icon-assets` committed in D-216, the Affinity documents local, the
sources in `.drafts/d216/brand-src`; the unit after the Look Book units.

**Decisions made for the founder** (each overturnable in one line):
1. **All three Android launcher entries are aliases and MainActivity is none of them** (the plan's): MainActivity is the
   activity every alias opens and cannot be disabled, and only entries that can be disabled can switch. Cost: the update
   may drop the old home-screen icon once (residue (c), the What to Test line).
2. **The icon changes only when the person leaves Appearance, and only if different** (the plan's): iOS shows a system
   alert on every change, with no public way around it, and needs the app active; three theme taps would be three
   alerts. Leaving is the end of the choosing, so the alert answers what the person just did, at most once a visit.
3. **A switch plus three always-live rows** (the plan's): the founder's words are a switch "on by default"; rows that
   stay live (a tap is a choice and turns matching off) avoid a dimmed, dead state.
4. **The picker sits after "Light or dark" and before "Text size"** (the plan's): theme, mode and icon are the look;
   text size and haptics follow. Both shells draw it inside the Light or dark item, as Haptics sits inside Text size,
   so the settings map and its tests are unchanged.
5. **The previews keep the icon's own rounded square in every theme** (0.225 of the side, Apple's ratio; the plan's):
   an icon keeps its shape, and S1's theme tiles would draw it as a Norse diamond.
6. **Lucide's bell is removed** (the plan's): it drew only the notification icon, and NOTICE must say exactly what
   ships.
7. **The sources and the glyph's generator stay local** (A1, A2: the founder's own wording read as written), with
   `brand/make_icon_resources.sh` committed so the resources stay reproducible from a clone. The plan had decided to
   commit them; one line overturns it.
8. **Decision 33**: Android's caption loses its second sentence ("Some home screens remove the old icon; SKIPTI stays
   in your apps."), so both phones read only "Your icon changes when you leave this page.". The look found Launcher3
   keeps a placed home-screen icon through the switch (redrawn as the new icon, still opening the app, surviving a
   launcher restart), which is the plan's own rule for dropping it. OEM launchers are unverified (residue).
9. **Decision 34**: the icon changes when the Appearance page CLOSES, never when it is only covered (an alert, the app
   lock, a push). On Android the page also closes when the lock returns or a link opens; on iOS those only cover it. A
   tab switch cannot happen on either phone. No code change.
10. **T4's no-entry case** (the controller, from the T2 review): `current` reads null when no entry is on and the
    switcher then writes, so a phone can never be left with no launcher entry.

**Findings that shaped it:**
- **The assets were incomplete for three themes** (the planner): Android had one set of adaptive layers and iOS no dark
  Norse or Vardr Labs icon, and Apple needs every alternate icon's own dark and tinted entries; without Affinity there
  was no honest substitute (a flattened icon cannot be split into a background and a mark with its shadow).
- **The Play manifest check had no test** (the planner): it checked permissions only; the launcher contract and the
  five-fixture self-test came with this unit, and the existing permission rule got its first test.
- **iOS's alert and PrivacyCover** (the plan, confirmed by T3's look and the paired look): on iOS 26.1+ SpringBoard draws
  the alert and the app turns inactive behind it, so PrivacyCover covers the page; the app lock reacts only to the
  background and does not lock, even on "Immediately".
- **`DONT_KILL_APP` keeps the process on API 34** (T4's look and the paired look: the pid unchanged throughout), so the
  plan's contingency (switching at `MainActivity.onStop`) was not needed.
- **The golden table cannot see a wrong DEFAULT** (T4's row A8): every table row still passed; the manifest-reading
  test caught it.
- **The tab switch is not a path** (the whole-branch review and the look's F2): both phones hide or replace the tab bar
  on Appearance.

**The founder's ask** (WORKLOG item 13, session 4, and the run order he set on 2026-10-17): both bugs fixed in 0.5.0,

**Decisions made for the founder** (each overturnable in one line):
1. **The server derives places from the group's own log** (the design review, plan v2), not the phones adopting the
   server's id (item 13's first call): adopting it splits groups made under the old id. Read per request, not stored:
   no backfill, and no stored field to keep right.
2. **The creator place is `members[0]` of the creator's earliest create, by the server's `createdAt`, then the HLC**
   (plan v2): `createdAt` is set by the rules, so it is the order a phone cannot steer; core orders by HLC and the two
   differ only when the creator wrote two creates of one group.
3. **The `you` check widened in this unit** (plan v2 Design 4): it is the same root cause seen from the target's side.
4. **`owner` and `admins` keep their D-210 meaning** for 0.4.0 builds; `places` sits beside them.
5. **Decision 35**: the role-asking rule ignores a refresh that ends after sign-out or after its group left, and asks
   once more when the group changed while a refresh was in flight.
6. **Decision 36**: when the creator path and another member's accepted invite name one place, the invite wins.
7. **Decision 37**: the creator path holds only while no removal record ever named the place.
8. **Decision 38**: a failed role check is asked again after 15, 60 and 300 s, as well as on the next change or return
   to the app, on both phones; no polling loop.
9. **Decision 39**: while `places.owner` is empty, the Owner pill follows the account rule on both phones (display
   only, what 0.4.0 shows); admins and your own place stay by place.
10. **M-f: hide, not act**: a role holder by place with no claim on this phone gets no Make admin, Remove admin or Make
    owner (Remove and Ask unchanged), on both phones.
11. **The after-push refresh is awaited before the profile share** on both phones (T5's order, the controller's
    alignment of T4), so the share reads the fresh place.
12. **Decision 40**: a profile share that failed (the cloud's function was down) is retried after 15, 60 and 300 s on
    both phones, not only at the next return to the app; the same schedule as decision 38 keeps one rule.
13. **The re-review's I-2 is fixed, not recorded**: iOS gets Android's F2 and F3 lines (CLAUDE.md section 10: a twin
    difference is a defect).

**Brief values corrected by the tree:**
- **The plan's sabotage table put F1 to F3 in index.js**: `creatorPlaceOf` lives in groups.js, where they ran.
- **The design's eighth server row, "a contested place not skipped"**, was replaced by F8 (the creator still holds after
  a removal); the contested branch is exercised by the `groupRoles` test, not sabotaged (T1 review Minor 9).
- **Two rewritten tests foreseen; six more assertions changed** (the `roleIds` comparison above).
- **Design 5 kept no participant-id fall-back on the phones**; decision 39 adds one, for the owner test only.
- **Design 8's after-push refresh** was detached in T4's first diff; awaited on both, as T5 built it.
- **v1's I1 to I3 were not rerun after T4**: decision 35 restructured `RoleAsking`, so I3's anchor no longer exists;
  their tests still pass, and I10 to I12 (A10 to A12) sabotage the new code.
- **Names**: `ProfileShare.known` (T5) became `GroupRoles.yourPlaces`, iOS's name, in the fix wave; `selfPlace`'s Swift
  labels come in another order than Kotlin's positional arguments, with the same meaning.

**Findings that shaped it:**
- **The server's id cannot simply win on the phones** (plan v1): records written under it are refused in groups made
  under the older id (`NonMemberPayer`).
- **A copied participant id could take a place** (the design review, by reading; now a refusal test).
- **Every create op lists the creator first** (T1, by reading the history), so `members[0]` is the creator's place.
- **A creator's late create could make two accounts unremovable** (the T1 review): decision 36; and **a removed
  creator's place could come back through any phone's `addMember`**: decision 37.
- **The owner read as a member while the cloud did not know its place yet** (T4's concern, the whole-branch review's I1,
  the look's item 4: 1.2 to 1.6 s warm, about 10 s cold): decision 39.
- **A failed role call with Firestore still up was never asked again** (the look's F1, 68 to 110 s until the app came
  back to the foreground): decision 38.
- **F2 and F3 were Android's alone in the look**; the Android fixer found iOS has the same trigger code and its page
  turned live because the shared profile arrived as a fresh record, which bumps the revision. The re-look proved it:
  with the Functions down, iOS's page stayed local after its records and roles arrived (R1), so iOS needed the lines
  (the follow-up's D and E).
- **A timer can outlive its asker** (the re-review's I-1): decision 38's retry needed decision 35's "only an answer
  that counted" rule too (the follow-up's A).

**Mistakes and corrections, recorded plainly:**
- **T1's CLOUD-SECURITY paragraph said the creator "picks its place once, before anyone else can be a member"**: nothing
  enforced it (the security review's finding); replaced in 8cbc479 by the honest account and decision 36.
- **T1's report did not say F8 replaced the design's contested-place row** (review Minor 9); said in the fix report and
  here.
- **The T1 fix's CLOUD-SECURITY sentence "no removal power over the place"** overstated the test (the owner removes the
  joiner); corrected in 9e1b41f.
- **iOS's after-push refresh first ran detached** (T5's concern 1): aligned to Android's awaited order before T4
  committed; I9 rerun.
- **The fix wave's iOS decision 38 tests were rewritten to Android's names after the stub run**, so their red is shown
  by rows F2 to F4, not by a stub run.
- **The Functions fixer's first emulator run failed** "Unable to locate a Java Runtime" (`JAVA_HOME` is set only in the
  login shell, CLAUDE.md 7); run again through `zsh -lic`.
- **The fix wave's decision 38 left a hole on both shells** (re-review I-1) and **iOS without the F2 and F3 twins**
  (I-2, which the iOS fixer had flagged as a concern): fixed in the follow-up wave, each with a sabotage row.
- **The JVM tally is carried forward, then re-run after the gate**: the gate's `make android-test` leg took 8 s and wrote
  no XML; the newest XML (all 52 at 15:08:23Z) was the Android follow-up fixer's whole-suite run in the checkout, 24 s
  before 1e9c6f4 committed, and `android/` is unchanged from 1e9c6f4 to 7cb11d3. But f705da5 then changed three files in
  `ios/Skipti/App`, a declared input of the JVM tests (several read the Swift sources), and the leg still wrote nothing,
  so the gate's artifacts do not show the JVM suite run on the gated Swift. After the gate, on the same tree, the
  records drafter forced it (`cleanTestPlayDebugUnitTest testPlayDebugUnitTest --no-build-cache --no-watch-fs`): all 52
  XML at 15:31:14Z, 886 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Why the gate's leg did not rerun on a changed declared input was not
  investigated (the build cache is on in `android/gradle.properties`).

**Process notes:**
- **Parallel agents in one checkout, on disjoint trees** (T1, T2 and T3; then T4 and T5; then the three fixers; then the
  two follow-up fixers):
  none stashed, reset or restored, each checked that the index held only its own paths before committing, and every
  commit holds only its own lane's paths. The Functions sabotage runners edit the checkout's `firebase/` files in place, one row
  at a time, restoring each and checking it with `filecmp` (no other lane touched `firebase/`).
- **The machine was loaded** during T2's look (load average 225 to 300 with the lanes and other agents running), so
  simulator taps lagged.
- **The looks talked to nothing real**: `--emulators` on iOS, one proof arg or `--emulators` alone on Android, the
  Firebase CLI's stored credentials invalid ("Authentication Error"), `otherphone.mjs` against the local emulators.

**Re-look** (`.superpowers/sdd/d227/relook-report.md`; branch at 4db75c5, after the fix wave and before the follow-up;
the same throwaway devices and accounts as the look, plus `ivy`, `ann`, `gus`, `fay` and two claimless helpers; the
emulators behind `.drafts/d227/relook/proxy.mjs`, a local proxy on the phones' ports that could close Firestore, answer
every Functions call 503, hold `groupRoles` or delay Firestore writes, logging each call and each answer's `places`;

  full one; four unprovoked creates showed Owner when People opened.

  and +300 s by the proxy's log (iOS Cove 09:54:09, 09:55:09, 10:00:09; Android Reef 09:54:56, 09:55:56, 10:00:56), and
  the Owner pill appeared on the open page without navigation; the pill comes at the next scheduled retry, not when the

  layout after their records and even after the roles retry succeeded, until reopened; Android's Bight went live at the
  push. **R2** (both): a share that failed on the Functions was not tried again when they returned; it waited for the
  next foreground (decision 40). **R3** (Android): its reconnect share ran when Firestore's listen stream came back, 32 s
  after the write stream, since the share's server read needs the listen stream; iOS's two streams came back together
  in that run, so a lagging iOS listen stream is unproven.

**The UniFFI checksum finding (Corrected D-228: the plan's Design 4 said "Doc comments do not enter UniFFI's checksums
(they hash signatures)", so the bindings diff would be comment-only. That is wrong for UniFFI 0.32, the version this repo
locks. T3 measured it: `make bindings` changed seven checksum constants in both files, exactly the seven exports whose
`///` text changed in af6eba3 (`ffi_auto_categorise`, `ffi_hlc_receive`, `ffi_merchant_table_parse_signed`,
`ffi_plan_import`, `ffi_rules_evaluate`, `SkiptiVault.clear_records`, `SkiptiVault.close_vault`); the docs of records,
structs and functions that are not exported moved none. The T3 review checked the pairing.)** The bindings diff is
therefore doc comment lines plus those integers, all from one `make bindings`, committed with the core change, which is
what the freshness leg compares. The consequence bit once: T1's first whole-suite run, in the checkout while T3's
bindings were in flight, crashed the host app with "UniFFI API checksum mismatch". A shell that links a core library
built before af6eba3 with these bindings fails at start, so every lane and the look rebuilt core first (`make ios-core`,
`make android-core`, `cargo build -p skipti-core` for the JVM tests); the gate's `make ios-app` and `make android-app`
rebuild it. The plan now carries the correction note at Design 4 and a banner, and CLAUDE.md section 8 step 5 says it
(64f70ff). The same will bite the public-beta sweep of core doc comments.

**Findings and mistakes on the way, stated plainly:**
- **Design 4 was wrong** (above). The plan's "0 dashes left" in the bindings was not reachable either: three dashes are
  uniffi_bindgen 0.32's own template text (Swift line 54, Kotlin lines 105 and 111), which `make bindings` writes back;
  decision 41 grandfathered them and decision 42 made that moot (the bindings are not public). Section 4.
- **T1's index slip**: during its first staging, a snapshot list wider than meant staged old blobs of other lanes'
  files. Caught by `git diff --cached` before the commit and returned to HEAD entry by entry (no stash, reset or
  restore); both iOS commits hold `ios/` files only, checked by `git show --stat`.
- **T3's sabotage runner** restored a file with `shutil.copy2`, which kept the OLD mtime, so cargo kept the sabotaged
  binary for the next baseline; the restore now uses `copyfile` plus `utime`. Two of its anchors also matched the test's
  own text, and the run stopped loudly, as designed.
- **T5's first sabotage run** was 39 of 41: G11's expected set was incomplete (a prediction miss, the red right) and H3
  found a weak test (below the scissors the line began with "+", which the trailer rule never matches, so removing the
  scissors handling changed nothing). The test was fixed to use a diff context line; the second run, 41 of 41, is counted
  and the first kept.
- **Commits during parallel lanes ran their hook on the shared working tree**: T4's commit staged heavy inputs, so its
  pre-commit fast gate (10 of 10, cargo 325) proved the tree as it stood with Tasks 1 to 3's edits in flight, not T4's
  files alone; the full gate on the committed tree is the proof.
- **T2's whole JVM run** read T1's uncommitted Swift through the parity tests (T1 had not committed yet); T1's own tests
  and the full gate cover the committed Swift.
- **The Android fixer's tests came after its source edits**, not first; the red for the right reason is its seven
  sabotage rows, each reverting one fix. The guard fixer's lexer pins passed at once on the old checker, being pins of
  behaviour that was already right; their red is their seven L rows.
- **Both shell fixers found the same residue**: where the placeholder sits inside a sentence or a row with no label
  of its own, a screen reader still reads the hyphen (section 4); and iOS's `Settled.swift` falls back to a visible ""
  at one line, which the money fallback guard allows.
- **The gate's JVM leg ran 8 s and executed no test.** The 53 XML files in `testPlayDebugUnitTest` carry their own
  timestamp 16:54:55Z, the Android fixer's whole-suite run (894 tests, 0 failed), though their file times were
  rewritten at 17:17:50Z inside the gate window: Gradle reused that execution. That is sound: `ios/Skipti/App` and every
  other file the JVM tests read are declared inputs (`android/app/build.gradle.kts`, the `unitTests.all { inputs ... }`
  block, D-162), and Gradle reuses a test task's result only when its last execution over byte-identical inputs passed.
  So the JVM tally is carried forward, as recorded above. **The same mechanism explains D-227's open item** (no new XML
  after f705da5 changed Swift files the JVM tests read): the inputs Gradle saw were the ones a passing run had already
  tested.

**Where the identity rules ended** (groups.rs module doc at acf37a7, decisions 44 to 52): claims are phone-written and
the first claim per member wins by record identity, which the phone chooses. An id named by two present members'
claims is contested (no alias; the victim's group read-only on its phone); removing the forger's member lifts it while
the victim's own member is present. An id that is not contested reads as the member of its EARLIEST-written claim that
still counts; a claim on a removed member counts, against a present claim or a marked alias, only when it was written
before it. So **only a claim written BEFORE the person's own claim can take that person's history**: backdated (the
record identity is phone-chosen), or written with an honest timestamp before the person joined by a member who
already knew the id (the whole-branch review's I2); a denial while both members are present, a history move once the
forger's member is removed, when it was written on an already removed member, or on a present member once the victim
has left (Q6). Since decision 52 the server keeps one account to one present member of a group (except a creator
whose create has not reached the cloud). The
fix needs a verified claim author and order (the server's `authorUid` and `createdAt` carried into core) or claims the
server writes: G-08, open for the 0.5.0 security audit, with G-31 for the Function. Every honest shape the reviewers
probed (a rejoin, two rejoins, a second phone, the invitee, a removal, no account) reads right.

- **The spec and plan** (ec97578, b7296e3). Goal: a phone-written claim can no longer take or deny anyone's place or
  history; every place an account holds is marked by the server and core believes only the mark. Design: the
  `heldPlace` op `{"op":"heldPlace","group":G,"member":m,"you":y}`, built by phones and never uploaded, written by the
  server marked `held: true`; two writers (`sharePlaces` after a push, `acceptInvite` in the join's transaction); core's
  precedence D1 to D6 (a mark waits for its member; the latest per member stands; a raw `you` other than the member
  contested; the mark seeds the member's winning claim and voids unmarked claims against it; a marked alias of a held
  id elsewhere contested; `placing` rule 1.5). Decisions 53 to 57 came with it.
- **T1, core** (7bfbede, 4 files; Opus): as the plan, with two additions the implementer named: the test
  `d230_a_held_place_comes_before_an_earlier_claim`, because sabotage C5 (rule 1.5 disabled) survived the brief's

**Where the identity rules ended** (groups.rs module doc at b83ea52, index.js at 55ec25a, decisions 53 to 67): a place
an account holds is marked by the server, which checked that the caller holds it (D-227's `holderIn`, or `heldBefore`
for a place ever removed that it held and no other account ever used an invite for) and owns the id (its participant id
or its own log, no other account's participant id, no other current or former member's log, and no other account's
mark naming it on a present member: decision 66), and which stamps the mark's record identity itself (the server's
clock, the record's index in its call, a random device: no phone clock plays a part). A marked place is final for its
member and its id: an unmarked claim on it with another id, or naming its id on another member, is void; a marked alias
of its id elsewhere is contested; an `addMember` of its id is an empty placeholder the mark wins over; per member the
latest mark stands, and an id held by two members (an honest rejoin) reads on the earliest-added. So **no phone-written
record can take or deny a marked place's history**. What stays is what has no mark (legacy members until their phone's
next push, placeholders nobody holds, a member whose join-time mark failed a check until the next push) and the id
races of G-31 (3): a copied id is a denial because of decision 66, never a takeover, except the seconds after a second
phone's first join (F2). Every honest shape the reviewers probed (a rejoin, marked or not, in either mark order; a
removed creator's rejoin; a failed new mark; two phones; a new install's first join; no account) keeps its place and
history; the one honest edge decision 66 refuses is an account switch on one phone (F3, fails closed).

- **The app lock fix, and the fail-open it briefly made** (Opus; `.superpowers/sdd/d232/lock-fix-report.md` sections 1
  to 9; incident 30). **The bug** (pre-existing, made reachable by decision 78): Android's `AppLock` stamped every
  `onStop` and re-ran its launch decision in every new activity, so a configuration change (rotation, the phone's own
  dark switch, and since 78 an in-app Light or Dark tap) locked the app at ANY timeout, not only Immediately. It failed
  closed, so it was a nuisance, not a hole. **a0e7a34** made the lock pure: `AppLockRules` over `LockLife`, one
  transition per callback; a change while in front marks the stop, `created` carries the mark into the new activity,
  and `launched` keeps the state for a re-creation in front; every real background (Home, the app switcher, screen
  off, another app, Back, process death) behaves as before. 2 tests (a 14-sequence table and a source pin); JVM 959.
  **C1, found by the confirmation review, Critical**: a0e7a34 failed OPEN. An activity re-created before the process's
  first launch decision (its `goOn` cancelled with it) kept `locked = false`, so the ledger opened without the lock:
  reachable by rotating the phone while SKIPTI opens, and, with no one trying, by decision 78's first tell on every
  upgraded Android 12+ install with the lock on whose mode differs from the phone's. The table had no row for that
  order. **69a5780** fixed it: `launchDecided`, false in a fresh process, so `launched` keeps the state only after a
  decision; otherwise it decides and locks (fail closed); new rows for a re-creation before the first launch at 2
  minutes and Immediately, and two in a row. **Confirmation 2**: C1 closed, no other fail-open path (every state traced
  against every event); h1, optional: a configuration-change mark whose replacement activity is never created in a
  surviving process could linger and open a later activity (no known path). Taken by the controller (the lock fails
  closed): **2e2adc8** stamps the mark with `SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()`, honours it only within 2 s (0 to 2,000 ms
  inclusive, chosen on the lock look's measured 0.4 to 0.6 s relaunch) and clears it on use; the expiry hid sabotage
  L3, so an in-window background row was added. **Confirmation 3**: h1 closed, no new fail-open path; the change only
  adds locking, so the lock look's locking rows stand, and the four no-lock rows now depend on the relaunch landing
  inside 2 s (the worst case is an extra prompt, never an open ledger). Plainly: **a fail-open app lock existed on this
  branch for one commit (a0e7a34 to 69a5780), was caught by review before any merge, and never reached main or anyone's
  phone**; the only build carrying it was the decision 78 re-look's throwaway emulator. iOS has no such path and was
  not changed.

**The audit** (the founder's instruction, 2026-10-19: "run a full opus audit of everything including bugs and security
(comes before the fable part) and fix them as needed"). Five read-only Opus auditors read main at c0b61d7 to one common
brief (`.superpowers/sdd/d235/audit-common.md`); none ran a suite, a device or anything against production; the core
auditor proved its findings with a scratch probe crate on the locked graph (`core-probe/`). Totals as each report
states them:

| Area | Critical | High | Medium | Low | Doubts | Report (`.superpowers/sdd/d235/`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| core | 1 | 2 | 2 | 5 | 6 | `core-audit.md` |
| Firebase | 0 | 1 | 2 | 5 | 5 | `firebase-audit.md` |

**The Critical (core C1):** since D-195 a group expense's money edit never reached any other phone: core's revision
decoder returned the new money with no group, and both shells' ingest refused it as another group's record and moved
the cursor past it. **The Highs:** no money check on any group record (core H1; one bad record broke export for every
member); HLC receive unbounded and its counter able to wrap (core H2); a removed member's own earlier invite link
rejoined them (Firebase H1); the iPhone's app lock was an overlay under every sheet (iOS H1); a reinstalled iPhone was
signed in and synced without a sign-in (iOS H2, cross H1); Android saved an expense twice on a double tap (Android H1);
one cloud picture with a huge declared size could crash every member's Android app at every launch (Android H2). The
triage (`triage.md`) kept the controller's calls, named the founder's (CSV formulas, lock-screen push text, the invite
push to strangers, export's refuse-or-skip, whether CLOUD-SECURITY goes public) and Fable's (core M2's backdated Create,
the doubts), and split the fixes into five waves.

**Built by subagents** (superpowers:subagent-driven-development; ledger `.superpowers/sdd/progress.md` from line 909;
briefs, reports and reviews in `.superpowers/sdd/d235/`). Every auditor, implementer and reviewer whose work landed
was Opus (a duplicate Sonnet dispatch of wave D's round 6 and a second agent for iOS round 5 were stood down). Waves A
(core) and B (Firebase) ran in parallel on disjoint files, then C (iOS) and D (Android) in parallel on wave A's FFI,
then E (cross-cutting); each wave's implementer carried its lane through its review rounds, and the final wave and the
look fixes were fresh agents.

The first full gate on this tree (`.drafts/d239/gate.log`) read
"GATE FAILED: 22 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped": only `cargo deny check`, on RUSTSEC-2026-0374 (basic-toml 0.1.10
unmaintained, published 2026-10-20, after D-238), reached only through `askama_macros`, a proc-macro of
`uniffi_bindgen` 0.32, so never linked into a phone's library; `cargo audit` passed it as a warning. Decision 140:
`deny.toml` gains an `[advisories]` section naming that id alone, with its reason; with it the check reads
"advisories ok", without it "advisories FAILED". The failing output is kept under
`scripts/gate-artifacts/20261020T155210Z-*`. No other leg changed between the two runs.

**The cause.** The founder's iPhone 17 (iOS 27) showed no animation in 0.5.0 with Reduce Motion, Low Power and Less
motion off; the App icon row snapped; turning Low Power on and off fixed it, force-quit did not. iOS reported Low Power
at launch (Adaptive Power on; the likely source, not provable from outside), and D-214's one rule
(`MotionClock.shouldTick(reduceMotion:lowPower:active:)`) stilled the art and every moment alike. The motion engine had
never run on a real phone before 0.5.0. Decision 137 (the founder's): power saving stills the art only.

**What was built.** iOS `MotionClock.momentTicks(reduceMotion:active:)` and an `ArtCanvas` `moment` flag (the settle
burst is drawn by an art canvas); Android `MotionState.moment()` (`copy(lowPower = false)`). Every moment site reads
them: the App icon row, the switch's travel, the disclosure chevron, the done check, the toast, the overlay and its
dim, the celebration's start and its burst; `Celebration.showsBurst(reduceMotion:)` on both. The art (curtains, stars,
runes, signs) keeps the Low Power / battery saver still frame.

**The review (Opus, read from git while the sabotage ran): Needs fixes.** I1 (Important): what a moment leaves running
after it lands is art, and it ran on: the done screens' Norse rune ring turned for as long as the screen showed, now
also under power saving, and Android's done check redrew at 30 fps forever in every theme (its canvas was an endless
art loop; a twin asymmetry older than D-239). Fixed (decision 139): iOS `MotionClock.artTicks` (main actor) into
`DoneCheck.moving(tick:artTick:theme:start:landedFor:)`, and a landed pause holds `CheckMotion.landedElapsed` (1.2 s)
so the ring stops where it is; Android `DoneCheck.runFor(theme, artTicks)` with `LaunchedEffect(own, art.tick)`, and the
check drawn from `p.elapsed(...)`, its moment's own clock, which ends. M1/M2: the guards count every read (iOS any
`.lowPower`: 4, all in ThemeMotion.swift, and `isLowPowerModeEnabled`: 2; Android `lowPower`: 16 in ThemeMotion.kt
alone, `isPowerSaveMode` and the broadcast: 2), pin the ring and the moment reads, and the unused
`rememberShouldTick()` is deleted. M4: eleven stale comments that said power saving stills moments. M5: the ADR
amendment says "Reduce Motion, Less motion and an active screen", and hedges the Adaptive Power cause as decision 137
does; the LG's stuck spell is marked a guess.

**The look** (throwaway AVD d239-look, `system-images;android-34;default;arm64-v8a`, hw.ramSize 4096, `-gpu host`,
deleted afterwards; the debug build with no account, so no network). Finding: an emulator on AC power ignores battery
saver (`mIsPowered=true`); `dumpsys battery unplug` first. Saver on: 0 frames in 3 s idle on Balance (the art
paused); You > Appearance, the App icon row tapped: 51 frames in 1.5 s (the moment plays). Control, animator duration
scale 0: 5 frames (a snap). Saver off: 91 frames in 3 s (the art runs). Shots `.drafts/d239/shots/look-saver-*.png`.

**Sabotage** (`.drafts/d239/sabotage.py`; round 2 on the final code, `sabotage-run-2.log`; each row one asserted edit,
the five affected classes per shell, restored and compared). Round 1 misread I1 and I3 as green: both were compile
errors (`PowerState.shared.lowPower` is main-actor isolated) and xcodebuild prints TEST FAILED for a build failure too.

**Root cause** (`.drafts/groupdelete/rootcause.md`, emulator repro `emulator-results.txt`): `deleteGroup`
(`firebase/functions/index.js:1479`) wrote the `deleted` notice to `members.filter((u) => u !== uid)`, so the deleting
account's other phones never heard; they saw the group leave the listing, stopped listening and kept it writable; an
Add was saved, refused by the rules (403) and parked. The D-210 plan specified it so and its test pinned "the owner is
not told". Production checked read-only (the 28 deployed Functions and the live rules byte for byte this tree's). Not a
security flaw: every read and write of a deleted group is refused.

**Built.** Functions: `groups.deletionAudience(members, caller)` (every member, the caller included), `push.loud(uids,
quiet)` (the caller never pushed), the notice carries `byUid`. Shells (twins): `Notices.deletedMark` (self-delete =>
"You deleted {group}.", idempotent, upgrades a vanished copy), `GroupGone` (refused / not found / found without
membership (`former` or neither) => read-only; network error => retry; found as a member => keep), `checkVanished` on
server listings only (skips a listing like the last checked; iOS's vault work off the main thread), the first listing of
a session as the sweep, a vanished mark lifting only on relisting, `Placing.ReadOnlyCopy` refusing every write path with
words before anything is kept, `setYourName` passing read-only copies, `GroupEndCopy` (Android reads the Swift table).
Android's GroupPage seeds its state from the kept read and never writes state while drawing (the D-250 reopen bug). A
DEBUG/debug-only proof tool `--group-end create|join|delete|watch`.

**Two-phone proof** (`.drafts/d252/proof/`, local emulators only; iOS sim + two AVDs; accounts X on two devices, Y a
member): iOS deletes: X's Android phone "You deleted Goa1." 1.6 s after the call returned, Y "Xan deleted this group on
October 21, 2026" 0.6 s after, every Add refused with words, records unchanged, nothing parked; Android deletes: X's
iPhone 0.5 s, Y 1.3 s; a 0.5.0 victim (the old Function, phone away): the next launch marked it "no longer shared with
you" 1.7 s after launch, then "You deleted Goa3." within 0.64 s of a new-style notice. Fix-wave re-look on one AVD:
reopening a deleted group from Groups (twice), Balance and after Cancel keeps the banner, no Add people, no Settle; a
writable group unchanged.

**Review** (Opus, `.drafts/d252/review.md`): ready once I1 is fixed (the Android reopen bug: state written during the
first composition from D-250's kept read; iOS does not share the path); M2 former members could still read the group
and stayed writable on a lost notice; M3 iOS's check on the main thread; M4 the 0.5.0 deleting phone's cosmetic line
(residue); fixed in 9211143.

**The problem.** D-252 ended a deleted group on every phone, but a phone of the deleting account that still held a
copy could put it back: `ensureGroup` created the group document again (200) and uploaded its records
(`.drafts/groupdelete/rootcause.md`, RESURRECT). The founder chose option C, the tombstone (decision 276).

**What was built.** Functions: `tombstoneOf(memberUids, former, caller)` (`groups.js`, pure: byUid, `uids` deduplicated,
no name); `deleteGroup` awaits `deletedGroups/{g}.set({...tombstoneOf, deletedAt})` before `recursiveDelete`, so a
failed tombstone write fails the call before anything is deleted; `purgeAccount` untouched. Rules: the group create
adds `!exists(deletedGroups/$(groupId))`; `deletedGroups/{g}` allows only `get`, for `request.auth.uid in
resource.data.uids`. Shells (twins, iOS `Roles.swift` / Android `Roles.kt` `GroupGone`): `Tombstone(byYou, at)`,
`asksTombstone` (refused or not found only), a `deleted` outcome in `decide`, `mark(for:tombstone:now:)`,
`createRefused`; `GroupEndCopy.wasDeleted` "This group was deleted." for a nameless mark that is not yours;
`Notices.deletedMark` lets the notice rewrite such a mark with the deleter's name; `CloudSync.tombstoneRead` (server
source, bounded 8 s, read only); `ensureGroup` on `.notMember` runs `endIfDeleted` (own signed-in account only):
marks the copy deleted, removes its listener, refreshes screens. The RESURRECT trace now: create refused (403), group
read refused, `.notMember`, tombstone readable, deleted mark, listener removed, records kept on the phone, unsent,
unparked.

**Calls taken** (decisions 279 to 285): a purged uid stays in `uids` and purge's own deletion of sole-member groups
writes no tombstone (279); the deleter is always listed, as `deletionAudience` does (280); a tombstone read with no
answer counts as none and leaves D-252's neutral read-only mark (281); no new refusal line, one new banner line (282);
the notice may rewrite a nameless mark, never make one vaguer (283); `endIfDeleted` marks only with a tombstone (284);
invite paths keep their refusal error (285).

**Deploy order.** The rules first is safe (the guard refuses only ids whose tombstone exists, and nothing writes one
until the Functions deploy), then the Functions. A shell meeting no rule for the tombstone get is refused and reads it
as no tombstone.

**The problem** (CLOUD-SECURITY G-04, G-23, G-17, G-18; the founder brought them into this pass, decision 269). The
daily limits were per account, so a group's invites, joins and removals had no ceiling of their own (lead (a): remove,
re-invite, rejoin); any member could make the cloud send an unbounded number of pushes; and a push's line was text the
author's phone wrote, so it could name anyone and say anything.

**What was built.** Quotas: `people.js` `LIMITS` gains `groupInvites` 100, `groupJoins` 50, `groupRemovals` 100 and
`pushes` 300 (a comment per number); `groupLimitId(g)` = `group-{g}` in `limits/` (Functions only; account uids are
alphanumeric, so no clash); `charge(id, kind)` takes any counter id; `groupChargeIn(tx, g, kind)` reads the group's
counter inside the caller's transaction and returns the write. Invites charge once in their own transaction after the
membership or target check and before `refuseHeld` reads the log; acceptInvite reads `groupJoins` right after the
group-exists check and writes it with the join; removeMember and adoptRemovals read `groupRemovals` first and write it
with the removal records. Push cap: `chargePush(state, today)` returns `{send, write, log}`; past 300 the day is marked
`pushesCapped` once and later pushes write nothing; a new UTC day resets; `onGroupRecord` charges after `push.notice`
and the authorUid check, BEFORE reading the group, and logs `push: capped` (info, no uid). The line: `validNotice` in
the rules takes `{expense, kind, title, amount?}` (exact keys, kind in added, changed, deleted; title 1 to 61, amount 1
to 40 and never on a delete, both through `oneLine`, which refuses C0, DEL, C1, U+2028 and U+2029) or the old `{text,
expense}`; `push.js` re-checks the new shape or returns `{expense, legacy: true}` for the old (its text checked, never
used); `authorName` is the trimmed server name of 1 to 60, else "Someone"; the body is `{name} {kind} {title}` plus ` ·
{amount}`, legacy `{name} changed an expense`; `onGroupRecord` reads `users/{authorUid}` only when there are phones to
send to; the title stays `groups/{g}.name`. Phones (twins: iOS `Push.swift`, Android `Push.kt`): `PushNotice.Notice`,
`notice(_:thisDevice:expenses:locale:)` without the `groups` parameter, `oneLine`, `title`, `field`; `CloudSync` writes
`PushNotice.field(notice)`. The activity feed is untouched.

**Calls taken** (decisions 291 to 302): joins and removals charged inside their own transactions, invites in one of
their own before the log read, so refused calls spend nothing and a stranger cannot charge a group (291); adoptRemovals
charges one per call (292); lengths are UTF-16 code units, measured in the Firestore emulator (30 emoji pass, 31
refused; 61 euro signs pass) and pinned in `rules.test.mjs`, both phones cutting at a whole code point of at most 59
units plus an ellipsis (293); one line on the phone: each run of control characters and U+2028, U+2029 becomes one
space (294); the amount is sent only when core's string is 1 to 40 units with no control character (295); the phones
no longer read `namedGroups()` for notices (296); old and new shapes never mix (297); a server name over 60 units reads
"Someone" (298); the emulator seam stores the built message at `emulatorPushes/{recordId}` under `FUNCTIONS_EMULATOR`
(no rule matches it; production never sets the variable) (299); the cap's "logged once a day" is the `pushesCapped`
mark, and records without a notice are never charged (300); lead (d) stays residue: the title is the group document's
name (301); the suite ran on ports offset by 10000 with its own `TMPDIR`, `firebase.json` reverted before the commit
(302).

**Sabotage** (`.drafts/fable/pass-051/d257/sabotage.py`; logs, backups and `results.jsonl` in `sabotage/`; each row

**The problem** (CLOUD-SECURITY G-26; decision 269). Signing one phone out from another set its device entry's
`signedOut`, but the phone's token stayed valid and nothing in the rules read the flag: until the phone itself noticed
(its devices listener), it could keep writing records and updating its entry.

**What was built.** Rules: `deviceSignedOut()` = the entry `users/{uid}/devices/{request.resource.data.deviceId}`
exists and `signedOut` is true; `&& !deviceSignedOut()` on the personal and the group record create, after
`validRecord()` (so the id is proven 32 hex before it enters a path); a missing entry does not refuse; the device
update becomes `isUser(uid) && ((approved() && resource.data.get('signedOut', false) != true) || tokenRemovalOnly())`.
Functions unchanged. The rules test (`rules.test.mjs`, with `DROP` support in `write`): a signed-out phone's personal
and group records refused; a signed-in phone unaffected; a phone with no entry still writes; `signedOut: false` writes;
on the signed-out entry a name, a version and a new token are refused and the token removal goes through; deleting and
remaking the entry (a sign-in after a stale flag) writes again; another account's signed-out entry with the same id
changes nothing. Shells (twins): `CloudSync.signedOutElsewhere()` (the devices listener's former body, which the
listener now calls); `uploadOneByOne` / `oneByOne` take a `phone` read and return the flag; on a permission refusal,
after the approval check, the entry is read once per call; `PhoneFlag` (signedIn, signedOut, signedOutBefore, unknown)
and a pure `phoneFlag` using `Phones.signedOutSince`; `serverPhone` (server source, iOS `groupReadTimeout`, Android
`GroupEnsure.READ_TIMEOUT_MS`); `pushAll` runs `signedOutElsewhere()` on signedOut before parking. Tests: iOS
`ApprovalTests.testASignedOutPhonesRefusalIsNotParked`, Android
`AuditFixesTest.a_signed_out_phones_refusal_is_not_parked` (signedOut and signedOutBefore stop with nothing parked and
the entry read once; signedIn and unknown park as before; an invalid argument parks without a read; an unapproved
account stops on the approval and never reads the entry; the pure reading; source-order guards for the read, the
sign-out path and the server-only bounded read); the server-read count guards name the new read.

**Calls taken** (decisions 303 to 309): a flag set before this sign-in parks nothing and signs nothing out, and the
records go up at the next push once the registration remakes the entry (303); no answer parks as today, keeping
decision 114 (304); approval first, then the entry, only on a refusal that would park, once per pass (305); one remote
sign-out path, the same function on both shells (306); a signed-out entry takes no update but `tokenRemovalOnly()`,
which also passes a lastSeen-only stamp when no token is left, kept as the approval gate's helper (307); Android's new
read bounded at 8 s to match iOS (308); emulator ports offset by 20000, `firebase.json` restored by copy before the
commit (309).

**Read cost.** One more document read per record create once the entry exists (always, after registration); whether a
batch is billed one entry read or one per record was not measured (the emulator does not bill), so the upper bound is
one per record create. A push's batch now makes one more distinct access (approvals, one per group, the entry): a
batch touching 19 or more groups exceeds the 20-access limit, is refused and falls to the one-by-one path, slower but
never parked (not tested in the emulator).

**The problem** (a finding of the pass, from the D-249 probe, `.drafts/fable/pass-051/d249/report.md`). Any approved
member of ONE group can write 9,224 expenses of `MAX_AMOUNT_MINOR` (10^15 minor units) on one member, each passing
`ffi_check_expense` and the ingest checks; the rules put no count, rate or per-author cap on record writes (D-257's
cap limits pushes, not records), and 9,224 small writes fit Firestore's free daily quota and take minutes. That
member's net passes i64: `balance_line`, `settled_progress` and `overview` returned `Overflow`, and since `overview`
propagated the first group's error, every other member's Home showed only "Could not load the ledger" for ALL their
groups, including groups the attacker is not in. One record fewer overruns the totals the same way (via
`accumulate`), or, with two payer ids (the payer is payload-supplied), lands a net of exactly i64::MIN, which fits i64
and which iOS's many `abs(...)` / `Int64(x.magnitude)` reads of balance amounts would trap on (RemovalFlow already
notes it; found by reading, NOT reproduced on a device). Before the fix the only recovery was thousands of delete
records or leaving the group; removing the attacker does not remove their records.

**What was built.** Core: `overview` in two passes. Per group, `balance_line`'s `Err(Overflow)` marks the group (empty
`nets`, `overflowed: true`, a new UniFFI field; bindings regenerated and committed); any other error still returns
`Err` (a bug, not an attack). Adding up (`add_up`): totals and People are summed in i128; if a total or a person's
amount does not fit (`narrow_sum`), the group adding the most in the overrun's direction is marked (earliest on a
tie) and the rest added up again, one group per round, so it ends. `narrow_sum` (ffi.rs) is `Overflow` unless
`|v| <= i64::MAX`, used for `balance_line`'s entries, transfers and viewer net and `settled_progress`'s settled and
outstanding; other `narrow` call sites unchanged. Shells (twins): `LedgerLine.tooLarge`, `LedgerCards.line(_:tooLarge:)`,
`LedgerCopy.tooLarge` "Amounts too large to add up." (the existing LedgerCopy parity test compares both), drawn in the
dim body text and spoken; `HomeOverview.load` skips the settled meter for an overflowed group and reads every other
group's through `settledOrNone` (core's `Overflow` is no meter, any other error rethrown); `HomeOverview.tooLarge`
reads core's flag. The group page was checked and left as it was: both shells show "Could not load the group." when
its reads throw (for the 9,224-record group the first throw is `ffiGroupStats`'s "amount overflow"). Settings: core's
`SETTING_PER_PHONE_PREFIXES` (`applock.`, `privacy.`) are refused by `check_setting` in `validate`, so encode and decode
both refuse and the projection lists the record in `rejected`; no production shell code changed (both shells already
write only the synced keys), and two shell tests (iOS `SettingsSyncTests.testTheExcludedKeysNeverSync`, Android
`SettingsSyncTest.the_excluded_keys_never_sync`) now write such a record by hand, as a modified client would.

**Tests.** Core: `an_overflowed_group_is_marked_and_the_others_are_unchanged` (the d249 reproduction, Trip between
Flat and Goa; the honest groups, totals and People equal the overview without Trip; one record fewer adds up;
`settled_progress` is Overflow), `a_net_of_exactly_i64_min_is_out_of_range`,
`a_total_past_the_bound_drops_the_group_adding_the_most`, `a_persons_amount_past_the_bound_drops_one_group`,
`an_error_other_than_overflow_still_fails_the_overview` (negative), `a_per_phone_setting_key_is_refused`,
`a_per_phone_setting_record_lands_in_rejected`; each shell a pure test of the card line.

**Calls taken** (decisions 286 to 290): the isolation covers the add-up step too, since one record fewer failed the
whole overview on the totals (286); when a sum overruns, the group adding the most in its direction is marked, not
the one that happened to tip it, which the test pins by putting Trip first (287); `narrow_sum` refuses exactly
i64::MIN (288); a group whose lines fit but whose meter overflows keeps its balance line and draws no meter, and the
card's line comes only from core's flag (289); the per-phone prefix check ignores ASCII case (290). The field name
`overflowed` is the brief's own suggestion.

**The problem.** body-parser GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828 / CVE-2026-111181 (High; published 2026-10-23T20:53Z; affected
< 1.20.9 and >= 2.0.0 < 2.4.0; fixed 1.20.9 and 2.4.0, both 2026-10-22T11:38Z). Two places in SKIPTI:
(1) the Functions lock held body-parser 2.3.0 (express 5.2.1 via firebase-functions 7.4.0), which turned the gate's npm
audit leg red on main with no change of ours; (2) the copy that serves every callable was NOT in the lock: with no
`@google-cloud/functions-framework` in `functions/package.json`, Google's Node buildpack injects its own framework
from its own pinned lock at build time. Cloud Build 47388bcb (the 2026-10-20 deploy) reads "Handling functions without
dependency on functions-framework", `npm ci ... --prefix /layers/google.nodejs.functions-framework/...` and the label
`{"runtime":"nodejs","version":"3.5.1","injected":true}`; the buildpack's lock pins body-parser 1.20.5. So the live
callables were exposed (availability only: an instance's process dies, its in-flight calls fail; no data), and
redeploying unchanged would have put requestApproval and adminApprovals behind the same copy.

**What was built.** `firebase/functions/package.json` declares `@google-cloud/functions-framework` 3.5.1 (exact, the
version already running, so the runtime keeps its framework and the buildpack takes ours); the lock regenerated with
`npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts` and `npm update body-parser --package-lock-only`: the framework's
body-parser 1.20.9, the top level 2.4.0, qs 6.16.1, +91 packages and no new `hasInstallScript` (still only
@firebase/util and protobufjs). `firebase/tests/deploy.test.mjs` test 6 pins the declaration, the lock entry and every
non-dev body-parser past its line's fix.

**Reproduction (not reproduced, stated).** `.drafts/d261/repro.mjs` runs the real framework server
(`build/src/main.js`) with an HTTP function and sends: a plain request; deflate plus trailing bytes; gzip with trailing
bytes in a later chunk; deflate likewise; `text/plain; charset=x-bogus` with gzip and junk after the 415 (the framework
passes `verify`, which reaches the charset path the patch moves). On body-parser 1.20.8 (the copy already on disk in the
locked firebase-tools tree) and on 1.20.9 alike: 200, 200, 400, 200, 415, process alive, next request 200
(`repro-before.log`, `repro-after.log`). This Mac runs Node 26.4.0; production runs Node 22 (22.23.3 at the 10-20
build); Node 22 is not installed here (CLAUDE.md 13). The fix rests on the advisory and the 1.20.8 to 1.20.9 diff
(the decoder is detached and destroyed after a read; the charset 415 comes before the decoder exists) (decision 325).
