**The first run went red, on purpose of a guard** (`.drafts/d262/gate1-note.md`, `gate1-ios-fail.log`): `GATE
FAILED: 23 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped`, the one failure `AboutTests.testTheBundledInventoryIsSoundAndShowsOnlyWhatIOSShips`
`XCTAssertEqual failed: ("12.19.3") is not equal to ("12.19.2")`: the Licences page's version pin, every other class
at 0 failures. The pin moved to 12.19.3; the second run above is the green one. That run's gate.log was overwritten by
the second (a slip; its tail and the quoted line are kept).

**The problem.** eMudhra intermediate CA keys were disclosed (2026-10-17 to 10-22). Firestore on iOS opens gRPC over
BoringSSL with an EMBEDDED root list, not Apple's trust evaluation, so Apple's block does not reach it; a holder of a
certificate from those intermediates on the same network could sit between an iPhone and Firestore and read the sync
traffic, the ID token included. Firebase Apple 12.19.3 (2026-10-22): "Removed root certificates associated with
compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs from the embedded trust store."

**What changed.** `project.pbxproj` exactVersion 12.19.2 to 12.19.3; `Package.resolved` firebase-ios-sdk 8c29ca98 to
42cf1417 (`git ls-remote`: the tag 12.19.3 is 42cf1417; no other pin moved); `licences.json` 12.19.3 (`licences.py`);
the AboutTests pin. Read before the first build (CLAUDE.md 13): 12.19.2..42cf1417 is three commits: versions, the
roots file, `Package.swift`'s FirebaseFirestoreInternal binary (12.19.3/rc0 zip, its checksum), CMake and `build.sh`
for CMake builds.

**The root store, measured** (`.drafts/d262/roots.py`, `split.py`, `fp-12.19.2.txt`, `fp-12.19.3.txt`, by SHA-256
fingerprint): 130 certificates to 99; 67 removed, among them emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and AAA Certificate Services
(the roots the compromised intermediates chain to), emSign Root CA - C1, emSign ECC Root CA - C3, the Entrust and
TrustCor roots, GlobalSign Root CA and the old GTS R1 to R4; 33 added, among them the current self-signed GTS Root R1
and R4 and the Sectigo R46/E46 roots; emSign Root CA - G1 stays. **Firestore still connects:** its live chain is WE2,
then GTS Root R4 cross-signed by GlobalSign Root CA; the served GTS R4's key (9847e565…) is 12.19.3's GTS Root R4
(to 2036) (`gts-keys.txt`). (A LibreSSL `verify` check with a one-root control printed an error and "OK" together, so
it was dropped as unreliable.)

**In the binaries** (`markers.py`: 48 characters of each certificate's own base64, one from emSign ECC Root CA - G3,
in 12.19.2's store only, one from Sectigo R46, in 12.19.3's only): the 12.19.2 debug build `G3 1, R46 0`
(`binary-before.txt`); the 12.19.3 debug build and the gate's Release build `G3 0, R46 2` (`binary-after.txt`; R46
appears twice in Google's bundle).

## 4. Gap register (open, honest)

### 4.1 Blocking store-policy compliance later
- **CI web job**: guarded skip until `web/package.json` exists (D-23). The Vite/React PWA itself is unbuilt.

### 4.2 Crypto / Phase 2 residue
- **GATE 2 reading, stated precisely.** The literal gate text — "every KAT
  passes, and the crypto module imports nothing from UI" — has held since
  the Phase 2 KAT work landed; `lykill` imports only RustCrypto/dalek crates,
  and no UI exists to import from. BUILD-LOG has consistently used the
  stricter reading that the store must also exist. **This session claims the
  stricter reading**: the SQLCipher vault now exists behind a keystore trait
  (D-39) with the KAT-backed crypto untouched. What is explicitly *not*
  claimed: biometric-gated unlock, and A-17's on-device proof (backup
  exclusion flags plus extracting a real iCloud/Google backup per §14.4).
  Those are shell work and are recorded below as open, not ticked.
- **The web build has no store at all, and this is larger than a keystore
  backing.** `skrin` is `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` because SQLCipher
  cannot target wasm32, so the PWA inherits none of D-39. SPEC §10.2 specifies
  a different engine, a different encryption model and a different key
  lifecycle for web — IndexedDB with **per-record** encryption rather than
  page-level, WebAuthn for unlock, and keys in memory only so a reload forces
  re-unlock. That is a second store implementation, not an adapter, and it is
  unbuilt. `core/src/lib.rs` records it correctly at the cfg gate; this entry
  previously understated it as a keystore backing.
- **Deferred to Phase 7 shells** (the trait boundary is defined; the
  implementations are not): real Keystore backings (Keychain
  `WhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly`, Android Keystore, web per §10.2);
  biometric-gated release of the database key; backup-exclusion enforcement
  (`NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`, `allowBackup=false` + dataExtractionRules)
  and the §14.4 device backup audit that closes A-17 fully.
- **Argon2id RFC 9106 exact vector** unreproduced (D-14). Mitigations pinned; a full-vector KAT requires a crate exposing secret/AD or a vendored reference implementation.
- **Nonce session-id analysis**: 4-byte session ids give birthday-bound collisions across very large session populations; counters prevent within-session reuse. Formal margin analysis not yet written down (SPEC mandates this exact construction; analysis belongs in THREAT_MODEL.md appendix).

### 4.2b First-run / vault residue (D-127)
- **The WrongKey dead end is handled, not prevented.** `VaultRecoveryView`
  explains it and offers an explicit erase, but the underlying cause —
  a database restored without its Keychain item — is still reachable
  until §4.2's backup-exclusion work lands
  (`NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`, `allowBackup=false`). That work is
  what stops a user meeting this screen at all, and it is still
  deferred to Phase 7.
- **No test covers the brick.** Reproducing it needs a vault whose
  keystore entry no longer matches, which the current fixtures cannot
  build — every test provisions both together. The fix was verified by
  reading `StoreError.WrongKey` off a real simulator install, not by a
  red-then-green test, and that is weaker than this project's norm.
  A fixture that provisions a vault and then swaps the keystore key
  would close it.
- **Android has not been checked for the same shape.** Its gate may or
  may not swallow the equivalent failure; D-127 fixed only the shell the
  founder reported. This is a named follow-up, not a claim of parity.
- **The design pass covered call-to-action styling only.** Onboarding
  now uses the accent, hairlines and real field affordances, but the
  screens were built before the design system matured and a fuller
  pass (spacing rhythm, the middot micro-label separators SPEC §11.1
  names, the kit's chip treatment) is unbuilt.

### 4.2c iOS shell residue (D-128)
- **"SETTLED IN <currency>" names the wrong currency — on BOTH shells.**
  The Balance micro-label is built from each line's own currency
  (iOS `header(_:)`, Android `headerFor`), so a USD expense in an
  INR-settled group reads "GOA TRIP · 4 MEMBERS · SETTLED IN USD". SPEC
  §5.2 means the GROUP's settlement currency. Found on the simulator
  during D-128; predates it; a twin fix is owed.
- **Sign in's weight differs between the twins.** Android's account hub
  uses a filled accent `Button`; iOS's is the hairline secondary style,
  chosen because a filled sign-in starts to promote the account
  (GUARANTEES #5). One of the two should change; not decided here.
- **iOS tab labels use the system typeface**, not the grotesk
  micro-label Android's bar uses: SwiftUI's `tabItem` ignores custom
  fonts without `UITabBarItem` appearance work.
- **Lucide's `receipt` contains a dollar-like stroke.** It is upstream's
  drawing, on both shells since D-115, and reads as "$" in an app used
  heavily in INR. A NOTICE-compatible alternative drawing is a design
  call.
- **A test expense exists in the founder's simulator ledger** — "D-128
  check", $10 USD, split between You and Rahul — added to prove Add's
  save switches to Balance on device.
- **Still open from D-127:** no test covers the WrongKey brick.

### 4.3 Sync / Phase 3 residue
- **D-126's residue, and the biggest of it is iOS's shell:**
  (a) **iOS has no designed home.** Its root is `SmokeScreenView`, a
  developer menu of NavigationLinks; Balance, Expenses, Add and Settle
  are destinations in that menu rather than a designed shell. Android
  has `HomeShell` with the four-tab bar. So D-126's account glyph exists
  on Android only, and the iOS hub hangs off the smoke menu. **This is
  now the largest product gap on iOS** and it blocks any honest claim of
  shell parity — the screens are twins, the shells are not.
  **CLOSED 2026-09-14 by D-128:** `HomeShell` is iOS's four-tab root, the
  account glyph sits in Balance's toolbar, and the smoke menu is a proof
  surface behind `--smoke`. The shells are now twins in shape; the
  differences that remain are itemised in §4.2c.
  (b) **Sign-in is reachable but is still the OTP flow only.** Passkeys
  (D-118/D-120) are wired at the transport but not offered in this
  surface; Google Sign-In (ADR-0007) is implemented nowhere.
  (c) **No sign-OUT.** The hub shows "Signed in" and offers no way to end
  a session on the device. Account deletion exists on the relay
  (`POST /v1/account/delete`) and is wired to nothing.
  (d) **The device list still shows no last-sync or platform, and has no
  Revoke** — D-124's residue, unchanged; the entry point existing makes
  the gap more visible rather than less.
- **D-125's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **The off switch gates the AUTOMATIC hook only.** That is the whole
  of the app's automatic ledger traffic today — no automatic pull exists,
  verified by reading every call site of `fireAndForget`/`ledgerChanged`
  and `restoreFromRelay`. If an automatic pull is ever added it MUST be
  gated too, and this note is the reason it will not be forgotten.
  (b) **Device-key bootstrap still runs at sign-in with sync off.** It
  publishes an agreement PUBLIC key and carries no ledger data, so it is
  not what a user turning sync off is protecting themselves from — but it
  is network traffic, and calling that out is the honest reading of
  "off". Revisit if a stricter "off means silent" is ever wanted.
  (c) **Turning sync off does not remove what the relay already holds.**
  Account deletion is the act that does, and it exists
  (`POST /v1/account/delete`). The screens say so; nothing in the product
  yet routes a user from one to the other.
  (d) **GUARANTEES #5 was amended, not merely reworded.** The old text
  promised sync was opt-in; the new text promises an account is opt-in
  and sync can be turned off. Anyone auditing the published guarantee
  against a pre-D-125 build will find the old promise, which is why the
  amendment is dated in ADR-0034 rather than applied silently.
- **D-123's open questions, stated not implied:**
  (a) **A user whose ONLY device is lost has no path back to the relay
  records.** Approve-on-existing-device needs an existing device. The
  local ledger was always the source of truth and §9's export exists, but
  this is an ADR-0030-adjacent retention question and it is now LIVE.
  Open decision, the founder's; no recovery path is designed in this
  unit.
  (b) **A two-key split is possible** if two devices sign in truly
  simultaneously before either publishes-and-founds — both would found,
  each with its own key. It fails LOUD (records do not converge, never a
  silent loss); a server-side founding epoch or a signed founding claim
  would close it if it ever matters.
  (c) **Revocation residue:** a device that already RECEIVED the current
  sync key retains it until the sync key itself rotates. What is proven:
  a device removed from the envelope set receives nothing more, and the
  epoch parameter threading the FFI is what the rotation unit builds on
  (D-37/A-12 prove the primitive).
  (d) **The agreement-keys list is readable by any session of the
  account** (by design — that IS the device set), and a revoked device's
  registry binding persists until account deletion; the envelope ROW is
  the enforcement point for removal.
  (e) ~~**The approval surface is HEADLESS this unit**~~ **CLOSED by
  D-124**: `DeviceApprovalScreen` ships on both shells with SPEC's
  six-word safety phrase. `--authorize-device` remains as the wire proof
  and performs NO human verification — it reads the relay's own answer
  back at it, which is why it now also asserts that a substituted key is
  refused.

- **D-124's own residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **SPEC §12 asks each device row for last sync, platform, and a
  Revoke button.** The relay's `agreement-keys` row carries only
  `{device_id, agreement_public_key}`, so last-sync and platform need a
  relay change; Revoke needs key ROTATION (D-37/A-12 prove the
  primitive, the wiring is unbuilt). The screen shows the phrase and the
  approved marker and claims nothing else.
  (b) **QR verification is not built.** SPEC §3.3 offers "a QR scan when
  together, or reading six words aloud"; only the second exists.
  (c) **Key-change detection is not built.** SPEC §3.3 wants "Bob's
  device key changed. Verify again before adding expenses." with new
  envelopes held until acknowledged. Today a changed key simply shows
  different words and `authorise` refuses — correct, but silent about
  WHY, and nothing is held.
  (d) **The screens are arg-mounted** (`--devices`), because the whole
  account surface including sign-in still is. SPEC §12 says the device
  list is "a first-class screen, not a settings sub-page", so the
  product entry point is owed — as one unit covering the account
  surface, not as a tab bolted on for this screen alone.
  (e) **A-01 is proven at the shell boundary, not end to end against a
  hostile relay binary.** Both proofs substitute the key in the memory
  relay, which is the faithful stub of the real one; no test drives a
  real relay that lies.
- **UNEXPLAINED, one occurrence (D-122, 2026-08-31):** during one full
  `make android-test` run the JVM `the_relay_stores_only_ciphertext`
  test failed ONCE — the relay's stored bytes appeared to contain the
  record's plaintext ASCII — and then passed on every subsequent run
  (5 consecutive full-suite/class/single-test reruns, 0 failures). The
  seal path was read end to end and cannot produce this: `ffi_sync_seal`
  → `lykill::aead::seal` is AES-256-GCM (ciphertext = keystream XOR
  plaintext; a 16-byte ASCII substring surviving is ~2^-116), there is
  no global seal state and no plaintext fallback; the memory relay
  stores `HexCodec.decode(blob)` verbatim — byte-faithful for a list or
  a map. No reproducing command exists, so this lives here and NOT in a
  §3 status claim. If it ever recurs: capture the stored bytes and the
  pushed blob hex from the same run before touching anything.
  **AUDIT CORRECTION (2026-08-31, external audit of D-122): the
  ~2^-116 figure above answers the wrong assertion.** It covers the
  16-char canary `plaintext-canary`. The same test also asserts
  `assertFalse(stored.contains("INR"))` — a THREE-character canary. An
  ASCII byte always survives UTF-8 decoding, so a specific 3-byte
  sequence appears in N random ciphertext bytes with p ~ N x 2^-24: for
  a ~300-byte stored blob that is ~1.8e-5 per run (about 1 in 56,000),
  roughly 10^31 times likelier than the canary the analysis priced. So
  "the seal path cannot produce this" is OVERSTATED for the `INR` line —
  a spurious red there is a test-design property, not evidence about
  the seal. This does NOT close the flake (one occurrence in a few
  hundred runs still sits well above 1-in-56,000), and the residue
  stays open. OWED, both shells: drop the 3-char canaries (`INR`,
  `payer`) or replace them with distinctive long tokens, so the
  assertion is deterministic rather than probabilistic — the same
  "a check that can fail, and only when it should" rule that hardened
  the iOS hex-string test in D-121, applied to its inverse.
- **Automerge decision settled: superseded, not integrated (ADR-0018).**
  ADR-0004's swap condition ("contained behind straumr") was verified against
  the tree and holds — no module outside `straumr/` imports it; FFI/wasm
  expose no sync types; server code treats records as opaque. SPEC §6.1
  prescribes exactly the mechanics straumr implements, so the library choice
  was superseded on the merits with explicit tripwires: any data shape not
  expressible as {signed op, per-field LWW, set union} — e.g. concurrent
  reorderable lists or collaborative text — triggers a new ADR before skrin
  freezes a schema around it. New op types must enter the convergence harness
  before shipping.
- Attachment chunking (256 KiB, per-chunk keys, lazy fetch) — not started.
- Cloud-drive, LAN-QR, hosted backends — trait boundary exists conceptually (`BlobStore` server-side) but no client backend abstraction yet.
- Batch/coalesce window + optional randomised delay — needs the async runtime that ships with clients.
- Relay storage is now persistent (SQLite vault, D-40), restart survival is
  proven (`persist_restart.rs`), and the subject-owned sync surface is
  implemented and adversarially proven (D-41, `authz_http.rs`).
  **TLS IS LIVE (2026-08-26): the relay runs at `https://skipti.vardrlabs.com`
  behind a valid Let's Encrypt certificate, verified from outside the box;
  the client proves the unauthenticated surface against it live (D-79).**
  Backup gap CLOSED TWICE OVER: D-83/ADR-0030 set the policy, and D-84
  IMPLEMENTED it — `deploy/skipti-backup.sh` + systemd units +
  `deploy/skipti-restore-drill.sh`, all version-controlled, proven end to
  end against an authentic relay vault (4/4 drill steps, restored instance
  answering /version with the production commit) with a corrupt-backup
  negative proof (Corrected D-170: on macOS; on the Ubuntu host the scripts
  failed on line one until they ran under bash, and the operator step below
  was first done in D-170). What remains is the OPERATOR step: install the units on
  the box and enable the timer (commands in DEPLOY-ORACLE §10.2), plus the
  Oracle volume backup policy in the console, and the first in-production
  drill recorded. `/version` DEPLOY status: the live binary
  answers 200 with `"commit":"unknown"`; the D-81 env-var path flips it to
  a verifiable hash at the next deploy. Remaining for the hosted story:
  IP-log disablement verification across LB → nginx → app logs, and the
  backup LAYERS being actually enabled on the box (the runbook exists; the
  operator executes it).
  - Passkeys: ALL deployment prerequisites are now real (Team ID
    27GK2T7UCT, live AASA, TLS, and the live relay serving
    `rp.id = skipti.vardrlabs.com` — D-82 probed it). The app side is
    wired (entitlement + ceremony option-driven). What remains unproven is
    exactly and only the on-device ceremony: no registered devices → no
    development provisioning profile; simulator controller starts fail
    (D-57) and simulator Face ID auto-matches rather than proving Apple's
    matching.
  - **Verify-before-first-user per ADR-0021** reduces to the items above
    plus THREAT_MODEL's IP-logging commitment; no code blockers remain on
    the relay itself.
- Full GATE 3 (offline-first E2E + proxied network capture): the client half
  now exists — D-67's round trip drives a runnable iOS client against the
  real relay end to end. What GATE 3 still awaits: the proxied network
  capture leg and the deployed-instance transport (TLS) reality.

### 4.4 Everything else
- **SNAPSHOT SYNC SILENTLY LOSES DATA ACROSS DEVICES (ADR-0034).** Found
  2026-08-29 while answering a founder question about multi-device use. The
  shells push a whole sealed snapshot per change and restore reads the newest
  one, so: phone pushes a snapshot containing X; laptop, which never pulled,
  pushes its own at a higher index containing Y and not X; restore reads the
  newest and **X is gone**. The 409 path pulls and advances the cursor but
  **does not merge** — verified in `LedgerSync`. Nothing crashes, nothing is
  logged. D-67 recorded the mechanism honestly ("newest snapshot wins") but
  never in terms of the consequence, which is why it sat.
  **Core already solves this and the shells throw it away:**
  `straumr::Hlc { millis, counter, device_id }` exists, `skrin` orders by it,
  and two gate legs prove three devices converge byte-identically from
  different orders. The gap is plumbing, not research — the shells send a
  photograph of local state instead of records. ADR-0034 decides the fix and,
  critically, the ORDER: record-level sync ships BEFORE sync-on-by-default,
  because default-on against the snapshot engine makes the loss path normal
  rather than rare. Per-device keys (D-42 deferred, D-67 carried) move onto
  the critical path.
- **Google Sign-In is in ADR-0007 and implemented nowhere** — no relay route,
  no client. Founder confirmed 2026-08-29 it should be built: Android users
  largely do not hold Apple IDs, so Apple + OTP leaves that platform with one
  fewer path than the ADR promises.
  **Update 2026-09-14 (D-129):** the founder decided it ships on iOS and
  Android, and GUARANTEES #6 was amended to allow it (ADR-0035). Planned:
  relay D-130, iOS D-131 (with Sign in with Apple, mandatory once Google is
  on iOS), Android `play` D-132. Still unimplemented as of D-129. The
  Android `direct` flavour will have NO Google sign-in (ADR-0035 constraint
  5) — a deliberate asymmetry, not an omission. The Apple path has no
  relay-issued nonce (D-63); Google's will, and that difference is open.
  (Corrected D-130: the D-129 update above was spliced into the middle of
  this bullet's original sentence — its anchor `no client.` matched partway
  through a line — and shipped that way in `a0ee677`. Restored to
  original-then-update order; no words changed.)
  **Update 2026-09-14 (D-130):** the relay side is built; no client exists
  yet.
- **D-130's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **Nothing has touched real Google.** No OAuth client ids exist yet, and
  the relay is not deployed with D-130. `google_http.rs` proves the relay
  against a local fake of Google's key set and token endpoint, nothing more.
  (b) **The iOS reversed-client-id redirect is unproven** (Google's docs are
  ambiguous; see D-130's §3 findings). A refusal from Google sends the choice
  of fallback to the founder.
  (c) **Nonces live in memory.** A relay restart between `/start` and sign-in
  fails that attempt; the user retries.
  (d) **`/v1/auth/google/start` has no per-client admission limit.** The
  10 000 cap keeps memory bounded and never evicts a live nonce, but a
  flooder who fills it can refuse Google sign-in to everyone for up to the
  600 s TTL. OTP and passkeys are unaffected, and ADR-0032's per-source
  connection limit applies at the kernel. Recorded rather than solved.
  (e) ~~**The Apple path still has no relay-issued nonce** (D-63), so an Apple
  identity token is replayable until it expires; Google's path is not.~~
  **CLOSED by D-131:** `/v1/auth/apple/start` issues a single-use nonce from
  Apple's own store, and verification spends it before checking the token.
  Residue: that Apple's real token echoes the nonce unhashed is unproven until
  the first device ceremony (D-132).
  (f) **Google will only let listed test users sign in** until the app is
  published to production, which needs a public home page with privacy-policy
  and terms links — the privacy policy is on this path too.
- **D-132's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **No real ceremony has run** for either provider. Production is still on
  `69aeb87`, so the founder deploys `91a84a1` or later first. Apple also needs
  the Sign in with Apple capability on the App ID, and a device or a simulator
  signed in to an Apple ID. Google needs the iOS client id.
  (b) **The Google button is not in the UI.** It waits on the client id and on
  Google's official mark (download permission pending). Until then the iOS Sign
  in screen offers Apple and the email code; passkeys remain wired at the
  transport but not offered (D-126 residue).
  (c) **The device label is hard-coded "iphone"** on the Apple path, as on the
  OTP path.
  (d) **Android has no Apple sign-in**, by design (SPEC §12.2 is an Apple rule),
  and no Google sign-in yet (D-133).
  (e) **That Apple returns the nonce unhashed** is still unproven until (a).
- **D-133's residue, stated not implied:**

- **D-150's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **The iOS sync round-trip E2E is red whenever a relay runs.**

  (c) **A signed-in device waiting for approval can delete too.** Deletion is
  allowed to any session of the account, as on the relay (D-62); the
  threat is already stated in THREAT_MODEL (a stolen sign-in can ask).
  (d) **The day, not the hour.** The screen names the day the deletion
  becomes final (the relay's deadline, local time); the hourly sweep can
  complete it up to an hour after that moment (D-149 (d)).
  (e) **Day format differs by shell**, as elsewhere: iOS writes "Oct 1, 2026"
  in en-US and Android "1 Oct 2026" in both locales.
  (f) **Neither shell's Settings offers a plain sign-out**; this unit did not
  add one, so after a deletion is cancelled the account stays signed in.
  (Closed D-155: Settings has a plain Sign out on both shells.)
  (g) **Not seen against the hosted relay.** The live relay refuses the dev
  mint, and an email code is never shown, so the end-to-end check ran
  against a local relay built from the deployed commit's server code.
- **D-151's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **Groups still do not survive a lost device.** Restoring from the
  relay brings back expenses and settlements but not the groups they belong
  to (names, members, settlement currency): groups are per-device kv, not
  records (D-121 (3)). The proofs no longer pretend otherwise; making groups
  records is the first step of the shared-groups work.
  (Closed D-153: both apps keep groups and "you" as records; a restored
  device gets them back, and both proofs assert them again.)
  (b) **Relay tests still skip in an ordinary gate.** This unit's gate ran
  with a local dev relay by hand; `scripts/gate.sh` does not start one, so
  the next gate skips them again (iOS 8, JVM 1 per flavour). Starting a
  throwaway relay inside the gate is possible and would stop a break hiding
  as a skip; it is not done here.
  (c) **Vaults written before D-151 keep their old byte order** until the
  next write or rebuild re-encodes them; nothing compares stored bytes
  except the proofs, so this changes nothing a person sees.
  (d) **Record blobs still use the default encoder.** They are written once,
  sealed and decoded by value, so their key order does not matter today; if
  a record's bytes ever feed an identity or a hash, they need the same
  treatment.
- **D-152's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **Nothing uses it yet.** Both shells still keep groups and "you" only in
  kv; D-153 writes these records, rebuilds `ledger/groups` and `ledger/self`
  from them, and backfills existing kv groups first (D-122 #3's lesson: a
  rebuild before the backfill would erase them).
  (b) **The merge is not built.** The projection reports other "you" ids;
  making them count as one person is its own unit, as decided.
  (c) **Nobody can be removed, and a group cannot be deleted.** There is no
  operation for either (unchanged from D-135's residue).
  (d) **"Told apart" is display only.** "Rahul (2)" is not written back; if
  someone renames either Rahul, the suffix goes away on its own.
  (e) **Group names have no length limit**, as `ffi::create_group` has none;
  member names keep the 64-character limit.
  (f) **Group records are still sealed with the account's sync key**, like
  every record today. Sharing a group with other people needs group keys and
  envelopes (ADR-0005), later.
- **D-153's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **Two "you"s are not one person in balances yet.** A device that
  adopts the account's "you" keeps its own old id as an alias; groups made
  under it show "(You)", but expenses paid by the old id still count as a
  different participant, so a group holding both reads as you owing yourself.
  That is the merge unit (D-154), as the founder decided.
  (Closed D-154: every id a device wrote as "you" reads as the account's
  "you" in expenses, settlements and groups.)
  (b) **"You" is decided by the earliest `you` record.** A phone that upgrades
  AFTER a fresh second device already wrote its "you" makes the fresh device's
  id the account's "you" and its own the alias. Harmless once the merge
  exists; until then the phone's own groups show "(You)" through the alias.
  (c) **Renaming yourself renames you only in groups under your current id**,
  not in groups under an alias.
  (d) **Builds from before D-153 store group records and ignore them**: a
  device on an old build keeps its kv groups and sees nothing new.
  Internal testing only; every device should update together.
  (e) **Selecting a group stays per device** (`ledger/selected-group`), on
  purpose.
  (f) **Relay tests ran because a relay was started by hand** (D-151 (b) is
  unchanged: the gate script does not start one).
- **D-154's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **Groups kept only in kv are not merged.** A group with no create
  record (one core refused to encode; the union rule keeps it) bypasses the
  projection, so it still shows an old "you" through D-153's alias fallback.
  (b) **Export writes the merged ledger.** It reads the projected kv, so a
  backup carries one "you"; the records on the device keep both ids.
  (c) **Nothing tells the person that a merge happened.** Two "Tim"s become
  one silently, as ADR-0034 §2 prefers; the losing names stay in the records.
  (d) **Not checked on screen**: an Add screen opened before a pull merged
  ids can still hold the old id until it reloads (reasoned, not observed); if
  it saves, the next projection reads that id as "you", so balances are right.
- **D-155's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **Signing in to a DIFFERENT account on the same device is not
  handled.** Sign-out keeps the sync keys, the push cursor and "you" so that
  signing back in resumes; a second account would reuse them. Unchanged by
  this unit (deletion's sign-out behaves the same), and not yet designed.
  (b) **An unconfirmed sign-out leaves the session alive on the relay** until
  it expires (30 days) or is removed from another device's device list. No
  device holds its tokens any more.
  (c) **Sessions are stored in the vault**, not split between memory and the
  keychain as SPEC §4.3 describes (access token in memory only, refresh
  token in Keychain/Keystore). The vault is encrypted with a keychain-held
  key, but the letter of §4.3 is not met. Found while reading §4.3 for this
  unit; it predates it and needs its own decision.
- **D-156's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **Not deployed.** The live relay is still D-149's `03e6abf` until the
  founder deploys this one (schema v4 → v5; §7.1 of the runbook, with a backup
  first).
  (b) **No app uses any of it yet.** Group keys and group-log sync (D-158), the
  invite link and the `claim` operation (D-157), the invite and join screens
  (D-159), the banner (D-160) and verification states (D-161) are still to come.
  (c) **Removing a member and rotating the key are not built** (SPEC §3.6).
  The existing `/replace` route is the relay half; nothing uses it for shared
  groups yet.
  (d) **The invite limits are the relay's first guess**: 64 live invites per
  group, 32 inbox entries per device, 16 per request, 4 KiB payloads,
  30-day expiry. None has been measured against real use.
  (e) **A member who knows another member's device id** (from the group log,
  once D-157 puts it there) can learn from `POST /v1/inbox` whether that
  device's account shares a group with them. They already know that from the
  group itself; recorded so it is not mistaken for new.
- **D-157's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **Nothing calls the invite functions yet.** The shells use them in D-158
  (group keys and group-log sync) and D-159 (the invite and join screens).
  (b) **A claim is not signed by the claimer's device.** Any member of a group
  can write a claim for any member who has not been claimed yet. The first
  claim stands and later ones are contested, so a hijack is visible but not
  prevented. Verification (six words, D-161) is what tells people apart.
  (c) **The inviter's name inside the payload is what the inviter's device
  wrote**; nothing proves it. The same holds for every name in SKIPTI.
  (d) **Group names in a payload are capped at 200 characters**, a limit
  `ffi::create_group` does not have. A longer name cannot be invited to until
  it is shortened. None is that long today.
- **D-158's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **No screens yet.** Inviting and joining work headlessly and in tests;
  the invite screen with its QR code, the join screen and link handling are
  D-159. The in-app invite (inbox and banner) is D-160; verification states
  and six words are D-161.
  (b) **Every group gets a relay log and one envelope row**, including a
  group that was never shared (ADR-0037's "one code path"). The relay
  therefore learns how many groups an account has and how much each one
  writes. That is new metadata since D-158; THREAT_MODEL's table now says so.
  (c) **Pulls read each group's whole log every time**, as the account log
  does; there is no incremental cursor on reads yet. Fine at internal-testing
  sizes; a long-lived group will want `since`.
  (d) **Nothing fetches while the app stays open**: changes arrive when it
  comes to the front, after your own change, or on restore. There is no
  periodic pull and no push notification (none is planned: GUARANTEES #6).
  (e) **Two of your devices minting a key for one group at the same moment**
  leave two keys; readers try both, so nothing is lost, and the first
  written seals from then on.
  (f) **A member can still rename anyone in the group, add people, and win
  last-writer-wins registers with a clock set ahead**, exactly as a member
  on your own devices could. That is membership, not a leak; D-161's
  verification tells people apart.
- **D-159's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **Opening a link straight into the app needs your deploy** (runbook
  §8.2). Until then a link opens the browser page, and the person pastes it
  into "Join a group". Android verification needs the Play app-signing
  fingerprint, which exists only after the first Play upload.
  (b) **The in-app invite (inbox and banner) is not built**: D-160.
  **Verification states** (UNVERIFIED, six words side by side) are D-161.
  (c) **No camera in the app, by design** (ADR-0037): the joiner's own camera
  app reads the QR and opens the link.
  (d) **A person added to one group is not offered for another group**; you
  add them by name there too. Choosing "people you already share a group
  with" is D-160's in-app invite.
  (e) **An account with two "you" ids (D-154) claims its place under the
  canonical id**; in a group that holds the older id, that claim waits in
  `pending`, and other members may still see "Invite <you>". Rare (two
  devices used apart before signing in); it resolves if you are invited and
  join.
  (f) **The `/join` page's CSP pins the script by hash**; editing the page
  means recomputing it (the runbook says how).
- **D-160's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **Device keys come from claims, which are not verified yet.** A member
  who wrote a false claim first could receive an in-app invite meant for
  someone else. They already share a group with you, and the relay checks
  that. D-161's verification states (UNVERIFIED, six words side by side) are
  the answer.
  (b) **A device added later is reached only after it has synced once**
  (that is when it adds itself to its account's claim, and the claim reaches
  the inviter).
  (c) **There is no permanent "decline"**: "Not now" hides the banner until
  the next launch, and the invite lapses after 7 days. Declining would tell
  nobody anything; the person is in the ledger either way.
  (d) **The banner shows one invite at a time**, the oldest first; the rest
  follow as each is accepted or put aside.
  (e) **An in-app invite to someone added under a different name** in this
  group (for example "Rahul K" here, "Rahul" in Goa) adds a second member.
  Send that member the link from INVITE instead. A picker for "which member is
  this" was not built.
- **D-161's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **Verifying by QR scan is not built.** SPEC §3.2 names QR or words read
  aloud. The app has no camera by design (ADR-0037), so it offers the words,
  side by side or read aloud.
  (b) **"Key changed" is not shown as its own state.** A reinstall makes a new
  device, which reads as UNVERIFIED again (the SPEC outcome), but SPEC §11's
  "Amit's device key changed …" line is not used. Holding new envelopes until
  a change is acknowledged (SPEC §3.2) is not built either: group keys reach
  your own devices only through your own log (D-158), and a member's changed
  key does not re-wrap anything.
  (c) **Verification is per phone.** Your other devices verify separately,
  because the result is never synced (it would tell the relay's log who
  checked whom, even sealed).
  (d) **Nothing is blocked while someone is unverified.** SPEC says "before
  adding expenses", and the copy says so; the Add screen does not refuse.
  (e) **The joiner trusts the inviter's key from the link.** A link read by
  someone else in the messenger lets them join as the named person (ADR-0037
  already names that); the inviter then sees them UNVERIFIED.
- **D-162's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **A phone restored from a backup made before this build** still has the
  old vault in it, and gets D-127's honest screen and a confirmed erase. The
  way back is sync or the Recovery Kit, as on any new phone.
  (b) **Other §3.7 rows are still open** and belong to the app-lock unit on
  the loose-ends list: the biometric gate, auto-lock, screenshot blocking,
  task-switcher blur, clipboard clearing, and root/jailbreak warnings. The
  Android vault key is not created with `setUserAuthenticationRequired`
  either; that needs the app lock first.
  (c) **SPEC §4.3's web rule is untouched**, and the web build is unbuilt.
- **D-163's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **Android's live tile:** opening Recents from inside SKIPTI shows the
  launcher's live view of the screen you were just on. SKIPTI's stored card
  is blank.
  (b) **Android 8 to 10 get no app lock**: letting the screen lock stand in
  for biometrics inside `BiometricPrompt` needs Android 11. Settings says so.
  **Android 11 and 12 get the lock but no Recents protection**, because the
  only tool there, `FLAG_SECURE`, also blocks screenshots. That is D-164's
  question.
  (c) **Not built yet (D-164):** screenshot blocking on ledger screens,
  clipboard clearing, root and jailbreak warnings. The Android vault key does
  not use `setUserAuthenticationRequired`, which would make the key itself
  need the unlock; the app lock gates the screens, not the key.
  (d) **The lock is per launch of the app process.** Force-quitting and
  reopening locks, as it should. A quiet crash and relaunch also locks.
  (e) **Android's lock screen has no lock drawing** (iOS uses the system lock
  symbol). Adding a Lucide drawing means a NOTICE change; left out.
- **D-164's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **iOS cannot block screenshots.** The setting covers recording,
  mirroring and sharing only, and says so.
  (b) **Android does not clear the clipboard on a timer.** Android 10+ keeps
  apps in the background away from the clipboard, and clearing it blind could
  wipe something the person copied later. The link is flagged sensitive;
  Android 13+ also clears old clipboard items itself.
  (c) **Root and jailbreak checks are a small, known list** and trivially
  hidden by anyone determined. SPEC's position is "warn, never block", and
  this is only the warning.
  (d) **The Android vault key still has no `setUserAuthenticationRequired`**:
  the app lock gates the screens, not the key (D-163's residue (c)).
- **D-165's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **Core's list is not exactly ISO 4217.** It carries six local codes
  ISO does not list (GGP, IMP, JEP, KID, PRB, TVD) and HRK, withdrawn in
  2023, and lacks XCG (which replaced ANG in 2025). The picker shows core's
  list as it is; changing the list is a core change with export and import
  consequences, not a picker fix.
  (b) **Currency names come from each platform**, so iOS and Android may
  word a name differently; the codes, the order and the search rule are
  shared.
  (c) **The default is not synced** between a person's devices: it is a
  preference of the phone, like Appearance.
  (d) **No UI test harness**: the iOS search-and-go-back fix and the
  labelled menu rows are proven by eye on the simulator, not by a test.
- **D-166's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **No undo of a whole import** after it is applied. SPEC §9.5 asks for
  "rollback of the entire import as one unit"; the dry run and the
  all-or-nothing apply are built, the undo afterwards is not.
  (b) **An import always makes a new group.** Importing into an existing group
  (matching the sheet's people to its members) is not built.
  (c) **Only Splitwise and Wallet by BudgetBakers.** Tricount, Settle Up,
  Splid and the generic bank CSV with column mapping (SPEC §9.5) are not
  built; nor are Splitwise's other date layouts (the flow reads YYYY-MM-DD).
  (d) **Still no real export read.** The sign fix rests on Splitwise's help
  page and an independent converter; a fresh export from a real Splitwise
  account should be imported before a store release.
  (e) **Multi-payer rows are refused**, as before, and listed with names.
  (f) **A wallet row near midnight can move a day** for someone far from UTC:
  its wall time is kept in the phone's time zone, and duplicate checks use
  the UTC day.
  (g) **Android's `--import` verification surface still writes kv only** (no
  sync records). It is a test entry point, not a user path; the user path is
  the new flow.
  (h) **Settings' Export card promises "a JSON backup to restore"**, and
  neither app restores one yet (found while reading for this unit).
  (i) **Core's merge check does not test that an expense's group exists, or
  that its payer and shares belong to that group** (`validate_snapshot` checks
  the id's shape only; sabotage run 1 found it). The import plans against
  the ledger plus the new group so the check would apply if core grows it; a
  core unit should add it, with its own golden.
- **D-167's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **No test draws the PDF on the JVM**: `PdfDocument` is a platform class.
  The page was drawn, saved and read back on the emulator; the layout is
  pinned on the JVM.
  (b) **The two apps' pages are the same design, not the same bytes**: iOS
  lays text out with Core Text, Android with its canvas, so line breaks in
  the paragraph can differ slightly.
  (c) **Where the saved file goes is the person's choice**, as on iOS's share
  sheet: a cloud folder picked in the system dialog is a cloud folder. The
  "Saved." line says to keep it somewhere only they can reach.
  (d) **Android still has no kit reminder** (D-147 (e)).
- **D-168's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **The refusal is on the phone only.** The relay does not know which
  phone holds which account's ledger (real sign-ins declare no sync device),
  so a modified app could still sign a second account in; the relay stores
  only ciphertext it cannot open either way (GUARANTEES #7).
  (b) **The erase does not delete the account** or what it synced. Signing in
  with the same account after an erase starts a new ledger on this phone; the
  old one comes back only through another approved device (D-124) or the
  Recovery Kit path.
  (c) **A refused session is ended best-effort**: if the relay cannot be
  reached, it lives until it expires, as with D-155 (b); the phone never
  stored it.
  (d) **The per-phone preferences stay** after an erase (appearance, app
  lock, default currency, privacy): they are the phone's, not the ledger's.
  (e) **No typed confirmation**: one alert, with "This cannot be undone.
  Export first if you want a copy."
- **D-169's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **The permission prompt's wording is unseen** until a device build: the
  simulator never shows it.
  (b) **Export compliance is not declared in Info.plist**
  (`ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption`). SKIPTI encrypts with standard algorithms
  (SQLCipher, AES-GCM, X25519); App Store Connect will ask on each upload
  until the key is set, and the answer is the founder's (with counsel if
  needed), not a build setting to guess.
- **D-170's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **No automated check that a deploy script runs on the host's shell.**

  (b) **Layer 2, the Oracle boot-volume backup policy, is unconfirmed**: it is
  set in the Oracle console, the founder's.
  (c) **Backups are on the same host as the relay** (layer 1). A lost
  instance loses both until layer 2 is confirmed; ADR-0030 names an
  off-host copy as a further layer.
  (d) **No monitoring**: a failing nightly backup is visible only in
  `journalctl -u skipti-backup.service` (DEPLOY-ORACLE, "What this does not
  cover").
- **D-171's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **No iPad support.** On an iPad the app runs in iPhone mode. SPEC §14's

  (c) **Xcode's "Update to recommended settings"** is still pending, cancelled

  (a) **Google sign-in on Android is still not proven.** The app now says

  (b) **The Add reset has no automated test**: it is view identity in the

  (d) **A sign-in from before D-172 shows "Signed in"**, with no method,

- **D-173's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **The tests pin the flag, not the layout**: a screen that drew the

- **D-177's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **The kit-step motion was never reproduced on a simulator**; the fix

  (a) **Balance, Expenses and Settle up still work on one selected group**; Balance across every group, the group page,

  build (e85e486) reads ALREADY_EXISTS from `createInvite` (a share link) as "Could not reach SKIPTI's cloud. Check your
  connection and try again." and from `inviteUser` (a find-person invite) as "That username is taken.", and offers Try
  again. Before D-218 the invite was made and failed only at acceptance. Low harm (internal testers, a rare state); the
  0.5.0 deploy notes and the testers' What to Test text must say "update before inviting" (WORKLOG).
  (c) **createInvite's read cost is 1 + 1 + N + K, with K unbounded** (the group, the group again inside the check, the N
  members' `users/{uid}`, and every invite ever made for the place, no `.limit`); `inviteUser` and `inviteKnown` add
  1 + N + K before a refusal, which is not charged to their daily quota. `createInvite` has no quota (G-04), and an unheld
  place takes any number of open invites, so a member spamming one place costs about K reads per call, quadratic in the
  spam. Recorded in CLOUD-SECURITY ("Open for the 0.5.0 audit (D-218, read cost)" and G-04); the audit's options are a
  daily quota on `createInvite` or a cap or expiry on open invites per place. Not changed here.
  (d) **iOS, found in the look and NOT root-caused (under investigation):** right after `--emulators --emulator-as al`
  sign-in and a group made in the same session, iOS's People list showed no Owner pill beside "Al (You)" and the Groups
  tab read "No groups yet" while Balance showed the new group (opening it from Balance worked). Android, the same steps
  as `an`, showed the Owner pill and the group. A relaunch hit the app lock, so it was not re-checked. Not D-218 code;
  unknown whether it is a look-tooling artefact or a real iOS roles or list refresh gap.
  (e) **Long-standing twin differences the look saw (not D-218):** New group (Android currency chips, iOS a "Settles in USD"
  picker); Add expense (chips and checkboxes against menus and switches); the group page's settled line (Android puts
  "settled" beside "$0.00", iOS right-aligns it). Routed to the Look Book units. Group tile colours differ by a per-group
  derivation, not a defect.

  the group's log (before the joiner's claim syncs, or a claim lost to process death between accepting and claiming); the
  cloud refuses it with the held copy and, since the fix wave, no Try again. There is no server list of held places for
  phones (not built). Invites created before a place became held stay open and acceptInvite refuses them
  (FAILED_PRECONDITION, read as "already used or has expired", D-210's behaviour, unchanged). The held check is a read
  before the invite is written, not one transaction with it: acceptInvite remains the guarantee. A member whose account
  was made with someone's place id makes that place held (participant ids are each phone's choice at account creation
  and not unique), as acceptInvite already refused joining it (D-210).

  translation set where the card is placed, so while a page slides (a push, about 250 ms) a card that does not move
  samples the art at a stale offset until it next moves or redraws. `PushedWindow` (a `Dialog`: the currency list,
  `ChoicePage`, the lock's section) inherits `LocalArtBackdrop` from the activity root and owns the art while open; its
  window is full screen at the activity's origin, so a covered page shows nothing wrong, but the round trip over glass
  cards was not looked at (final review M4). A card scrolled over the art at two offsets was not captured either (T3
  review); the mechanism was read, not pictured.
  (d) **Frame time**: iOS's was never measured. Android's, on the emulator (Aurora light Balance scrolling), stays
  **about +4.5 ms at the 90th percentile over 87b1be8 (decision 31)**: +4.5 at the look; +4 after fix wave 1 (30 ms
  against 26, its two same-pixel changes measuring as nothing); after fix wave 2's 15 fps blur copy 28 against 23.5,
  no gain over the 26.5 before it (7.5 fps 27.5), so 950dfe0 was reverted in 389332b. The cost is the cards drawing
  the shared blurred art during scroll frames (cards not drawing it measure as the base), not the blur pass. Options
  not built: each card's art from a snapshot bitmap sub-rectangle (a bitmap per card), or the card art frozen while a
  scroll is in flight. **Owed at the 0.5.0 release gate**: the number on a real Android phone, which decides whether a
  unit is owed (an emulator's software path is not a phone's GPU; the base's 50th percentile is already 17 ms), with
  the API 26 to 30 fallback, beside D-220's bar blur already on that list.
  `dropShadow` rebuilds a per-card shadow bitmap on every size change (Compose UI 1.12), so a card that animates its
  height would rebuild it per frame; no such card was looked at (T3 review minor 4).

  contrast, plain only at x 16 (`norse-zoom-page-top-glow-stretched-twins-after.png`). The iOS fix lane tried four
  mechanisms (a 1 pt blur with `.dithersResult`, an extended-linear canvas, a float canvas with the gradient in a layer)

- **D-216's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **When the icon changes, and what that costs** (decision 34): only when the Appearance page closes, and only if
  the phone shows another icon. Someone who updates while on Norse or Vardr Labs keeps the Aurora icon until they next
  visit Appearance and leave it (an alert at launch would be the surprise the founder ruled out). iOS shows its system
  alert on every change, with no public way to suppress it (the private route stopped working in iOS 26.1); it arrives
  1.2 to 3.5 s after Back, once the pop has finished, with PrivacyCover behind it. A choice made and then left unapplied
  (iOS: the app killed while still on Appearance) waits for the next visit. On Android the page also closes when the app
  lock closes over it on return (the switch then runs behind the lock screen), when an invite link opens and when a
  tapped push changes the route; on iOS those only cover the page, so the icon changes when the person later pops it.
  Both follow the one rule; neither is a defect.
  (b) **Nothing guards that Appearance pushes no page** (final review M9): a future push from Appearance would run the
  switch on both phones (iOS `onDisappear` fires on a push; an Android child route disposes the page). One assertion per
  shell would close it (no `NavigationLink` or `navigationDestination` in the Appearance cases; no route whose parent is
  `account/appearance`).
  (c) **Android launchers**: only Launcher3 on API 34 was looked at. It keeps a placed home-screen icon through a switch
  (redrawn as the new icon, still opening the app, surviving a launcher restart), which is why the caption has one

  whose icon is the application icon; look M1). The application icon in system Settings stays Aurora's by design.

  every `setAdmin` and `makeOwner`; `acceptInvite` and every `placeIn` caller read the whole log. The log grows with every

  re-listen and a new failed call, an old sleeping timer holding token 1 matches and triggers one early pass (`trigger`

- **D-230's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **Nothing is deployed.** `sharePlaces`, the `places` limit, `acceptInvite`'s `records`, `peekInvite`'s

  (decisions 44 to 51), so G-08's early claim still works against: members from before 0.5.0 until their phone's next
  push after updating (a 0.4.0 phone never marks; every updated phone marks its own places once); placeholders nobody
  holds (there is no account to verify; out of scope by the spec); and a member whose join-time mark failed a check,
  until `PlaceShare` repairs it at the next push. No operator backfill (every phone marks its own); no revoke callable (a
  later mark supersedes, the hook for one); `authorUid` and `createdAt` are not carried into core (not needed once the
  server marks and stamps).
  (c) **The id races (G-31 (3)) are a denial because of decision 66** (the first account to mark an id keeps it; a join
  naming an id another account's mark names on a present member is refused): without decision 66 a copied id that
  reaches a mark would void the owner's own claim, a takeover (the whole-branch review's I1). An id held only in a
  non-member's log (the T2 review's M4, inherited from D-229), one not yet in its owner's cloud log, or a purged
  account's can be copied and marked by a member, and its owner's join is then refused HELD until the copier's member is
  removed. **Except** the confirmation's F2: a second phone that joins before its first pull mints an id the server does
  not yet know as its own, so its join mark is skipped, and a co-member watching the log who copies that id within those
  seconds keeps it: records the owner writes under that id in the window read as the copier's, and the owner's phone may
  place itself at the copier's place (rule 1.5) and merge it into "you"; after its pull the owner is marked under its
  participant id and writes correctly from then on (closures for later: push the personal `you` op before the join's
  call, or let the join wait for the first pull). **After decision 66's remedy** (the copier's member removed) the owner
  joins and is marked only under another of its ids (decision 46 still refuses the copied id: the copier's log holds
  it), and its own phone merges the copier's removed place into "you" (D-154): that place's history and "who paid" lines
  read as the owner's there, locally and for good (its balance was redistributed at the removal). "Present" means not
  removed on the server, so a phone re-adding the copier's member blocks the owner again. **F3**: a phone that switched
  accounts keeps its "you" (G-31 (3)(a)), so the second account's join is refused HELD while the first account's marked
  place is present (fails closed). **F5**: a skip is still remembered by the phone for good for the transient refusal
  left (an id the server does not yet know as the caller's); the clock refusals that made this common are gone.

  the earliest-added holder of one account's id (decision 59 orders by the member's first add, a phone-written
  identity), so the rejoiner's pre-removal history moves onto the new place and the removal's redistribution is counted
  twice on every phone; bounded to one account's own places, no cross-account takeover. M-3: a placeholder another member
  added with the holder's id lends its name to the holder's own merged row, on the holder's phone only, unless the holder
  has a profile (cosmetic). Decision 36's race (the creator marked first, the invitee's mark later) still reads the
  creator's earlier raw records as the place's new holder (D-227's residue, unchanged).
  (e) **The Functions** (the Task 2 review and its re-reviews). M3: a co-member's `addMember` of a victim's id, written
  before the victim's mark, denies that mark for good (a raw-place `you` is refused; a refinement by server `createdAt`
  order is possible); on pre-D-230 data the victim's own phone places itself at the attacker's placeholder (D-229's rule

  query per record (up to 50 a call), the join the held query per record (up to 11); bounded by the quota, for the

  text ("Someone has already joined as this person."), which does not describe "your id is someone else's here"
  (confirmation F4).

  (0.5.1: the removal record carries the removed uid, and only the creator's own removal counts). **The lift of a
  decision 44 denial on an unmarked member** costs that placeholder's place, which may carry real balances (pre-D-230
  data only; a marked place is never denied).

  account's ids already holds, so the latest mark never flips; marks written before it (two marks of one member, the
  later superseding, and records written as `p.you` between them reading as no one until the next `AliasShare` push)
  exist in no production data, only in internal testing. The I-B transient (the whole-branch review's M2): a rejoin's
  records written before its new place's mark lands read as the removed old place for good, and their money sits on a

  two-phone flip on Android) and A10 M1 closed its effect; the join names the account's "you" on both, and each shell's

  reads on main; performance only). Android has 14 `d230_` tests and iOS 12: the same vectors, folded differently. The F1

- **D-231's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **Nothing released; no cloud change.** Less motion reaches people with 0.5.0. The speed it buys on a real
  lower-spec Android phone is not measured (the look measured pixels on emulators, not frame time), and it does not
  touch the Aurora scroll blur's cost (decision 72: decision 31's bake does).
  (b) **The low-RAM default (decision 70) catches phones sold with 3 GB.** Reported memory sits under the nominal RAM,
  so on Android a nominal 3 GB phone starts ON, and on iOS very likely iPhone XR and SE (2nd generation), which run iOS
  17 and 18 (not checked on a device; the spec's "false in practice on iOS" was wrong). Kept on purpose. The low-RAM
  read runs even when a choice is stored (m5; one cheap read, discarded) and again on an Android activity recreation
  (never stored, same result).
  (c) **What the switch does not reach.** System-drawn Android motion (dialogs, sheets, menus, ripples) follows only
  the phone's own setting (M4; decision 68 says "every place the app draws"). iOS `GroupSheets.swift`'s two
  `withAnimation` calls never honoured Reduce Motion either, and Android's twin has no animation (M3, pre-existing;
  for the twin-fix unit). iOS's `MotionReducedKey` defaults to false, so a view rendered outside the root applier (a
  future `UIHostingController`, second scene or window) would lose the phone's own Reduce Motion, the one way this
  design could remove stillness (M1; none exists today, unguarded).
  (d) **The guards are source text** (decision 71). Not caught: an animation that reads nothing at all (as GroupSheets'),
  an `animate*AsState` with no `label =`, whose text runs on and can borrow a later call's gate (C1; only the count of 9
  trips first), `animateItem`, `animateEnterExit` and `SharedTransitionLayout`, not on the unlearned list (C2; none in
  the app), a `var reduce` or a `reduce: Boolean` parameter (only `val` bindings are checked). Brittle but loud: an
  unrelated `val still =` or `val motion =`, a trailing comment on a `val reduce` line (m4 and the confirmation), the parity test's string
  match of the Swift bound (m2), TypeThemeTests' 400-character window after the applier's `body` (m8, which T2 had to
  work around). The iOS guard scans `ios/Skipti/App` only (m9; the other folder holds the two sign-in files). The
  `lowRamAtLaunch` assertion recomputes its own expression and has no row (m1).
  (e) **The iOS one-line test cannot see a truncation.** `testTheMotionSummaryKeepsToOneLine` measures the row's
  height, and `ListRow`'s summary is one line with an ellipsis by default (`summaryLines = 1`), so a truncated summary
  keeps one line's height: it passed while "Holds the art still, fewer animations" truncated in all five sets on the
  phone. The final text is held by the copy pins and the parity test, and its fit is the re-look's to show; a test that measures the
  summary's own width is owed.
  (f) **The copy in the committed docs.** The spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-19-d231-less-motion-design.md`,
  sections 3.4 and 6) and the plan still read "Holds the theme art still"; decision 69 and this record carry the final
  text. The copy sabotage rows (T1 I6 and A6, T4 I5 and A5) anchor on the texts of their own commits; no row was run on
  "Still art, fewer animations".
  (g) **Not checked on iOS:** the row as one accessibility element (no Accessibility Inspector on this Mac); VoiceOver
  and TalkBack on real phones on both.
  (h) **Look tooling:** the `pixel_7` AVD profile makes AVDs with `hw.ramSize` 2G, a low-RAM phone where the switch
  starts ON; future looks on that profile set 4096M. Editing the iOS app's preferences plist with PlistBuddy is served

  (i) **Doc nit:** the "twenty drawings" sentence in `TabIcons.kt` sits on `UserRound`'s KDoc (m10).

- **D-232's residue, stated not implied:**
  (a) **Nothing released; no cloud change.** The dark default, decision 78 and the lock fix reach people with 0.5.0.
  Every look ran on a simulator or an emulator with debug builds; the upgrade from a real TestFlight or Play build to
  0.5.0, the first run on a real phone, and the lock on a real phone are not checked.
  (b) **The launch screen can disagree with the app for the whole cold start** (decision 77; review M1, now in
  ADR-0042). Nothing can read the app's stored choice before the app runs. On iOS it always follows the phone: a light
  phone opening a dark install (every new install on a light phone) shows a white launch screen, measured at about 1.2
  to 1.7 s warm on a Debug simulator, and a dark phone opening an install set to Light a dark one. On Android 12 and
  later the splash follows the app from the launch after the app has told the system (decision 78: a new install's
  second launch, and the launch after any change); a first launch, and every launch below Android 12, follows the
  phone (a white splash of 0.2 to 0.4 s measured). iOS has no way to follow the app here: a twin asymmetry that is
  truly impossible, recorded in ADR-0042.
  (c) **System chrome.** The keyboard is the keyboard app's own on both phones and follows the phone (or its own
  setting), not SKIPTI: light over the dark app on a light phone (the re-look). Android's floating text-selection
  toolbar follows the app on Android 12 and later (decision 78) and the phone below 12. A new install on Android 12+
  on a light phone re-creates its activity once on the first launch (Dark is told); any visible flash from that was
  not measured.
  (d) **A cleared preferences file reads System, not Dark**, when the vault stays (the migration sees a vault and no
  mode); no current path clears one without the other. The vault check is file existence only, so a vault file that
  exists but will not open still counts as "ran before". **An iOS restore of a pre-D-232 backup opens Dark** (review
  M3): preferences come back, the vault never does (`VaultBackup.exclude`, D-162), so the migration sees no vault and
  stores only the mark; the ledger is empty then anyway, so it reads as a new install.
  (e) **Durability of the records.** Android's `commit()` returns a Boolean the code ignores (a failed disk write keeps
  this process's value, and the next launch settles again; review N2, accepted); Android lint, which would flag the
  pattern, is not in the gate. iOS writes the mode, then the mark, through cfprefsd in order; a kill between them loses
  at most the mark and the next launch settles again harmlessly. `nightModeTold` is written with `apply()` after the
  call: a lost or stale record only re-tells the same value, or leaves the window theme following the phone (decision
  77), cosmetic (confirmation m2).
  (f) **The guards are source text.** Both order tests (`testTheDefaultIsSettledFirstAtLaunch`,
  `the_default_is_settled_first_at_launch`), decision 78's pin
  (`the_night_mode_is_told_on_android_12_and_later_and_only_when_it_differs`) and the lock's pin
  (`main_activity_tells_the_lock_of_configuration_changes`) match source text, and the Kotlin parity test slices
  Appearance.swift's functions at a four-space closing brace: a reformat gives a false red, never a false green. The
  iOS stored-property guard (M4) refuses initialisers that name `LedgerStore`, `vault`, `loadGate` or `Sync.`; one that
  reaches the vault under another name would pass. A new iOS mode reader with another property name is caught only by
  the count of three `String?` readers. The Kotlin `parse` and `migrate` are parity-checked by behaviour, not text.
  `defaultVaultPath()` repeats `loadGate`'s path literals (pinned together by
  `testTheMigrationChecksTheLaunchsVaultFile`).
  (g) **Stale sabotage anchors** (review M5, confirmation m4). T3's rows B2 and B4 ran against a37ae9f; 6606864
  rewrote B2's line and 3ec870f put `tellNightMode` between B4's two lines, so neither can run again as written
  (re-anchor B2 to `edit.putBoolean(AppearanceMode.SETTLED_KEY, true)`). What they guard is still guarded: a missing
  mark by `the_launch_settles_the_default_once` (and sabotage row C1 for `commit()`), the launch order by

  (h) **ADR-0023 is not annotated.** ADR-0011 and ADR-0038 carry an "Amended by ADR-0042" line and ADR-0036 an
  amendment; ADR-0023 (line 45) still says "light first" with no note, and ADR-0042 and SPEC 11.1 say how to read it.

- **D-237's residue, stated not implied (the Fable audit's own list; CLOUD-SECURITY section 7 carries the same):**
  (a) **Nothing deployed.** The Functions change (decision 133) deploys with D-235's set in decision 126's order; no
  new index, no rules change; its CLOUD-SECURITY section 2 row is owed on the deploy day.
  (b) **Left for 0.5.1, Low:** a backdated Create changes a group's settlement currency and creation time (core M2;
  the money is not converted, the default currency, the "settles in" labels and the Settled card's order are; append-
  only, so permanent until the group is deleted; needs a modified phone); the `seen` ordering and the held marks'
  "latest" are exact only with the server's `createdAt` carried into the vault (the one fix for all three); the
  shells' "is this me" sets outside money are still global (`selfPlace`, the removal rows' offers, the profile
  share's place: cosmetic, the server decides every role and share; the money paths are per group since this unit);
  Firebase doubts D1 (a deleted group's id can be created again: a tombstone), D2 (a removed member reads the live
  group document: by design), D3 (adoptRemovals' sole-member power equals an ordinary expense) and D5 (a changed
  handle is free at once: product); `onGroupRecord`'s push title stale after a rename; invite pushes carry the
  inviter's free-text profile name (the founder's call: a blocklist pass, or "Someone" for a name containing
  "skipti"); G-22's unsalted email fingerprints (before public, the founder's call).
  (c) **Accepted for internal testing:** the G-04 family (about 200 to 300 colluding accounts past the 60 s callable;
  the remove, re-invite and rejoin loop; no quota on createInvite, acceptInvite attempts, groupRoles and
  shareProfile) and the capacity note (60 calls at once; 512 MiB doubles GB-seconds); before public: App Check and
  per-group daily quotas on invites and joins.
  (d) **A2's bound is probabilistic, not absolute:** a next id is one guess in about a million per stamp; a revision's
  192 KiB blob holds about 3,900 guesses, so a co-member who writes many maximum-size revisions raises the odds a
  little per revision (and pays the log's read cost for every member); the sound end is the server-time ordering.
  Heavy writers (an import of thousands of records in one millisecond) run a few hundred milliseconds ahead of the
  wall clock, inside the 23-hour bound.
  (e) **A3 reads up to 20 profiles holding an id**; an attacker with more sockpuppets than that registered LATER
  than the victim gains nothing (only an earlier registration decides); two profiles created in the same millisecond
  tie and neither denies the other. A caller with no profile yet loses to any holder, as before.
  (f) **The read-only production checks** (every joined member has a used invite; no place with two current
  holders; records written under an id the group does not know; accounts purged before `departed`; profiles
  without a participant id; the bucket and the service account; the live Functions' settings) and the Auth record's
  fields (one user, the founder's eyes) wait for the founder's yes: `.drafts/audit-050/prod-reads.py` reads through
  the REST API with the gcloud login and writes nothing.
  (h) **Round 2, from the Opus review (`.superpowers/sdd/d237/review.md`): recorded, not fixed.** I3: a two-phone
  account's second "you" id is never registered as a participant id, so the first profile that registers a copy of it
  owns it and that phone's marks and aliases with it are refused (fails closed, as before D-237; G-31 (3)'s family;
  the fix is dating a `you` op by its own-log record's server time, 0.5.1). M6: a deleted account that signs up again
  from the same vault keeps its old "you" id, and a copy registered in between owns it (the same family). M4: the
  shells' "is this me" sets outside money still read the global list: `selfID` / `selfId` (the groups read), the
  activity feed's `me` set, `ownClaims`, `rebuildGroups`' `mine` (names, offers and which claim to write; none writes
  money). M3: a next id is one guess in a million per id, and nothing caps revisions per author: about 270
  maximum-size revisions (52 MB of writes, each read by every member) could still cover one targeted edit; the
  server-time ordering ends it. M9: Android's `Placing.of` returns `NONE` when nothing is placed or lost, iOS's a
  `Placing` that maps nothing: the same behaviour.
  (g) **Not re-looked on a device:** D-237 changes no screen; the Placing change is covered by twin unit tests and
  the full gate's suites. VoiceOver under the iOS curtain stays unchecked on a device (D-235's residue).

- **No local profile name.** The no-account path has nothing a user can open
  and later attach an account to. When an account is added its name should
  seed the profile and stay editable.
- **No selective offline→cloud migration.** An offline user who signs in has
  no way to choose what moves (transactions, invoices, profile — all, some,
  or none). Deciding for them is the wrong default given GUARANTEES #5.
- ~~**`LedgerSync.fireAndForget` has no test**~~ **CLOSED by D-115** — the
  synchronous half is guarded and sabotage-proven
  (`a_failing_hook_never_throws_to_the_save_path`). Residual coupling, stated
  rather than left implicit: the coroutine's inner catch is defence-in-depth
  ONLY because `pushLatest` carries a blanket catch and cannot throw. Remove
  that blanket catch and the inner one becomes load-bearing again with nothing
  testing it. They are an invariant pair.
- ~~superseded gap text follows~~
- **`LedgerSync.fireAndForget` had no test, and it is on both save paths**
  (opened by the D-114 audit). Its `try/catch` around `pushLatest` is what
  keeps a background sync failure from reaching the default handler, where an
  uncaught exception in a `launch`ed coroutine crashes the Android process.
  Replacing that catch so the exception propagates leaves all 65 JVM tests
  GREEN — nothing calls the function. The guard is correct and unprotected.
  Fix: a test that invokes `fireAndForget` with a throwing transport and
  asserts it returns without propagating. Same class as D-112's saver blind
  spot — a real runtime failure on the user path that the JVM suite cannot see.
- **The iOS passkey client cannot enrol until its transport carries a bearer**
  (opened by D-102). Enrolment is authenticated now, and
  `PasskeyAuthService.startRegistration`/`finishRegistration` send no
  `Authorization` header, so both would take a 401. This costs nothing today
  — no screen calls either method — but it is the first thing to fix when the
  enrolment UI lands, ahead of the ceremony work, and the Swift file says so
  at the call site. Sign-in (`authenticate/*`) is unaffected and still needs
  no bearer, correctly. **EXPOSED LIVE 2026-08-28 (D-117):** with any relay
  on :8080 the gate's iOS leg FAILS —
  `PasskeyE2ETests.testAllFourRoutesAgainstTheRunningRelay` drives
  register/start without a bearer and takes D-102's 401. Pre-existing since
  D-102 (no prior gate had a relay running, so the red was unreachable);
  D-117's Android live proofs booted one and surfaced it. The test is RIGHT —
  it caught the client defect; the fix is THIS item, landing with the passkey
  unit. Until then, "no relay on :8080" is part of the gate's recorded
  environment for the iOS E2E legs. **CLOSED by D-120** — the enrolment
  legs carry the bearer and send no identifier; the gate runs with a
  relay up, and the E2E passes for the right reason (§3). No transport
  change was needed: RelayHTTPRequest.bearer existed and is how
  SyncService/IdentityService already authenticate.
- **The Android passkey ceremony is wired and cannot COMPLETE anywhere
  yet** (D-118). What is proven: the four routes' transport (bearer on
  both enrolment legs, no identifier anywhere, D-27 uniform), the
  platform-JSON → relay-wire bridge (pinned on fixed bytes), the screen
  hierarchy (passkey primary, OTP fallback, enrol offer armed by an
  OTP-proven session), and ON DEVICE the bearer'd `register/start` leg
  plus the honest degradation. What is owed for completion: a real
  device with a screen lock, a credential provider (Google Play
  services), digital-asset-links hosting for the RP ID
  (`skipti.vardrlabs.com`/.well-known/assetlinks.json — the Android
  analogue of iOS's AASA + entitlement), and the
  `credentials-play-services-auth` provider artifact (deliberately not
  taken until it can be exercised). iOS records exactly this class of
  limit for its own ceremony; neither shell pretends.
- **ADR-0034's follow-up units, named by D-121** (record-level sync
  shipped; default-on is the NEXT unit and must not be folded in):
  (1) **Per-device keys** (D-42's deferral, now on the critical path):
  the sync secret is per-subject material held per vault, so cross-device
  OPENING needs the key hierarchy over the FFI — until then, record sync
  runs against the existing material (the engines are proven with a
  shared fixture secret, which is exactly the sharing that unit will
  deliver). (2) **Sync default-on for accounts** — the ADR's second half,
  safe to build only now that the loss path is structurally gone;
  GUARANTEES #5 is untouched (no account created, implied, or nudged).
  (3) **Group records** — groups sync per-device as kv fixtures today;
  the three-device proof compares ledger-level per-currency totals, not
  group-scoped balance containers. (4) **Record edits/LWW** — records are
  immutable; the version field and the "losing version RETAINED" rule
  (silent resolution, nothing destroyed) await the edit flow. (5) The
  one-time projection transition: pre-ADR-0034 vaults' canonical
  settlement blobs do not project (they still merge); dev vaults are
  disposable, no production vault exists.
- **The §9 surfaces are engine-complete but not chrome-complete — on
  BOTH shells** (D-119). Proven on Android (mirroring iOS's existing
  state): the formats byte-proven, the review model atomic, the full
  loop driven by hand on device, SAF/file-picker destinations, §9.4's
  gates structural. Residue, honestly: (1) the tab-bar/shell entry
  point exists on NEITHER shell (iOS's ExportScreen is `--export`-
  mounted; Android's `--export`/`--import` join the headless args) — a
  navigation decision, not this unit's; (2) §9.4's optional
  passphrase-protected ZIP (AES-256) remains the recorded dependency
  decision on both shells; (3) the import member-binding UI is raw
  `Name=participant-id` text on Android — the polished mapper is
  product residue; (4) generic bank CSV and Tricount/Settle Up/Splid
  stay §9.5's open list, pinned only when formats get evidence.
- **Relay rate limiting: DECIDED (ADR-0032/D-105), layer 1 now RUN on the box
  (2026-08-27) — and its first run caught a defect, incident §5.21.**
  `apply` + `verify` executed on the production instance: DROP at position 1,
  above the `dpt:443` ACCEPT at 7; `0 LOG targets in INPUT`. The counter line
  was unfalsifiable and is fixed. **Still open on this item:**
  `netfilter-persistent save` and a reboot-survival re-`verify` — an
  unpersisted rule vanishes silently and the first anyone knows is the next
  flood. `remove` has still never executed anywhere.
  Superseded description of the original gap follows for the record:
- ~~**Layer 1 WRITTEN-NOT-RUN.**~~
  The fork this register opened is closed. Layer 2 — the relay's global
  admission bucket — ships in the binary, is covered by three tests and four
  sabotage runs, and needs no operator action. Layer 1 —
  `deploy/skipti-connection-limit.sh` — is the honest gap: it is
  version-controlled, syntax-checked, and both its guard paths (usage, root)
  are exercised, but **its iptables paths have never executed anywhere**.
  There is no iptables on the development Mac, so `apply`/`remove`/`verify`
  are unproven exactly as D-84's backup scripts were before their first real
  run — and that run is what caught three defects there. Assume the same here
  until it runs on the box. What must be verified on first run, in order:
  the rule lands ABOVE the `dpt:443` ACCEPT (below it, iptables' first-match
  rule means it is never reached and looks installed while doing nothing);
  `verify` reports `ok: 0 LOG targets in INPUT`; and it survives
  `netfilter-persistent save` plus a reboot, because an unpersisted rule
  vanishes silently and the first anyone knows is the next flood.
- **Passkey happy path is proven (was the top gap here).** A real software
  authenticator (`webauthn-authenticator-rs`, D-32) now drives registration and
  assertion through all four `/v1/auth/passkey/*` routes; a genuine assertion
  verifies, mints a session, and that session is attributed to the right
  subject (D-31 binding asserted directly) with a working refresh token.
  Residual honesty note: the soft passkey claims the user-verified bit rather
